productions.expectedTotalNoteEn: 4,744 episodes aired from Episode 0001 (10 November 1969) through season 56 (2025–26, last aired 8 June 2026), the sum of the Muppet Wiki season guides; Wikipedia gives the same total. Season 57 is announced for 23 November 2026 on Netflix and PBS KIDS and has not aired. The 1969 test pilots, specials and spin-off series are not counted. Season 45 is numbered 4501–4526 and 4552; 4527–4551 are repeat labels, not episodes.
productions.expectedTotalNoteHe: 4,744 פרקים שודרו, מפרק 0001 (10 בנובמבר 1969) ועד עונה 56 (2025–26, שודרה לאחרונה ב־8 ביוני 2026): סכום מדריכי העונות של Muppet Wiki; גם ויקיפדיה מונה כך. עונה 57 הוכרזה ל־23 בנובמבר 2026 ב־Netflix וב־PBS KIDS ועוד לא שודרה. פרקי הניסיון מ־1969, תכניות מיוחדות וסדרות נלוות אינם נספרים. עונה 45 ממוספרת 4501–4526 ו־4552; 4527–4551 הן תוויות של שידורים חוזרים, לא פרקים.

episodes.summaryEn: In the first episode of Sesame Street, Gordon takes a girl named Sally on a tour of Sesame Street, introducing her (and the viewers) to the various characters on the show. On the street, Sally meets the human cast -- Gordon, Susan, Bob, and Mr. Hooper -- as well as two Muppet characters, Big Bird and Oscar the Grouch.

altLabels.labelEn: Gordon introduces Sally to Sesame Street
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

altLabels.labelEn: Gordon Introduces Sally to Sesame Street
altLabels.sourceLabel: Sesame Workshop, Five Things You May Not Know About Sesame Street, retrospective title label

episodes.noteEn: Sesame Workshop’s anniversary article calls this episode Gordon Introduces Sally to Sesame Street. Stored as a sourced retrospective label; original broadcast title is not established.

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon wants to show Ronald an example of something that's round. He asks Oscar if he can use the lid from his trash can, but Oscar grumpily declines, so Gordon uses a nearby lid instead.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar decides to leave Sesame Street
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon welcomes the viewer to another swingin' sunny day on Sesame Street. That's a lot of S words.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird makes a sweater for Susan
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon, Bob, Susan and some kids look through the doors (which normally lead to Big Bird's nest area), and watch in amazement as a steam shovel digs a hole.

altLabels.labelEn: Gordon, Susan and Bob run Hooper's Store for the day
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon picks up his newspaper from Hooper's Store and welcomes the viewer to Sesame Street, right as it starts to rain. As he goes inside, he sees Oscar getting wet on purpose, which Gordon thinks is weird, but Oscar doesn't.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar gets wet in a rainstorm
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon invites the viewer to the block party that's going to be held tonight on Sesame Street.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon, Bob, Susan, and Mr. Hooper sneak up on Oscar and surprise him for his fifth birthday. Oscar has no idea what they mean when they ask him if the number 5 means anything to him.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar's birthday / Mr. Hooper counts jelly beans
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon and Sally are on a B treasure hunt: they've found a ball and a blue box. Mr. Hooper is stumped.

altLabels.labelEn: B treasure hunt; Ernie erases Cookie Monster
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon encounters Bob and Susan looking for a stray cat they found. Gordon assures them that he's really good at catching cats.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Susan welcomes the viewer to Sesame Street while cooking in her kitchen. Meanwhile, Jennie draws some silly pictures to have the kids find out what's wrong with them.
Gordon welcomes the viewer and plans on returning a carton of eggs to Hooper's Store. Why?
Bob sings "Feelin' Groovy" as he walks down the street, stopping to buy a newspaper at Hooper's Store.
episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki flags this episode as missing from the Sesame Archives; its guide is reconstructed from archival scripts, not confirmation that a complete recording survives.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird wants to earn some extra money today, so he asks Gordon, Bob and Susan if they have any odd jobs he can do. Gordon points him to a sign at Hooper's Store which reads "Boy Wanted" and recommends him to Mr. Hooper.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: After stumbling through the door yet again, Big Bird finds some mysterious yellow footprints on the ground, and thinks they came from a monster. Doubtful about this theory, Gordon and Susan confirm that their feet don't fit in the footprints, and point out that Big Bird's feet do fit, since he stepped in some paint earlier.
Gordon and Bob greet each other, then hear some happy music coming from somewhere. They ask Oscar if it's coming from his trash can, which it isn't.
Susan welcomes you back to Sesame Street. You're just in time to watch Gordon play a trick on Ernie.

Gordon, Susan, Mr. Hooper, and Bob are going about their business on Sesame Street when they hear a series of loud hiccups coming from Oscar's trash can. They approach, and Oscar the Grouch admits to his ailment, saying that he likes hiccups.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon teaches Big Bird how to play hide-and-seek, but tells him he can't hide behind trees or the kids because he's too wide and tall. Gordon suggests Big Bird be "it" since he can't grasp the concept of hiding, so he begins counting while everyone else hides.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird's hide-and-seek; Mr. Hooper's rocket launchers
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: After bumping into the Sesame Street lamppost, Big Bird encounters Bob, who presents a film about Big Bird's "relatives" …
Gordon observes how peaceful Sesame Street is today, but a barrage of flying trash ruins it. He encounters Oscar doing something uncommon: cleaning house!

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird walks by Gordon and Ford blowing up balloons on the street. He has a balloon too, but he thinks it's a rare fruit until Gordon tells him what it is.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird discovers balloons; Susan in the kitchen
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon invites the viewer to Jay's tenth birthday party. He asks how many that is, and counts to 10 on his fingers.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon shows Susan and Myron some picture sequences of he and Susan having lunch, and has Myron guess which order the pictures go in.
Susan says hello to everyone, including the viewer. She encounters Big Bird, who feels a little woozy today, and suggests he gets some exercise.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon welcomes the viewer, letting us know that Bob is about to read a story with a lot of D words.
Gordon gives some of Mr. Hooper's ice cream cones to Susan, Bob, and Jennie. He has one left, which he'll give to Oscar, because everyone likes ice cream.
Gordon greets the viewer, and hears the sound of a typewriter coming from Ernie's apartment …

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon notices a string tied to a basket hanging in front of his window. Mr. Hooper explains that he has installed the "Hooper Super Automatic Remote-Control Elevator," a push-button dumbwaiter to carry grocery items to Gordon's apartment.
On the stoop of 123 Sesame Street, Susan, Gordon and a girl look closely at a short-bill toucan Bob has with him.

A postal carrier named George (played by Brandon Maggart) makes his way down Sesame Street delivering mail to its residents. Oscar the Grouch pops up from his can and asks if he's got any as the postal carrier leaves mail in Big Bird's nest.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Susan greets the viewer, and says that Gordon is getting ready to play a trick on Ernie.
Bob sits on the steps of 123 Sesame Street sorting shapes with Gayle and Josh. Bob asks if you can imagine what would happen if all the shapes were put together.
Gordon is excited because Michael Cooney is coming to Sesame Street today. He tells Bob, some kids, then wonders if Ernie and Bert know.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: It's a windy day today on Sesame Street. Gordon spots some moving leaves, Mr. Hooper places weights on his newspapers so they don't blow away, Bob claims to have been blown away three blocks down, and Susan tries to keep her hat on her head.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon tosses the football around with Jay as he welcomes the viewer.

A gruff-voiced man (Brandon Maggart) wearing an apron asks Mr. Hooper, "Can you tell me how to get to Sesame Street?" The man, Mr. Glopper, scopes out the street everyone's been talking about, and decides to place his hot dog cart by the stoop.

altLabels.labelEn: Mr. Glopper sets up his hot dog cart on the street
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon plays a "what happens next" game with Reggie and Sarah, in which he points them to some clips of Buddy and Jim; the videos pause so that the kids can guess what will happen next. The first is of Buddy and a roller skate on the floor, and Jim performing a ball trick as a magician; the results are surprising.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Susan greets the viewer and mentions that Gordon will be a little late coming home from work. Right now he's helping Ernie with a problem.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon greets the viewer, and spots Josh and Chris pitching baseball cards. He introduces the Anything Muppets in a gripping, intense story...
Gordon and Troy want to think of words that begin with K and words that end with K, so they go to Oscar. Oscar shows them a rock and a stick, then a key, none of which he wants to give away to Troy.
Gordon is about to pick up his newspaper from Hooper's Store, when he looks up and sees Alphabet Bates skywrite the letter N . He asks Big Bird and Carlos if they know any N words.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon overhears Oscar singing in the shower from within his can. Bob, Susan and Mr. Hooper also stop by Oscar's can out of curiosity.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Susan is on the stoop of 123 Sesame Street and welcomes the viewers while she is knitting. Then, after discussing about various emotions with Brynne, she introduces the upcoming segment.

altLabels.labelEn: The cast introduces L, Q and Y; Kermit explains big and small
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: During the opening theme, a dog named Rufus looks for Sesame Street.

altLabels.labelEn: Rufus visits / Cookie Monster moves in with Oscar
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon greets the viewer, teasing about a few people and things they'll be seeing today. He mentions how much he likes it when their visits begin; beginnings are groovy!
Gordon calls the others to come and see what he's found. On the construction door fence is a large circus poster.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon and Duncan notice some boxes on the ground. They look up and see Alphabet Bates skywrite the letter Q, and think of Q words.

Bob, Gordon, and the kids sit on the stoop of 123 Sesame Street clapping and singing along with Pete Seeger as he plays his banjo and sings "Skip to My Lou." Gordon greets the viewer and introduces Pete, who explains how families used to make music before television, movies, and other modern conveniences.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon and Susan greet the viewer while waiting for some kids to show up to play a board game. Susan points out one of the shapes on the board: a rectangle.

Susan welcomes the viewer, and is about to read a story, when Big Bird interrupts and says he'd like to tell a story for once. Susan lets him go ahead, and he tells the story of "Little Red Riding Hood", but mixes it up with several other fairy tales (including "Jack and the Beanstalk," "Goldilocks and the Three Bears," and "Rumpelstiltskin").
Gordon encounters Jennie drawing a picture of Sesame Street. One by one, Susan, Bob, and Mr. Hooper join and all give their commentary on it as she progresses.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob and Gordon sit on the steps with Rico and Leslie. Bob attempts to make a different shape out of some cutout triangles and squares, which turns out to be a square within a big square.

Gordon, sitting with Carlos and Sheryl on the stoop, invites the viewer to play a guessing game where they look at something closely and try to figure out what it is. The first one is something to eat...

Susan welcomes the viewer and tells them that Oscar the Grouch told her to go to the store to buy five pounds of sugar for him. Oscar, wearing a baker's hat and apron, explains that he's preparing for his friend Herbie's birthday.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar bakes a cake; Mr. Hooper invents a 10 machine
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: On the steps, Gordon plays a guessing game with Roma and Patty, where they both cover their eyes and guess what sounds they hear. They hear the sounds of traffic, a plane, an ice cream truck, and clumsy Big Bird crashing into something.
Oscar the Grouch pops out of his can, and isn't too pleased to see the viewer. Mr. Hooper passes by, and Oscar asks him if he makes ice cream sundaes.

altLabels.labelEn: Mr. Hooper bakes Oscar a baked bean sundae
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon greets the viewer, saying there is a lot to do and see today.

Gordon shows Mauricio and Robin some picture sequences and has them decide which order the pictures go in. The first sequence is of a boy fishing, the second is of a house in different stages, and the third is of a girl eating.

A balloon man (James Catusi) attracts the attention of Gordon, Susan, Bob, and Mr. Hooper. He's only got ten balloons left, but every time Susan tries to buy one, he accidentally pops it with his lit cigar.

altLabels.labelEn: Balloon activities / Big Bird's rubber love
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon has Troy and Mauricio introduce the capital and lowercase letter I with art cards, leading to Bob's story.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob gets ready to play a game with Big Bird, Gillian, and Rico. He invited Ernie, but he figures Ernie's probably busy eating cookies.
While Gordon and Bob get ready for today's activities, Susan welcomes the viewer and displays the capital and lowercase E.

Gordon welcomes the viewer as he dumps some trash into Oscar's trash can, then realizes that Oscar might be annoyed by this. Instead, Oscar greets Gordon and forgives him; he's unusually okay with it, knowing it was an accident.
Gordon and Mr. Hooper encounter a pile of junk in the middle of the sidewalk, and each believe the other is responsible for it. They start to get into an argument, and Bob attempts to mediate.
Bob greets the viewer as he plays catch with Lance and Kevin; he says it's nice to have friends to play with.

Mr. Hooper and Jay discuss painting when Big Bird alerts Mr. Hooper that he has a big package waiting for him at the store. Mr. Hooper takes out the contents, piece by piece, and has Big Bird guess what it is: an adjustable stool to replace an old one from his store.

Gordon greets the viewer, and talks with Marlon and Big Bird about "over," "under," "around," and "through." Big Bird is a little rusty, so Gordon shows him over and under with a jumprope, then he and Marlon have Big Bird walk around them, and through the construction doors, crashing in the process.
Gordon greets the viewer while getting the mail. He has Big Bird guess who was just here.

Gordon greets the viewer with Murray and Carlos, saying that so many people have said they were going to be in the neighborhood today. And here comes visitor number one, and visitor number two - Ernie and Bert.
Gordon meets up with Susan when he gets home from work. They suddenly hear a raucous trumpet coming from Oscar's trash can, and then a whiny saxophone.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar and the Groovin' Grouches / Susan's plant
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird wants to help Mr. Hooper in his store. Mr. Hooper is planning to paint a sign advertising orange juice, and Big Bird says he can do the job… but he's a little forgetful about the alphabet.

Oscar needs to mail a letter to his mother, then another one to his friend Hubert Rotten, the president of the Disagreeable Order of Grouches. Gordon helps him out with the first letter, which is picked up by Claude, a beatnik mailman, who explains to Oscar how a letter gets to its destination.

altLabels.labelEn: Ethel Kennedy visits / Big Bird builds a television set
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon welcomes the viewer as he arm wrestles with Ronald and Mauricio. He points out that he sits behind a desk all day and doesn't get enough exercise; if he did, he'd be more like this guy...

Gordon sees Big Bird reading a book of magic spells. They don't believe the spells would really work, but they try one just for fun; it ends up conjuring a giant letter R in the middle of the sidewalk!

Gordon and Jay walk over to Oscar's trash can and see a giant letter O on it. Gordon assumes that it stands for "Oscar" or for "open" or "only," but Oscar says it's none of those, and tells them to unroll the nearby roll of paper the O is attached to.
Gordon and Carlos visit Oscar's trash can and Gordon knocks on the can lid. Oscar responds, but is fed up with everyone banging on his trash can lid, saying it's giving him a headache.
Gordon overhears Oscar cheering for the Grouch Bowl on TV. The opposing teams playing today are the Midtown Meanies vs.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar watches the Grouch Bowl/Mr. Hooper's missing glasses
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon, Josh and Reggie talk about things that everybody does. Gordon mentions that everyone takes baths, including Ernie.
In the kitchen, Susan helps grade papers with Gordon as they welcome the viewer. They suddenly hear Oscar shouting for help outside.

Gordon comes home and calls out for Susan, but sees she's not there. He looks around and sees some evidence on the kitchen counter that she was here: her keys, a half-eaten lunch, and a newspaper with a notification to register to vote.
Big Bird has to carry a lot of balloons over to Hooper's Store. He thinks that instead of bringing them one by one, he can put all the balloons into a nearby box.
Gordon greets the viewer and says that a busy day is coming up. Michael Cooney is going to stop by again, and all sorts of things are going on.
Big Bird (performed here by Daniel Seagren) welcomes the viewers and explains that he has trouble carrying all of his bags of birdseed to his nest. Mr. Hooper helps him put the birdseed in a box.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird moves birdseed to his nest
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Susan encounters Rufus the dog (who only lives a couple blocks away from Sesame Street), who has set up a lemonade stand. He plans on charging ten cents per glass, so Susan helps him make a sign, since he doesn't know what a 10 looks like.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon sits with Mason and Mauricio on the stoop to greet the viewer. Instead of just listing all the fun things they'll see today, Gordon turns it into a rhyming guessing game and the kids try to figure out the answers.
Bob, Rhonda, and Robin observe a Margay cat named Montezuma. Bob remarks that there are many pets to choose from, but he wouldn't want to pick one from a game show.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon watches as Kwami and Paul build a couple of block towers in front of 123 Sesame Street. Gordon asks, "How would you like to take a trip to the beach?

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Mr. Hooper gets a call from a distressed Oscar who asks him to come over to his can. He wants to take his grouch friends to the movies because one of the worst films of all time is playing: "The Cowboy and the Meanie" starring Roy Rotten and his horse Crummy.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon is about to introduce the letter T, which he can't find at first. Lance and Guy point out to him it's sticking out of his back pocket.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar keeps missing the day's activities
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon, Bob, and Mr. Hooper observe the tree in the middle of Sesame Street and notice that it's looking sick. Gordon decides to throw a block party to raise money for taking care of the tree.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon and Ronald spell out words on a magnetic board when Big Bird arrives. He's got a new poem, but only has the first line written.
Gordon passes by Oscar's trash can, where he sees signs reading "Construction, Crane Crossing," "Caution Careful!" and "Coming Closer Causes Catastrophes!"

Gordon is touching up the mural in the yard and says he's not going to tell anyone anything about today's episode. He's approached by a pair of identical sisters whose names he has to guess, and after guessing that they're triplets or quadruplets, finally figures out that they're twins.
Gordon displays a letter F which he cut from a piece of paper.
Gordon recites the alphabet and asks Chet to identify the letter he left out: F.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon sits in the yard reading a copy of The Daily Tribune featuring a headline that reads NURSE SHORTAGE CRITICAL. He explains that he's been reading an article about how 350,000 years ago (which is a little bit older than he) the ocean floor was covered with millions of shelled worms.

altLabels.labelEn: Susan re-enters the workforce by renewing her nurse's license
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon sits on the stoop of 123 Sesame Street with Chris and welcomes the viewer. He teases an upcoming story by the Anything People before heading to the playground, where Buddy and Jim are right now.

Gordon reads a story in The Sesame Street Sun about Ernie's new job. Several children come tearing down the street, one on a bicycle, a couple following on foot, and another on an orange crate scooter.

Gordon sits on the steps talking to two kids about clean and dirty. Gilian has lost a tooth, so he needs to keep his new ones clean, and Cedric is wearing dog tags that he's kept shiny, so they know about keeping things clean.
Gordon observes how busy everybody on Sesame Street seems to be today. He encounters Susan with a watering can in the windowsill and has us guess that she's watering her fern.

Susan says hello to some kids and welcomes the viewer. She displays the china platter she's polishing, which her grandmother had passed to her mother, who passed it down to her when she married Gordon.
Bob welcomes the viewer, observing that a lot of friends are with us today. Robin, Carey, and Claudia are jumping rope, and Jennie is working on a new drawing.

Gordon wanders around Sesame Street and watches everybody playing games. Troy and Kate are jumping rope, while Bob, Jay, and Lance are pitching baseball cards and Susan, Brynne, and Reggie play hopscotch.
Gordon makes things out of a couple of lines on a felt board and has Gayle, Marta, and Guy guess what they are -- an arrow, a seesaw, a triangle, and finally the letters Y and K.

Gordon has three pairs of shoes: one for babies, one for kids, and one for adults. He starts up a game with a kid as a shoe salesman, and pretends to be the customer trying on a big, bigger and biggest shoe.

altLabels.labelEn: Reading Sylvester and the Magic Pebble
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki flags this episode as missing from the Sesame Archives; its guide is reconstructed from archival scripts, not confirmation that a complete recording survives. Sponsor field is blank in the source; no sponsors inferred.

episodes.summaryEn: While Susan works late, Gordon is stuck making sandwiches with Sally and Mauricio. Sally's favorite food is spaghetti, while Mauricio's is hamburgers.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Mr. Hooper greets the viewer, and whispers that he rearranged some things around Sesame Street so we can point out what's wrong with them. The kids observe such things as some dishes on the newsstand, upside-down chairs, a Christmas stocking, and a fire hydrant wearing a hat, mittens, and facial hair.
Word makes its way around the street from the grown-ups and the kids (including Brynne, Jill, and Jay) that Pete Seeger is visiting today. Gordon relays the message to one last person...

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon and Vanessa are having a "heavy discussion" about actors when Oscar invites them to play a grouchy rhyming game involving things in and around his trash can. Oscar claims the game is very difficult, but Gordon and Vanessa guess the answers easily until the very last one; "elephant" neither rhymes with Oscar's clue, nor does he actually own one.
Gordon and Susan welcome the viewer, then meet Pete (George Zima), the new street cleaner, who tap-dances and rhymes while he sweeps.

Bob, Susan, and Mr. Hooper notice some boxes in front of Oscar's trash can. They figure the boxes belong to Big Bird, since they've seen him use boxes to make a truck, a television set, and a cuckoo clock.
Susan comes home from work and greets the viewer. She sees Oscar the Grouch wearing a chef's hat, and Oscar announces that he's making alphabet soup ("I'm known as the Julia Child of Grouches!").

Gordon and Susan are trying to help Big Bird learn the alphabet; he keeps getting stuck on one letter that looks like a circle. Bob enters and learns of the situation, then contacts Alphabet Bates (voice of Will Lee) via the walkie-talkie he happens to have in his pocket.
Gordon comes home from work, and has to get his supplies upstairs in a hurry. He tells Bob to tell Oscar the Grouch that Don McLean is coming with his banjo and guitar.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Susan passes some kids playing checkers, then greets the viewer. She and Gordon observe how beautiful a day it is to go driving, but Susan points out that they don't have a car.

altLabels.labelEn: Gordon, Susan, and the kids go on an imaginary car ride
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob encounters Big Bird, who has a close call while crossing the street. He was so excited to share some poems he wrote about how special birds are, that he ran over to tell everybody and forgot to look both ways.

At the steps of 123 Sesame Street, Gordon, Bob, and the kids welcome Odetta Holmes, who sings "If I Had a Hammer." Gordon introduces her to each of the kids by name, then asks what would you do if you had a U...

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon observes a mess of trash that has been thrown all over Sesame Street. He recruits Susan, Bob, and the kids to start gathering it and tasks Ronald with finding the largest cardboard box he can find.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Susan welcomes the viewer, and asks if we can guess who the mother in the family is.
Susan finishes hanging out her laundry to dry. Oscar tells Susan that today is laundry day for him too, only he does his laundry by making clean things dirty.

Bob compliments Cedric on his bicycle and tells Troy that they're going to have a treasure hunt today. He gives Cedric a push on his bike as if blasting off a rocket so that he can go buy some jellybeans at Hooper's Store.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon greets the viewer, while in the background are sounds of busy street noises. He says that you probably guessed there's a lot of traffic on Sesame Street.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird builds a racing car
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

The kids are outside playing Kick the Can when "Oscar the Magnificent," having taken up magic, invites everyone to see his card trick. Susan takes a card, and Oscar correctly guesses that it's the number 7.

Big Bird singsongingly boasts that he can draw letters better than anybody else on the block and instantly recognizes any letter he sees. His claim is put to the test when he, Gordon, and the kids look up and see Alphabet Bates skywriting a letter .

Oscar talks during the opening theme sequence, trying to direct the filmed children elsewhere; nobody seems to be paying attention to Oscar today. He announces that he's taking over the show while Gordon and Susan are at work.

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar's been doing some "deep thinking" about people, and how they communicate their feelings with the noises they make. He has Susan and Gordon play a guessing game and try to determine how he feels.

Big Bird teaches the kids that "Everyone Makes Mistakes" in the Season 2 premiere. Herry Monster and Sherlock Hemlock are introduced in this episode, and Farley can be glimpsed when Cookie Monster eats Big Bird's J.

Oscar the Grouch is happy to see the viewers for a change, because he is having a grand opening sale at the Oscar's Odds and Ends Store. He is selling dandy things like half a record, back issues of The Daily Grouch from 1935, and a knob from a color TV set (some assembly required).

Oscar writes a poem in honor of Charlie Rotten for tonight's testimonial dinner at the Disagreeable Order of Grouches (D.O.G.) lodge meeting. Gordon, Mr. Hooper and Susan suggest some complimentary rhymes about his friend, but Oscar would rather write grouchy rhymes.

In her kitchen, Susan has just finished getting the laundry from the clothesline and Big Bird is "helping" her fold and put them away. She notices that she has five orphaned socks, and wonders where the others could've gone to.
Bob, Mason, Brian, Robin, and Tracy play different rhythms (including "Shave and a Haircut") on the barrel tunnels near Big Bird's nest.
Miguel won't waste a second; he reveals a letter A.

On a rainy day, Bob makes his way down Sesame Street carrying a newspaper over his head to keep dry. Mr. Hooper is busy covering his newspaper stand, and Gordon tells Bob that it's not a fit day out for man nor beast.
Bob explains why we need the letter J: without it, there'd be no jumping (like he and the kids do), jellybeans (like Mr. Hooper has), jobs (like Susan has), or junk (which Oscar wallows in).
Bob welcomes the viewer and wants to talk about the concept of away from. Oscar interrupts, as he's trying to read his book.

Big Bird and Little Bird are practicing a choreographed "wubba-wubba whoop-whoop" chant. As they're doing so, Gordon and Susan come out of 123 Sesame Street to buy some pancake turners and overhear their chant.

Susan and Gordon greet the viewer when they hear Oscar laughing. Oscar tells them that he just saw the funniest thing, but he's too much in hysterics to go into details.
Gordon welcomes the viewer, and asks if everybody's ready.
Gordon welcomes the viewer, and attaches a wing to a model airplane. What's going to happen next?

After greeting the viewer, Mr. Hooper, Reggie, and Robin notice a sign on Oscar's trash can: "Don't bother me unless you know the secret knock." Oscar explains that too many people knock on his can, so the special knock lets him know if anyone has something important to tell him.

Big Bird invites Susan and Bob over to his nest for some birdseed tea, where they find some unusual clues. First, a bag of spilled birdseed is laying out, which Big Bird is sure he put in his nest before he took a walk.

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon, Susan, and Bob sit on the stoop talking about how lazy a day it feels today. Bob brings up the idea of pretending something special is going on.
Mr. Hooper sifts through some letters in order to find the correct one for today. Betty Lou asks him about something sticking out of the newsstand: the letter I.

Big Bird visits Susan so he'll have something to do today. Susan suggests that they can listen to the sounds around Sesame Street, which include vehicles, a dog, and an ice cream truck, but soon includes horses, a wolf, a lion and a train!

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon hears some strange mechanical noises coming from Big Bird's nest. He investigates and finds Big Bird adjusting the franistrat and adjusting the crasinopholus on his structure.

Molly Scott arrives on Sesame Street, playing guitar and singing "How D'ye Do." Beginning at Mr. Macintosh's stand, she sings her way down the street greeting Mr. Hooper at Hooper's Store, through the yard where the kids are playing and Bob watches from his apartment window, and past the steps of 123 Sesame Street where Gordon and Susan greet her.

Bob finds the perfect place to paint the first letter of the day, proceeding to paint the letter P right on the television screen.

Gordon welcomes the viewer as he and the kids admire Rafael's (Reuben Figueroa) pet collie in the yard. Gordon asks him how much he walks his dog and what he has to do to take care of him, and Mr. Hooper brings the dog some water.

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon introduces the letter M, which starts such words as "man, "motorcycle," and "mailbox."

The cast sings "The Word Family Song" with the AN family. Susan and Mr. Hooper spell MAN, Little Bird spells CAN, Bob spells FAN, and Gordon spells PAN.
Susan finishes ordering her groceries over the phone, and tells the viewer about today's sponsors. She recalls the number is 2, but can't remember today's letter.

Gordon walks down the steps of the carriage house carrying something behind his back. He makes his way over to the front of Big Bird's nest where he greets Little Bird and produces the object, displayed backwards.

Big Bird calls out for Susan from the window of 123 Sesame Street, balanced atop the gate wall (pretending to be a tightrope walker). He explains that he's created "toy poems," which don't even need to be written down.

Mr. Snuffleupagus greets Jay on the street and explains that he was writing the alphabet, but he made a mistake, so he's going to throw his paper away. When he tosses it on the ground, Jay tells him he can't just dispose of it anywhere, it has to go in a trash can.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: David, Bob, Maria and Susan try to count and stack boxes with the help of Jay and the other kids, but Big Bird knocks them over while looking for Alphabet Bates. They point out that since Big Bird is looking down, he's unlikely to see him as Alphabet Bates is usually flying up through the sky in his plane.

David welcomes the viewer, explaining that today they will be explaining first and last. To start off, David recruits Bob, Luis, Maria, and some kids to form a line, then has the last person in line come to the front and become first.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar babysits; Big Bird's taxi service
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki notes an additional scripted street scene was unaired. This does not mean the numbered episode itself was unaired.

episodes.summaryEn: Maria recruits Oscar the Grouch to help teach the concept of here and there. Oscar obliges, militantly barking orders to the viewer.

altLabels.labelEn: Snuffleupagus drinks soapy water from a bucket
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Susan brings over an old rusty pipe to give to Oscar. When Enrique throws his ball at his trash can, Oscar complains how he is constantly bothered by people, especially when they're tapping on his trash can.

Gordon appears on Sesame Street with only his head, hands, and lower legs visible (as he's wearing blue against a chroma key background). The rest of his body is missing, and he takes his cue from the audience as to which parts are gone as they return (removing the blue pieces of fabric).

altLabels.labelEn: Maria and Big Bird play a rhyming game
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob greets the viewer, and thinks he hears the sound of the milkshake machine inside Hooper's Store. The sound makes him thirsty, so he calls out to David for a glassful of whatever he's got.

David finishes painting a chair for Mr. Hooper, and is about to make a "wet paint" sign, when Sam the Robot offers to do it for him. The first sign he generates is way too small, fitting in the palm of David's hand.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar warns everyone that it's going to rain
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird hears the sound of Joey playing his drum in the Fix-it Shop. Big Bird loves drums, even to the point of standing around waiting for a parade just to hear them.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird makes his own drum
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Since everybody else is busy, Big Bird asks the viewer to help him identify several letters of the alphabet that he has trouble learning.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Luis is about to clean three mud spots off the front window of the Fix-It Shop. He asks the viewer if he cleans one off, how many will be left.
Bob displays a picture for the kids in the yard. Teaching the IG family of words, the picture is of a big pig wearing a wig, and Bob adds those words to the picture.

altLabels.labelEn: Sam tells a joke/Big Bird wants to be a dog
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird encounters Mr. MacIntosh's produce cart, which is unattended. He wonders if he could try and ride it; since Mr. Mac is so nice, he probably wouldn't mind.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar mistakes his reflection in the mirror for another Grouch
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: David greets the viewer, and gives a lesson in subtraction using his feet. He first stands on two feet, then one foot, then no feet (by hopping onto the tire swing).

altLabels.labelEn: David gives Oscar a lesson in manners
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon and the kids list threes of different things they don't usually count on Sesame Street. He asks one girl about three of her favorite foods, and another kid about their three favorite games.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird offers to be Luis' songbird
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria greets the viewer, and hears Oscar throwing trash out of his trash can. The sounds of his tin cans clanking to the ground puts him in a musical mood, so he sings "I Love Trash" to the kids.

altLabels.labelEn: Somebody keeps squirting Bob and Luis with water
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar decides not to tell the viewer to go away as he's admiring the big mess of litter all over Sesame Street. He surmises that the wind knocked some cans over and caused it, but Luis and Susan don't like what they see.

altLabels.labelEn: Luis, Susan and the kids work together to clean the street
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria greets the viewer and decides to read a book outside since it's so quiet. The silence is broken when Oscar begins to practice for a Grouch loud-yelling contest.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: At Hooper's Store, Jill asks for two balloons from Mr. Hooper. He climbs up a ladder to get them from a box, then back down to give them to her.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird tries to blow a balloon
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria climbs a ladder to show the viewer what the Sesame Street sign looks like without its E’s. She removes the green pieces of tape covering the E's so it looks right again.
Gordon demonstrates up and down by mailing a letter: he holds it up before putting it down into the mailbox. He then asks Oscar to help out, but he naturally refuses.

altLabels.labelEn: Sam the Machine tries to make a handball
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: David leads Big Bird, Susan, and the kids in doing "The Arm."

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird and Grover play hide-and-seek. Grover is "it" but he keeps forgetting what number comes next and has to get help from Big Bird, who's trying to hide.

altLabels.labelEn: Cookie Monster tries to trick David for a box of cookies
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Luis has finished fixing a mirror frame at the Fix-it Shop. He tells the viewer that sometimes he likes to look into the mirror and make different faces.
At Hooper's Store, Big Bird tells David that he's been practicing adding and subtracting. A new kid in the neighborhood, Alex (nicknamed "Smart Alex") approaches and befriends the two.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob welcomes the viewer from the window of his apartment, introducing some friends who are about to sing a song...

altLabels.labelEn: Sam the Robot makes orange juice
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Susan engages Big Bird, John-John, and Shola in a guessing game on the steps of 123 Sesame Street. Susan has three boxes and has the others try to guess what's inside them based on what they rhyme with.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob greets the viewer while pushing Debo on the tire swing. He asks the other kids around if they have any older or younger siblings, then gauges how old each of them are (as well as the viewers).

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Outside the Fix-it Shop, Luis welcomes the viewer while putting tacks into a coffee can. He leaves for the bank, and Big Bird and Mr. Snuffleupagus find the coffee can.

altLabels.labelEn: Snuffy spills Luis' can of tacks
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria uses a bucket of "magic paint" to paint a duplicate of herself that presents today's sponsors.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird waits for Susan's phone to ring
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird encounters Gordon, David, Bob, Maria, Jay, and the kids collecting empty bottles around the street so they can either be recycled or deposited. Big Bird is elated when Bob asks him to help out, and believes he'll be able to find thousands of bottles.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird helps collect empty bottles; Oscar's phone ringing prank
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird demonstrates the difference between fast and slow with his toy box: first, he dumps the toys on the ground and picks them up one by one (slow). Then, he dumps them out again, and they all go back into the toy box themselves with a reverse-tape edit (fast).

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: While some kids play softball in the yard, Maria introduces the letter H (on her jersey, with an 11 on the back). She joins in the game, and points out the words “hit” and “home run” as she scores them.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar disguises himself as a bush
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Luis saws a wood plank into 6 pieces as the kids (including John-John and Shola) count them. He then puts the plank back together with a reverse-tape edit.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird greets the viewer, wheeling a giant L that he borrowed from some workers who are putting a sign up on a building nearby. Before he can properly explain the shape of the letter L, Gordon arrives to take the L back to the workers.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird tries to fit a barrel through his door
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Loud crashes, jackhammering, and bangs are coming from inside Oscar's trash can. Luis, Susan, Jay, and the kids gather and ask what's going on.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar's noise machine; Big Bird looks after Hooper's Store
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird realizes that it's almost time for him to meet up at the bus station with his cousin Abelardo, who's coming from Mexico. In his rush he realizes that he doesn't have time to return the lunchbox he borrowed from Luis.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird needs to make a phone call to Luis; Oscar plays Grouch Steps
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria welcomes the viewer from her window, and observes the cold weather. Bob calls across from his apartment with information from a weather report that it might even snow, and offers her an extra sweater.

altLabels.labelEn: Snow — Big Bird is all ready for the cold weather
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Everyone steps out into the morning snow, but they're not quite ready. With the blink of an eye, each of them gets equipped with the gear they need for the weather: Susan gets her boots, Luis gets his gloves, a sled pops in for Troy to play with, and a snow shovel pops into Gordon's hand.

altLabels.labelEn: Snow — Oscar orders a million snowballs
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: David is glad to see that the snow has stopped and tells the viewer they're just in time to learn what "next to" means. Through a series of jump-cuts, David stands next to the newsstand, the staircase, and Susan's building.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: At the Fix-it Shop, Luis sweeps the snow off the front step with a broom when he comes across a "SESAMESTREET" sign underneath the snow. He explains the importance of adding spaces between words, and separates the one sign into two.

altLabels.labelEn: Snow — David and Maria figure out how to carry a load of bricks
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar the Grouch is positioned behind his trash can with four snowballs to demonstrate subtraction. As Gordon, Susan, and Bob walk by, he tosses a snowball at them, subtracting one each time.

altLabels.labelEn: Snow — Oscar prepares for a snowball fight
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: On another snowy day, Big Bird leads David into Hooper's Store because he made a present for him. Inside, they find an American Flyer wagon filled with water, a scarf, some cork pieces and a carrot.

altLabels.labelEn: Snow — Oscar tries to do something rotten, but ends up helping people
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: On another snowy day, Gordon is about to brush the snow off the 123 Sesame Street stoop railing, when The Count shows up looking for something to count. He considers counting the millions of snowflakes on the railing until Gordon says he can count the number of times it takes him to brush off the snow.

altLabels.labelEn: Snow — Big Bird looks for a place to deposit snow
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon is shoveling the steps of 123 Sesame Street, annoyed that he has to do it again after another fresh snowfall. To keep warm, Gordon calls Maria, Big Bird, and the kids over to play a rhyming game.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird excitedly welcomes the viewer and builds up they'll be doing a lot of fun things today. He runs around gathering everyone else around the street to say hello.

altLabels.labelEn: Snow — Oscar gives out Grouch winter gear
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird can't find his mittens and resolves to buy a new set. Luis asks him why he's on his way to Hooper's Store, but Big Bird can't recall what he meant to buy: "I've got a perfect memory except I never can remember anything!"

altLabels.labelEn: Snow — Luis explains "LOVE" to Sam the Robot
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon, Mauricio, and Reggie count three snowballs, then throw them at the camera.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Early in the morning, Big Bird wakes up and notices he’s the first one up; everyone else is asleep, and even Hooper's Store is still closed. He wants to practice his bass drum, but then imagines the kind of reaction he’d get if he were to do so, with Gordon, Bob, and Maria waking up and complaining.

altLabels.labelEn: Snow — Big Bird wakes up in the morning
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: David sings “What Can I Do?” with the kids, pretending to be cars, planes, and hiccups.

altLabels.labelEn: Snow — Big Bird helps David put away dolls; Oscar disguises himself with a beard
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar plans to trick everyone into saying the word "NO" with his sign. He tries it out on Farley, asking him if he's heard of the doofus who said that word.

altLabels.labelEn: Snow — Snuffy helps Big Bird find something that rhymes with "man"
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria sits with Jay and Vanessa, who are babysitting Kim. They play a game where Kim is asked to point out the things Maria’s wearing that start with S: her sweater, shirt, socks, and shoes.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob greets the viewer, as his head moves up and down out of the shot. What’s he doing?

altLabels.labelEn: Snow — Oscar and Maria prank each other
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: David welcomes the viewer, and tries to display the word UP, but the word keeps rising up. When David tells the word to wait until he gives it the right cue, the word then refuses to cooperate.

altLabels.labelEn: Snow — Big Bird the pirate; Sam the Robot writes a note for David
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird demonstrates front and back (popping in and out of space with the aid of tape edits) using a bicycle, a wagon, and the construction doors.

altLabels.labelEn: Snow — Slimey the Worm performs tricks
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird finds Bob taking a photo of Gordon and Susan. He suggests Big Bird get in the picture as well, but he struggles getting behind them, opting to go in front of and next to.

altLabels.labelEn: Snuffy fills Big Bird's pool; Sherlock Hemlock solves the mystery of Big Bird's missing birdseed
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria introduces the letter B. Harvey Kneeslapper comes in with a B word - box, "the funniest box in the world," he claims.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar witnesses Gordon and Susan being affectionate with one another after they both return from work. He finds their mushiness upsetting, and Gordon believes that Grouches don't know what love is.

Big Bird spots a sign on the construction doors in front of his nest that he has trouble reading, so he calls Maria over for some help, who comes over with Linda. Maria reads it out, "Little Theatre of the Deaf Coming to Sesame Street," and asks Big Bird if he remembers Linda, who can't hear.

altLabels.labelEn: The Little Theatre of the Deaf visits
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Mr. Hooper, Gordon and Kate follow a long clothesline that stretches from Hooper's Store to the doors leading to Big Bird's nest area. Big Bird claims it’s his "new invention" which allows him to place orders from Hooper’s without leaving his nest: just attach a message to one of the clothespins, then wheel it to its destination.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird decides to become a famous inventor
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird attempts to take a box from a pile to keep his eggshell collection in, but Bob warns him it's better to get a box at the top of the pile rather than the bottom. Big Bird wants to find out for himself and gets a bottom box anyway, causing the others to fall over.
Luis listens to some loud Pachanga music on his radio outside the Fix-it Shop. David complains of a headache, but Luis is too into his music and doesn't want to turn it down.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar wins the Grouch of the Year Award
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Susan greets the viewer, asking if anybody has any N words. Luis has a newspaper, and David has a napkin (which he puts on before digging into his sandwich).

Susan welcomes the viewer from their home as she prepares for a dinner visit from Oscar and Kate. She's about to start making a cake in the kitchen when The Count appears, having finished counting her silverware.

altLabels.labelEn: Gordon and Susan have Oscar and Kate over for dinner
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon watches Big Bird rapidly show off some R words - run, race and rush (which he does while imitating the Road Runner), carrying a sign with each word. He finally brings in a stool, which Gordon notices is not an R word - it's for Big Bird to rest on.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird redecorates Hooper's Store to give it bird appeal
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria and Luis greet the viewer, and Maria invites them to do some imagining with her. She imagines that she's almost as small as a group of jacks, and is worried that the enormous kitten that Luis is petting might want to eat her.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird watches as David balances a triangle on his finger, showing that it has three sides and three corners (and is also a trick being played on him).

Peering from over his cape, The Count makes a dramatic entrance to count people who say hello: Maria, David, Luis and Big Bird. At the climax, the four of them cower from the Count's thunder and lightning.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: At Hooper's Store, David is preparing to cook some eggs for Kate and the kids. When he turns on the electric griddle, the store suddenly loses electricity.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Luis tells the viewer why he likes stormy, overcast days. He describes back in his childhood in the desert, he would be fascinated by watching the lightning and hearing the sounds of thunder.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird demonstrates none, some and all as Mr. Hooper is chromakeyed into the shot. Big Bird himself is chromakeyed out of the shot until there's none of him left.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria comes out of 123 Sesame Street carrying a paper bag of trash, but the bag rips apart so Maria goes back inside to get a broom and dustpan. Oscar delights in seeing the spilled trash in front of his can, and decides to add to it with one of his own tin cans.

The camera pans in on Ella Mitchell, sitting along in front of 123 Sesame Street. As she sings "Oh, Brother," everyone in the neighborhood gathers to hear her sing (including Bob, Maria, David, Brynne, Shola, John-John, Mauricio, Ronald, and the other kids).

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird excitedly welcomes the viewer from his nest, and calls Susan over to talk about what will be happening today. Susan asks him to not yell so loudly, especially considering that a baby is napping in the floor above her.

While opening Hooper's Store, David gets angry when he's almost hit by a stack of newspapers thrown at his feet by a newspaper deliveryman. The offscreen driver of the newspaper truck (voice of Caroll Spinney) apologizes to David, who handles the situation calmly and decides to get the second stack of papers handed to him instead (despite the broken twine tied around it).

altLabels.labelEn: A rainy day on Sesame Street
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird wonders where everyone is today. Pete Seeger passes through, asking if he's seen Jimmy Collier around.

altLabels.labelEn: Pete Seeger and Jimmy Collier visit
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Everybody on Sesame Street (including Bob, the Busby Twins, Maria, Big Bird, Roosevelt Franklin and his mother, Gordon, Luis, Cookie Monster, and some kids) all clap to a Johnny Carson-style version of the Sesame Street Theme.

Big Bird has been thinking about up and down lately, and wonders what the world would be like if everything was topsy-turvy. He gives it a try by twisting his head so he can look upside-down, and observes Gordon throwing the basketball down instead of up, then sees Maria going up the stairs instead of down, and a kid who drops his ice cream cone up.
Luis says S.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Mr. Hooper has the day off, but drops by the store to check-in. He sees David has his nose in a book instead of working, which he finds upsetting at first.

altLabels.labelEn: David tries to study for a law school exam
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: As David rides by on his delivery bike, Oscar asks him to hold a rope while he goes to get a glass of milk. David overhears Oscar making a table, then sewing a napkin, then milking a cow — which is attached to the rope he's holding.

Maria wants to show today's number in a special way, so she calls Big Bird over so he can assist her and the kids in showing what it is. Big Bird counts Maria and two kids which makes 3, but that isn't the number.
Oscar sets out six pieces of junk that he intends to subtract. He explains to Gordon that they keep falling out of his closet, so he’s subtracting them by throwing them out onto the street.

Gordon, Susan, and the kids see a giant pipe next to Oscar's trash can, billowing lots of pungent smoke. Oscar explains that it's for his new business, thinking of how he'll be able to sell what he's making in his factory to all the Grouches.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: David greets the viewer, mentioning that he has a big headache. He notices Oscar wearing a stethoscope and putting out a sign on his trash can reading “Doctor Oscar” with a red cross on it.
Luis teaches Vanessa how to play a guitar chord, encouraging her to keep trying.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar installs a doorbell on his trash can
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria observes Oscar putting up a "WET PAINT" sign on his trash can, thinking it will trick everybody into believing that he painted the can and they'll stay away. Shortly after Maria leaves, Gordon walks by and sees the sign, not believing Oscar actually painted the can.
The Count is sad as he wants someone to count with him. He tries asking a kid, then Oscar (whom he almost hypnotizes), but they either can't or don't want to.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Kate plays guitar and sings “All Over Everything” as the kids play different kinds of games in the yard.

altLabels.labelEn: Gordon threatens to stop giving Oscar trash until he learns some manners
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Luis shows off his new hat, but notes that the box got mangled a bit on the bus ride home. Oscar is in awe of its color and structure, so Luis says since he loves it so much, he'll give it to him.

altLabels.labelEn: Luis buys a new hat; Big Bird orders bags of birdseed
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: "You...who said you could come here?" Oscar asks the viewer before showing off a dirty shape he has.

altLabels.labelEn: Grover and Queenie comment on sketches
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon welcomes the viewer and announces that T is the letter of the day. He notices a T on Oscar's trash can and inquires about why it's there.

In the yard, "Magical Maria" tries to make a letter V appear from her hat. It takes awhile, but a tiny Kate appears from the hat with the V, apologizing for the delay (the V got caught on the lining).
Oscar joins David in singing "What Can I Do?" with the kids as Oscar suggests everyone pretend to be bulldozers, a traffic jam in Akron, and a herd of cattle.

Big Bird tries to organize some people in the neighborhood for a photograph, including Gordon, Maria and the kids. He asks for the "little people" to pose on the steps of 123 Sesame Street, and the "big people" to stand next to them.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird tries to organize some people in the neighborhood for a photograph
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: David waters the tree on the street. The Count comes by, eager to count something, and starts counting the hose and the drops of water coming from it.
Luis and the kids notice Oscar doing physical exercises in his can while counting. They join him in doing eight deep-knee bends and eight jaw stretches.

altLabels.labelEn: Susan shows Big Bird that he's important on Sesame Street / Big Bird builds a nest
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob sings "Hi Friend" with Susan, Gordon, and the kids.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird guesses that Susan is going to the shoemaker
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: At Hooper's Store, Mr. Hooper receives a parcel containing some dolls that he's ordered. The Count slinks in and introduces himself before counting the 10 dolls Mr. Hooper places on the shelf.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Stevie Wonder performs "123 Sesame Street."

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: As Bob and Grover greet the viewer, Sam the Robot arrives on the scene. Grover, never having seen the living machine before, is scared out of his skin.

altLabels.labelEn: Grover is afraid of Sam the Robot
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria finds Oscar smashing cookies with a hammer, preparing them for a Grouch party he intends to throw. Maria assists him in sprinkling pepper into the punch, and assumes that the napkins Oscar will set out are more like dirty rags.

altLabels.labelEn: Sam the Machine becomes a time machine
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Kate greets the viewer from Big Bird's nest with a few kids (including Joey). Big Bird arrives and wants to show Kate his new "Pete Cigar" record, but first he wants to call Susan as she's borrowing it.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird finds that life without a telephone can be exhausting

episodes.summaryEn: Riding his delivery cart, Mr. Hooper stops in front of Oscar as he begins to conduct an orchestra inside his trash can, the Grouch Philharmonic.
