episodes.summaryEn: Maria and David introduce Pete Seeger, who is about to chop a log. Big Bird thinks it’ll tire him out, but Pete tells them to join him as he sings "Didn't Old John" while he chops.

altLabels.labelEn: Pete Seeger and Jimmy Collier visit
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob encounters Sam the Robot, standing next to a U.S. weather map.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: The kids look up and see Alphabet Bates skywrite the letter Z.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar decides to move his trash can
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria overhears Oscar wailing, and goes over to investigate. He's mourning the loss of the trash he saw littered all over the street an hour before.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon introduces today's sponsors and demonstrates none, some and all: when Harvey Kneeslapper tells jokes to all of a crowd, he drives away some of the people, until there are none left.

altLabels.labelEn: Prince Charming has a cold; Grover plays a sound game with Oscar
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird tries to demonstrate in, on, and under, but has a difficult time. In his search, he can't find anything in the garage, under the stairs or the table outside, on David's stool in Hooper's Store, under the newspapers, on the fire hydrant, or on Maria's and Susan's heads.

altLabels.labelEn: Maria tries to get Oscar to say "please"; Big Bird needs help demonstrating subtraction
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: The Count counts the various items at Hooper's Store while David tries to study. To distract him from counting so much, David suggests that the Count find something else that he may enjoy, like rhyming.

altLabels.labelEn: David tells the Count to find words that rhyme with tree
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon asks Luis to help him lug a piano downstairs; in exchange, he’ll work at the Fix-it Shop on Saturday.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird uses Susan's old eye chart to test Mr. Snuffleupagus' eyesight, but Snuffy isn't able to tell him any of the letters he sees. Big Bird says his mother should know how terrible his eyesight is.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob initiates a rhyming game with the cast, rhyming the word "hello." Susan watches a flower grow on her windowsill, while a kid makes a slow throw with a ball to Gordon.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird wonders where Mr. McIntosh is
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: David tunes his radio to some funky music which he and the others dance to. Big Bird is surprised to learn that the kids are teaching the grown-ups some new moves: Reggie shows Maria how to do "the Basketball" while Shaun and Luis step in time, and David and Joey flail their arms and legs.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob tries to use reverse psychology on Oscar to get him to count backwards from 10 to 1 by asking him to count forwards instead. Oscar gets wise and counts forward just as Bob asked.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird stops by Hooper's Store to ask "Mr. Dooper" for something. Tired of Big Bird always mispronouncing his name, Mr. Hooper produces two cards and has Big Bird read them.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird tries to remember how to pronounce Mr. Hooper's name
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar practices for his Grouch magic show, where he plans to make things disappear. He wishes to practice alone, but Susan and the kids have no plans on leaving.

altLabels.labelEn: Mr. Hooper and David have an argument
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria is busy putting her laundry on the clothesline from her apartment window. Bob also has a basket of wet clothes ready to be put out to dry, and reminds Maria that today was supposed to be his day to use the line.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird watches a nature program on TV; Oscar changes his name to "George the Grouch"
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon welcomes the viewer and finds the word "TELEPHONE" near Oscar's trash can. Oscar explains that it's for his latest invention: a Grouchophone.

altLabels.labelEn: Rafael moves to Sesame Street; Big Bird helps Susan inflate her bike tire
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon wheels a shopping cart of groceries back to 123 Sesame Street. He can't take them all in at once, so he asks Big Bird and Grover to keep an eye on it while he goes inside.

altLabels.labelEn: Prince Charming looks for Sleeping Beauty
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: At the Fix-it Shop, Luis is working hard on fixing a radio when The Count saunters in and startles him. Luis berates the Count and expects to be bothered by his incessant counting.

altLabels.labelEn: Mr. Hooper loses his glasses, finds Mr. Snuffleupagus
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: A cheerful Maria says hello to the viewer, as well as to a grouchy Oscar who mocks her high spirit and points out that she seems happy all the time. He wonders if anything makes her angry, and continues to push her buttons and interrupt her until she yells her answer: "YOU!!"

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Luis watches as Oscar recites the alphabet to an audience of Grouches inside his can, who all boo and toss junk at him (the highest form of Grouch flattery).

altLabels.labelEn: Luis has Biff put up a DANGER sign; Sam the Robot is too big to enter Hooper's Store; Big Bird's home movies
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: At the Fix-it Shop, Big Bird notices that Luis has a new pet canary in a cage, and feels left out when Luis says it sings beautifully. He’s not that impressed, saying he's a bird, too, and tries to sing for Luis.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird buys a newspaper from Mr. Hooper to give to Susan, but he gets distracted on the way by joining some kids in making paper dolls. While doing so, he accidentally uses Susan’s newspaper to make a pair of paper girls.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird writes a giant note to Snuffy; The Count has chickenpox
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: While happily walking down Sesame Street, Big Bird overhears his friends’ conversations. Bob and Susan talk about someone who’s “tall and cute, but awkward” and “bumps into everything.”

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird tries to run away
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: David watches as Big Bird vacuums his nest in preparation for the arrival of his friend from the forest, Waldo Woodpecker. When Waldo arrives he pecks on the door softly, but Big Bird doesn’t notice from the vacuum noise.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Susan tells Bob and Luis what she heard from Big Bird: when he was young, he couldn’t see well, was kept in the dark, and was often alone. They all assume he had a troubled childhood because of that, so they visit him.
At Hooper's Store, Mr. Hooper has Big Bird guess what we'll be learning about today using a glass. When he fills it with water, it's full, but when he drinks it, it's empty.

altLabels.labelEn: Everyone looks for things that rhyme with "toot"
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: In the early hours of the morning, Big Bird greets the viewer and tells them his job today is to make sure things are quiet for everyone who's still asleep. Just then, milk delivery person Millie (Rita Moreno, reprising her role from The Electric Company) appears and wonders what's going on.

altLabels.labelEn: The Electric Company meets Sesame Street
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon encounters The Count waiting at the bus stop. It looks like rain, so the Count asks Gordon to hold his bus while he goes to fetch his umbrella.

altLabels.labelEn: The Count waits at the bus stop; Big Bird, Snuffy, and the kids play a pretending game
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Sam the Robot encounters Luis and the kids painting pictures. Sam announces a picture making contest, certain he’ll win because machines are better than people.

altLabels.labelEn: Sam the Robot's paintings; Oscar makes popcorn
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Biff comes to Hooper's Store to buy what he assumes is lots of things for his friend Moose at the plant. Biff goes on to describe everything that is requested; something round, something white, something plastic, something that bounces, and so on.

altLabels.labelEn: Biff buys ping-pong balls; a hipster describes things on the street; Big Bird's block tower
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria is in a hurry to get to an exam and asks Big Bird to do two favors for her: give David the dollar bill she owes him, and place her letter in the mailbox for her mother in Puerto Rico.

altLabels.labelEn: Sam the Robot wants to go to the movies
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird displays a number 9, and demonstrates it by spinning around 9 times. ("Why, you'll really be able to call me a spinney!") He gets dizzy after his performance, and his eyes see Maria split into multiple people.
Big Bird finds the letter G on the basement railing of 123 Sesame Street. He tries to think of a G word as the letter says, "Grow," over and over again, increasing in size.
At Hooper's Store, David complains about the rain, but the Count counts raindrops. David's attempt to engage him in conversation causes the Count to lose his place, so he starts all over.

altLabels.labelEn: A rainy day on Sesame Street
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Outside the Fix-It Shop, Grover is hesitant to aid Big Bird in a lesson on subtraction (using heavy bags), since he usually gets the short end of the stick. Big Bird assures him that he will do the hard part, while Grover will do the easy part this time.

Oscar the Grouch tells Biff to knock off the racket he's making with his jackhammer in front of his trash can. Biff goes on a rant about how he and Sully hear complaints like that all the time, but he's a city worker who must repair the street, noise or not.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar moves into a dirtier trash can
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Susan calls Mr. Hooper over to look at a sign on 123 Sesame Street: "Sam’s Singing School." Sam the Robot has started his own school where he teaches singing.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Jimmy Collier performs "Love and Drive" as Luis, Susan, and Big Bird help Akim learn to rollerskate. The others (including John-John and Joey) join in on the chorus.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird sees Gordon and some kids playing “Pin the Tail on the O,” where players try to add the line on an O to make it into a letter Q. Big Bird joins in their game, and Gordon blindfolds then spins him around when it's his turn.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar disguises himself as a baby; Big Bird gets a postcard from Poco Loco
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar meets the new sanitation man (played onscreen by Jerry Nelson), who hauls away the trash near his can. The worker almost picks up Oscar's trash can itself, but Oscar protests, saying it's his home – the regular sanitation man knows that.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar and the sanitation worker; Big Bird tries to order birdseed; Big Bird eats his birdseed sundae for a long time
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Susan leads Big Bird, John-John, Nicki, and Martha in a "short/long" game, where they compare the length of their hair and their jackets. Big Bird feels left out since he doesn’t have hair or a jacket, but he does have the longest neck, which he boasts about to Mr. Hooper.

altLabels.labelEn: Snuffy eats some, more, and the most spaghetti
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: All is fine on Sesame Street in the evening; Luis is drilling something at the Fix-it Shop, and Maria returns home, saying hello to David who's enjoying some music on his radio at Hooper's Store. Suddenly, all the lights and power go out.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: In the morning, after a stormy night, Bob, David and Maria observe how wet it is outside. Oscar arrives back to his can after having a campout in the rainy park, discovering his home is now full of water.

Gordon and Susan have an argument about chores: Susan wants Gordon to take out the trash, but Gordon would rather do it later. Oscar cheers them on as they argue, with the couple periodically telling Oscar to mind his own business.

Early in the morning, Luis has to make some deliveries and asks Big Bird to pass along a message to Bob that he can’t go fishing with him today. Big Bird tries calling for Bob at his apartment window, but Bob can’t open the stuck window and can't hear what he's saying.
Oscar agrees to watch the Fix-it Shop while Luis steps out for a few minutes. Before Luis leaves, Oscar answers the phone twice and is rude to both customers.

It's nighttime on Sesame Street and the locals (Gordon, Bob, Maria, Mr. Hooper, and the kids) are engaging in evening social activities. Some of them are dancing to some rock music near the stoop, and when they get on his nerves, Oscar decides he's going to have to scare everyone in order to make them go away.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird decides to visit Luis at the Fix-It Shop. He ends up surprising Luis in the middle of repairing a television, which blows up in his face.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird plans to run away
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon sets down a bucket of water to clean the windows of 123 Sesame Street and asks Big Bird to watch it for him while he goes back in for some cleaning rags. Mr. Snuffleupagus comes along with a case of the hiccups, which Big Bird says can be cured with a glass of water, so Snuffy empties the bucket with his snuffle.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: David and Maria explain to Big Bird what being proud means. David is proud of having just shot nineteen baskets in the yard, while Maria is proud of being able to speak both English and Spanish.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird is proud of riding a unicycle / Oscar sabotages David's date
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Linda and her friends from the Little Theatre of the Deaf — Timi, Freda, Ed, and Joe — chat with Gordon on the stoop of 123 Sesame Street. A fire engine drives by clanging its bell and blaring its siren, and Mr. Hooper tries to explain what just passed.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: During a heavy downpour, Maria and David take shelter under the awning of Hooper's Store. Neither of them has an umbrella, so they decide to cooperate: David shares Maria's old newspaper to use as a temporary umbrella, and they both rush over to 123 Sesame Street to deliver some groceries and (almost) without soaking Maria's bag of books.
Big Bird wakes up early in the morning, and is surprised to see that the Fix-it Shop's door is open and the lights are still on. He finds Luis inside, sleeping at the counter.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria, David, Gordon, and the kids pester Oscar the Grouch at his can about helping them teach the audience the concept of big, bigger, and biggest, but he's not having it. In response, he produces a sign he's made with a definitive answer to their plea: "NO".

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird approaches Luis, who is working on a cuckoo clock on the bench in front of the Fix-It Shop. Luis is having trouble fixing it, so Big Bird takes a look at it and suggests keeping the clock warm and giving the bird lots of orange juice until it gets better.

The Count greets the viewers perched on top of the Sesame Street lamppost so he can count all the lights on the street as they come on for the evening. He counts the various lights as they are turned on by Luis (opening the Fix-It Shop), Mr. Hooper (at his store), Bob, David, Maria, Gordon and Susan, Bert and Ernie, Oscar, and Big Bird.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird finds David dozing at the door of Hooper's Store. David explains that he was up late last night studying for a law school exam, but had promised Mr. Hooper to take care of the store the next day.

altLabels.labelEn: David is too sleepy to take care of Hooper's Store
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: It's a rainy and windy day on Sesame Street, and Oscar couldn't be more thrilled. He tries talking about it with Mr. Hooper, who wishes to be left alone as he reads inside his store.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar is delighted by the rainy day outside
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: The Count coaches David through filling some candy jars with beans and explains he's going to play the sorting game; although not with sizes, but with numbers. David explains no one could ever count as many beans as he's poured into the jars; no one, that is, except for the Count.

altLabels.labelEn: Sam the Machine tries to act like a grandmother
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird tells the viewer that sometimes he worries about getting lost and finding his way back home. So, he's hatched a foolproof plan to help him get back to his nest: he leaves a trail of stale breadcrumbs from his nest to Hooper's Store.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird tries to leave a trail of bread crumbs so he won't get lost
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Biff directs Sully while he's driving, causing him to back into the mailbox in front of 123 Sesame Street. The crash prompts Maria to come out and see what happened, but Biff is too busy overcomplicating the mess to explain himself to the "little lady."

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar invites Bob into his trash can
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob, Susan and Luis fawn over Bob's new canary, Fairbanks, making Big Bird jealous. They remind Big Bird of the things he can do because he's a big bird, like counting to 5, saying the alphabet, and rollerskating.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar gets his hand stuck in a jar
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar's rock band, the Groovy Grouches, can't make it to rehearsal today, so he shows Susan his replacement players: Shola on trash guitar, John-John on tenor grouchophone, and Laurie on trash can drums. Oscar admits they don't sound great individually, but when they all cooperate and play together...

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird writes a love note to Maria
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird introduces the viewer to Poco Loco, a parrot who repeats almost everything he says. This nearly ruins his talk on the difference between their sizes, as Big Bird worries about Poco confusing the viewer about who really is big or little.

altLabels.labelEn: The Amazing Mumford decides that he's all washed up as a magician
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: The Count encounters a bespectacled Big Bird finishing some poems in one of his books. Count offers to help find rhyming words for his poems, which coincidentally happen to all end with numbers.

altLabels.labelEn: The Count helps Big Bird write a poem
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird is reading his "Western Tales" book and thinks it might be fun to have lived life as a cowboy. He begins to imagine what it would be like living in the Old West...

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird imagines that he's living one hundred years ago
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird tells Susan, Gordon and Luis that he is about to leave for a vacation, but Luis notices that his suitcase is empty. (Big Bird: "Whoever heard of going on vacation without a suitcase?") Big Bird says he doesn't need anything but a rest, so they start listing things he may want to pack: his pajamas, his beakbrush (instead of a toothbrush), his bathing suit, his sailboat, and so on.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: The Count is bored, having counted nearly everything on Sesame Street. As an example, he states the number of steps in 123 Sesame Street and the number of bricks making up the garage from memory.

altLabels.labelEn: Sam the Robot confuses everyone by imitating sounds
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar has Bob and Maria fish in his can so he can illustrate "heavy" and "light," though Bob and Maria are skeptical. To their amazement, Bob ends up catching a light fish.

altLabels.labelEn: The Count counts things in Oscar's trash can
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: While Biff and Sully dig up Sesame Street, Oscar loses his phone service and Susan's water stops running. Just as Biff tells them all will be restored after the work, Susan gets a call from Oscar's grouch hotline on her hose, and water starts spraying out of Oscar's phone.

altLabels.labelEn: David turns into a hot dog
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Luis has dumped out all his screws and nails to find just the right one to fix Bert's radio at the Fix-it Shop. He has to drop it off soon (Bert doesn't want to miss an upcoming interview with a pigeon commisioner), but dreads having to clean up the mess.

altLabels.labelEn: The Count helps Luis by putting away nails and screws
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob finds a young Muppet girl named Jane, who thinks her name is boring.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird helps David to keep from falling asleep
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar is bothered by the kids hanging around his can. He believes people like to bother him because they enjoy watching him be grouchy.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar impersonates other people on the Street
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Grover the Photographer has his camera out, looking for subjects to capture. He sees David and Maria nearby, but they're already engaged in their own photo session.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar is having a Grouch baseball game inside his can, but the umpire just quit and he needs a new one. Luis volunteers, so Oscar hands him the proper hat and face mask.

altLabels.labelEn: Luis becomes an umpire for Oscar's baseball game
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria exits 123 Sesame Street and is shocked to find a tree potted right in front of Oscar's trash can. Maria teases Oscar with her bag of trash, which Oscar accepts through the leaves.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar plants a tree in front of his trash can
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Linda sits outside reading. David wants to sit by her and makes sure she's okay with that.

altLabels.labelEn: The Little Theatre of the Deaf visits
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Sam the Robot wants to play, but Susan says he can't jump rope since he doesn't have feet, Big Bird says he'll break the rope swing since he's too heavy, and Bob tells him he sings like a railroad train when he tries to join in with him and Luis. He tells his woes to Oscar the Grouch, who recommends they instead not do all the things Sam can't - by just sitting there.

altLabels.labelEn: Sam the Machine plays a game with Oscar
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird wants to join in a game with Maria and the kids, though Maria thinks it might be difficult as it involves Spanish. Big Bird gives it a try anyway, and correctly guesses the body parts Maria is saying in Spanish as the kids demonstrate each one.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar admires the sound Maria's hammering makes as she nails a poster advertising the block association meeting later. ("Sounds like 'Sonata for Door and Hammer' by Ludwig von Grouch!") Maria ends up hitting her finger, and warns Oscar not to enjoy her pain.

altLabels.labelEn: Maria hits her finger with a hammer; Snuffy waits for the bus at Hooper's Store
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: At Hooper's Store, David sings about his "Subtraction Blues" while Mr. Hooper, Maria and Jay subtract his slices of pizza as David makes his way down the street. He drops the last slice on the ground when the kids bump into him, and tosses the final dirty slice into Oscar's trash can.

altLabels.labelEn: Maria imagines that she's a bus driver
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar asks the viewer if they have any trash, as he's noticed there's a considerable shortage of it for him lately. He's expecting a group of Grouches from Cincinnati to visit, and finds himself in desperate need of trash for games.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar is expecting a group of Grouches from Cincinnati
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bert is admiring his bottle cap collection when he offers to show the viewer his rarest piece: a Watermelon Whip. Upon closer inspection, he finds that the rare item is lost.

altLabels.labelEn: Bert loses his favorite bottlecap. / Cookie Monster fills suitcases with cookies
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: At Hooper's Store, Biff wants to share a glass of chocolate milk with Sully. To ensure they both get an equal amount, Biff asks Mr. Hooper to draw a line around the middle of glass; Biff claims the top half of the drink as his and the bottom for Sully.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Luis leaves the Fix-it Shop to deliver a radio and notices a sign on Oscar's trash can that reads: "OSCAR'S BREAK-IT SHOP." Oscar explains that with his new business he intends to break items that already work.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Luis and Linda are washing the windows above the Fix-It Shop when the store's phone rings. Luis asks Linda to answer it, but then remembers that she’s deaf, and climbs down from the ladder to answer it himself, more than once.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: On a very cold morning, Big Bird calls Gordon (dressed in a T-shirt, briefly coming out to take out the trash) and the kids into his nest for a quiz game. He asks them all what happened last night that froze his bucket of water, stiffened his wet laundry, caused his plant to wilt, and brought down the thermometer.
Luis gives Big Bird a box to put things away while he cleans out his nest, but Big Bird realizes he'll need more. He goes to Hooper's Store and places his box on one of the stools.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar tries to have peace and quiet
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob talks to Debo and Revy about how he can recognize someone’s voice without seeing them. Big Bird joins them (situating himself on Bob's lap) and they all imagine they're at a “sound zoo,” with animal sounds coming from the empty cages.

Big Bird tries helping Rod and Jenny get a ball that is stuck on the fire escape of 123 Sesame Street. They try lifting him, and getting a kangaroo to help, but Big Bird is too heavy, and the kangaroo is too far away in Australia.

altLabels.labelEn: Maria borrows a cup of sugar from Oscar's kitchen
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: At Hooper's Store, David is getting ready to send back a box of plastic cups, since he ordered paper cups instead. He explains to Bob that he prefers the paper cups over the plastic ones for environmental reasons (that and he fears what would happen if Big Bird got near glass cups).

altLabels.labelEn: David and Big Bird have a misunderstanding
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird learns about what other birds eat
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki labels the street story as a repeat of Episode 0574. A separately numbered broadcast edition remains a separate inventory record.

episodes.summaryEn: David and Maria explain to Big Bird what being proud means. David is proud of having just shot nineteen baskets in the yard, while Maria is proud of being able to speak both English and Spanish.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird is proud of riding a unicycle / Oscar sabotages David's date
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki labels the street story as a repeat of Episode 0660. A separately numbered broadcast edition remains a separate inventory record.

episodes.summaryEn: Mr. Hooper and Susan talk to the kids and Sam the Robot about what rhyming is. Sam shows off his rhyming prowess with the word "red."

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird is jealous of the Count
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: David and the kids observe Kyle's pet dog. David recalls seeing how little it was as a young puppy, and uses Luis' tape measure to see how big it is now.

altLabels.labelEn: The Count wants to count everybody in the world
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Back from a long trek, Buffy finally reaches Sesame Street. She visits Hooper's Store for some breakfast, but it’s so early in the morning that the store isn’t open yet.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird shows Susan the life-size photo portrait of himself he had commissioned. She points out that something's wrong - the portrait is upside down.
Luis brings David some fresh baked oatmeal cookies. He thinks they’re the best, but David has him try one of the vanilla cookies he made in the store this morning.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob, Gordon, and Big Bird arrive for some breakfast at Hooper's Store, but they notice that the store hasn't been opened at its usual time. It's still dark inside, and Big Bird's imagination goes wild when he believes that Mr. Hooper has been abducted by space creatures.

altLabels.labelEn: Mr. Hooper stays up all night studying
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Buffy greets Luis, Biff, and Sully at the Fix-it Shop, telling them she needs a place to stay since the hotel where she normally stays when she visits Sesame Street is all booked up. Biff offers to build her a place from scratch, but she can’t wait for the construction as she needs it by tonight.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria and some kids see a sign on Oscar's can: "INSULTS 5¢." Oscar says he’s now charging a nickel for each insult he gives rather than just giving them away.

altLabels.labelEn: Snuffy leans against Big Bird's door; Biff and Sully build a subway tunnel
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird wakes up in the morning after his alarm goes off. He tells us that Mr. Snuffleupagus slept over at his nest, but now he seems to be missing, along with the blanket he slept with.

Maria works in the Fix-it Shop trying to fix a staticky radio. While she goes to look for a new tube, a Martian (Jerry Nelson) appears, sees the radio, and guesses that it’s either a cat, a chicken, or a doggy.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: A short Fat Blue Anything Muppet boy (Jerry Nelson) invites the viewer to a game about perspectives. First, we see how things look from his point of view close to the ground, where he only comes up to Luis and Big Bird's knees.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria encounters Oscar the Grouch waiting at the corner bus stop. Every time she asks him if he’s going somewhere or related questions, he answers with his favorite word: "No."

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Susan sings that it takes "Two to Seesaw."

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar takes the Hooper's Store phone
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Walking toward Hooper's Store, Big Bird frets about being so tall and wonders what it would be like to be short like everyone else. He sees Mr. Hooper through the window, surprised to see how tall he's become; it turns out he's just standing on a stool to feather-dust the top of his shelf, making him look taller than Big Bird.
Herry Monster sets out a pile of bricks on the stoop of 123 Sesame Street for Maria. She notes it must have been effortless for a monster such as him and believes having his strength must be great.

altLabels.labelEn: Maria imagines that she's as strong as Herry Monster
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar the Grouch tries to convince the viewer to change the channel to watch some cartoons, but Herry Monster, Susan, and Gordon provide a tease for some of the segments coming up in this episode. Oscar makes another attempt to get them to change the channel to the Super Bowl.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar starts a fire in his trash can
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird and Mr. Snuffleupagus recite the first half of the alphabet soft, and the second half so loudly that it attracts the attention of Bob and David. They knock on the door to Big Bird's nest to ask him to come out and Snuffy leaves to go home for his nap.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird finds a lost boy / Winnie Wiggins introduces herself
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon finds Big Bird speaking to the arbor post and a wagon. Big Bird reminds Gordon that Maria's cousin Ada is coming to visit all the way from Puerto Rico, so he's making sure he can remember the Spanish phrase he's learned.

altLabels.labelEn: Maria's cousin Ada visits from Puerto Rico
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar notices a lady wearing a broad-brimmed hat sitting on the stoop of 123 Sesame Street reading a book. He tries to get her to scram, only to have the woman ignore him.

Oscar the Grouch prefers his own, battered seesaw to the functional one that Chris and Jerome are using in the yard. Susan tells him how a proper see-saw works, and Oscar reluctantly agrees that it looks more fun.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar joins the Grouch Club; Buffy joins the Sesamettes
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Herry Monster shows Bob, Maria, and the kids how he's been practicing all week to open and close a door without pulling it off his hinges. Maria is so proud of him, she's going to buy him a glass of milk.

altLabels.labelEn: The Amazing Mumford makes Sesame Street disappear
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon has a picture of 123 Sesame Street on an easel, and asks Elisa, Chrissy, and Lena to put the missing pieces back onto it. After the kids put the door, the windows, the stairs, the flowerbox, and Oscar's trash can in the proper places, a miniature Oscar pops out of the cut-out can, telling them to be quiet and stop bothering him.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird makes a sign for David
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: With encouragement from Maria and Bob, Ernst, Carolyn, Laurie, and Christopher crawl under a bridge made with two chairs in the yard to get to Big Bird, who rewards them each with a hug and a kiss. Big Bird wants a turn, but finds that he's too big to get under the chairs - but not too big to get more hugs and kisses from everybody.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: David cleans up Hooper's Store in preparation for a visit from his grandmother, whom he hasn't seen in a long, long time. He chides Maria and Big Bird when they come close to touching anything in the store as he prepares for her arrival.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Susan finds Maria having trouble repairing the sink at the Fix-it Shop. The only tool that can help fix it is a Stillson wrench, but Susan points out that she knows somebody who has one: Oscar the Grouch.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird opens the Sesame Street Pretend Zoo
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird tells Luis, Jay, Buffy, and the kids that Maria is taking a chemistry class in school. They watch in awe as she works meticulously at her chemistry set in the yard, combining various liquids.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob and the kids sing "Right in the Middle of My Face."

altLabels.labelEn: Luis and the kids play the "Feely Box" game
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird tells Gordon that he's planning to go on a vacation tomorrow. He wants Gordon's help to see if he has everything he needs, though he has a feeling he's forgotten something.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria and David have lunch in the yard, happy to be alone together. David is about to ask Maria something when Big Bird joins them, not quite understanding the concept of being alone.

altLabels.labelEn: Super Grover helps David close Hooper's Store
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Mr. Hooper and Willy get into an argument about which of them makes the best hamburger. They get a second opinion from Gordon, who prefers Mr. Hooper's burgers, but Luis says that he likes Willy's burgers better.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob is greeted by Linda and her friends from the Little Theatre of the Deaf (Ed, Julliana, and Robert). Bob recalls how to say "How are you?"

altLabels.labelEn: The Little Theatre of the Deaf visits
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird, not having gotten enough sleep, sits on the steps of 123 Sesame Street to take a short nap. He sets an alarm clock next to him, which will go off in a few minutes.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird imagines that he's married
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria strolls down the block when she notices a sign on the doors to Big Bird's nest reading, "Big Bird's Invention Company." Inside, Big Bird shows Maria his latest invention: a letter Y.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird enters Hooper's Store and is surprised to see Buffy singing a song without moving her mouth. She explains that what he heard was a recording she just made on her tape recorder, and shows how the machine works.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird records the alphabet on tape
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: This episode is adapted from the 1975 album Bert & Ernie Sing-Along. It was written by Joseph A.

altLabels.labelEn: Ernie disrupts Bert's bath with a sing-along
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird makes his way to Hooper's Store humming a tune and finds that Linda is minding the store while David is out. He wants to ask for bird seed, but he doesn't know how he'll communicate it with her since she's deaf.

altLabels.labelEn: David leaves Linda in charge of Hooper's Store
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird wakes up early ready to play, finding his stickball bat near Oscar's trash can. He rallies Susan and Gordon for a stickball game, but they have to go to work.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird wants to play, but everyone is busy
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird calls Bob over to hear Frazzle recite the alphabet. Naturally, Bob can't understand a lick of it, but Big Bird can and points out where Frazzle makes errors.

At his store, Mr. Hooper is puzzled that no one ever takes the top issue of the newspaper on the newsstand after witnessing Bob and Mr. Macintosh go for the issue underneath instead. Bob claims that nobody is interested in the top issue as it usually gets ripped by others and sooty from air pollution.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar takes a photo of Mr. Hooper and Bob
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob, Gordon and Luis sit in the yard, bored. David comes by and shows them something he found while cleaning: a ticket to Saturday night's football game.
Oscar gets up in the morning after a very windy night. He sees the wind has blown paper all over the block and he wants to collect it for his own stash.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Today is Gordon and Susan's anniversary. Unbeknownst to Gordon, Susan has taken the day off and is preparing a surprise anniversary dinner in Maria's apartment.
At the Fix-it Shop, Buffy looks on as Luis finishes fixing Gordon's record player. Just as Luis tests it out, Gordon comes in with one of his records to play on it.

Oscar witnesses as Bob and Linda run into each other and have a pleasant exchange, and tries to sabotage their conversation by answering Bob’s questions to her. Bob explains to Linda that Oscar is bothering him while he talks to her, and she yells at Oscar in sign language, thus "out-grouching" him.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: “Oscar van Gogh” finishes painting some realistic looking trash cans and garbage bags on the outside wall of Hooper's Store, thinking it’ll make people upset and grouchy. He ducks out of sight when Gordon, Susan, Maria, and Luis come by having a discussion.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird, Grover and company sing a zany song about surprises.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Mr. Hooper is having trouble with a geometry problem for his night school homework. Bob offers a solution he thinks will work.

altLabels.labelEn: A cow looks for a role to fill.
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: David plays a relay game with the kids, where they first have to hop, then get a balloon from Maria, and finally get a big hug from Big Bird in the yard. Big Bird observes that the game isn't over yet as David and Maria join in for some hugs as well.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar's washing machine/Gordon and Susan invite Big Bird for a trip
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird has just delivered the punchline to a joke for Maria (who isn't laughing) when Linda enters the Fix-It Shop with a TV that gets picture but no sound. Big Bird wonders why that would matter for Linda since she's deaf, so Linda explains that it's out of consideration for any guests she may have over.

altLabels.labelEn: Linda's dad visits for her birthday
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: The Anything-in-the-World Prize Game — Despite not wanting to be bothered, Oscar the Grouch gets every question right.
Grover's kite is stuck in a tree and he can't get it down. While brainstorming with Big Bird, they come up with the idea of standing on each other's shoulders.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird helps Grover get his kite down from a tree
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Luis and Susan come into Hooper's Store, where Mr. Hooper is focused on studying for an upcoming night school exam. He says a friend from his class is coming over to help study, but he can't mind the store while studying.

altLabels.labelEn: Mr. Hooper studies with a friend
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Luis has Spencer, Cheryl, Ernst, Alicia, and Heather play a game in which they stand in a line and pass a bunch of ping-pong balls to the next person using different containers. The Amazing Mumford joins the fun, and the kids empty the balls into his top hat.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: While reading "How to Be a Detective," Big Bird learns about employing disguises. He dons a false mustache and attempts to listen in on Mr. Hooper and Susan’s conversation about produce prices, but he's instantly recognized.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird tries to be a detective
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob (from his apartment window), Maria, Linda, and Big Bird show how they can say, "Hi, welcome to Sesame Street," in different languages: English (Bob), Spanish (Maria), sign language (Linda), and bluejay (Big Bird). Big Bird then proceeds to welcome the viewer in crow, owl, nightingale, and canary.

altLabels.labelEn: A day with Linda / Maria's surprises
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: The Count sees a rainstorm forming with plenty of thunder. However, everyone (Gordon, Susan, and Luis) is bothered by the noise and assume the Count is responsible with his usual post-counting dramatics.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: In Big Bird's nest area, Big Bird and the kids play “London Bridge” with Mr. Snuffleupagus, then take turns feeding him some cabbages that were sent in by Granny Bird.

altLabels.labelEn: Sam the Robot disguises himself as a tree
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: David sings a song, instructing the kids to ring a bell every time he says "belly button."

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Luis, David, and Susan observe Oscar nearby wearing a beret and using a film camera. ("He thinks he's Kubrick or somebody," David comments.) They witness him filming Maria coming out of Big Bird's nest area, running a gamut of emotions as Oscar calls out instructions.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob goes to meet up with Maria, but instead Big Bird is at their meeting spot. He says she was there, but had to leave, but he has a phone number he can contact her at.

altLabels.labelEn: Maria asserts she can do anything a male can; Herry helps Oscar move his piano
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: As everyone mingles around Sesame Street, Grover is surprised to see the viewer as he hums to the "Sesame Street Theme." He realizes that nobody else has seen them, so he asks the viewer to hide until he tells them to come out.

altLabels.labelEn: Mr. Hooper celebrates the 25th anniversary of his store
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon practices playing his guitar (a pastiche of "What's the Name of That Song?") on the stoop of 123 Sesame Street, attracting the discriminating ear of Oscar the Grouch. Oscar thinks that Gordon can help him practice for his act at the Grouch talent show.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob helps Laurie get properly dressed to go out in the rain to meet Big Bird.

altLabels.labelEn: Luis and Herry cooperate to put up a flyer.
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: In the early hours of the morning, Mr. Hooper groggily opens Hooper's Store for the day; Bob and Count von Count are also in rotten moods as they join him for some coffee. They all didn't get much sleep last night, which leaves them tired and irritable.

altLabels.labelEn: Mr. Hooper leaves the store for five minutes.
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar's TV is busted, only showing picture and no sound. He frets missing his favorite programs on Grouch TV, until he remembers that Linda can read lips and help transcribe the shows for him.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: On a hot day, Big Bird is hoping to beat the heat. He complains about the hot pavement on his bare feet as Luis fixes an electric fan for Hooper's Store, working outside since it's too hot inside the Fix-it Shop.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Mr. Hooper decides to wash the windows of Hooper's Store, feeling that today is a nice peaceful day where nothing unusual will happen. He entrusts Big Bird to watch his bucket of water while he goes back inside the store to get a sponge and squeegee.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird explains to Mr. Hooper what happened to a bucket of water
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird asks Luis and Maria if he can borrow their ladder for a bird game. They put the ladder on the ground and join the kids as they walk along the rungs pretending to be different birds.

altLabels.labelEn: Maria watches Susan on the job
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Susan wants Gordon and the kids to guess the item that she's bought. She gives clues to help them out: she's saved money for it for three months (which doesn't jog Gordon's memory), it's black, made out of metal, glass, and plastic, it clicks, you can't use it in the dark, and people say "Cheese!"

altLabels.labelEn: Gordon tries to guess what Susan has bought
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: David arrives at Hooper's Store to take over for Mr. Hooper, and tells him and Maria about the great movie he recently saw: The Ketchup Men from Mars. David excitedly describes the plot, but Maria has seen it and thinks it was the dumbest movie she ever watched.

altLabels.labelEn: Luis and Maria demonstrate musical instruments from Puerto Rico and Mexico
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Cookie Monster comes to the Fix-it Shop with a large concrete block. Luis uses a chisel and a hammer to round out the block, making it a concrete cookie, which Cookie Monster then eats.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Mr. Snuffleupagus encounters Big Bird practicing his baton twirling for the bird and animal parade next week. Big Bird teaches him how to march, and while Big Bird marches into the yard, Snuffy goes off in the wrong direction, so Gordon and Susan don't see him with Big Bird.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: It's twilight on Sesame Street. Luis fills a large barrel with water to rinse it out, while Mr. Hooper brings out a bowl of water to wipe down the outdoor tables.

altLabels.labelEn: Maria and Mr. Hooper go out for the evening
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Luis describes the sounds of various tools and items in the Fix-It Shop, such as a squeaky bicycle seat, his rubber mallet, his hammer, and a TV set. He admits that sometimes he likes to imitate the onomatopoedic noises to himself before Big Bird comes in with a broken radio.

altLabels.labelEn: Luis describes the sounds in the Fix-It Shop
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird wants to surprise someone, and tries to surprise Maria in the Fix-it Shop. It doesn't work since she spots him immediately, so he goes to surprise David and Bob at Hooper's Store.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird tries to surprise people
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: In the early hours of the morning, Luis strolls over to the Fix-It Shop and discovers that the door is already unlocked. He hears some sounds coming from within and suspects a robber is in the store, and leaves to call the police.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar learns some Grouch phrases in Spanish
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar is unenthused by the way building superintendent Winnie Wiggins has been keeping 123 Sesame Street in tip-top shape. Thus, he has a bouquet of nice flowers he intends to give her, thinking such a kind act will persuade her to grant him a favor - namely, to stop fixing things and let the building fall into disrepair.

altLabels.labelEn: Susan and Gordon have bad days
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Following the events of the previous episode, Big Bird attempts to replace the fallen tree on the street. He knows that trees grow from acorns and has placed one on the ground, commanding it to grow.

altLabels.labelEn: A new tree on Sesame Street
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird watches as Susan starts to replace her car’s flat tire. She realizes her spare tire needs more air, so she goes to fetch a tire inflator in the garage.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Luis makes his way to the Fix-it Shop, passing by Mr. Macintosh, Susan, and the kids. He notices the viewer, and in response sings "I'd Like to Know You Better."
The train finally arrives at City Island. David asks where all the supposed beaches, boats, and fishermen are in such an urban setting as New York City.

altLabels.labelEn: Maria, David, and Big Bird go to City Island
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Susan, Gordon and Maria complain about the cold, windy weather on Sesame Street, attracting Oscar the Grouch, who loves it. He then hands them music sheets for a song he's written, "A Beautiful Day," his ode to rotten weather.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird has finished making a list of things that he wants to do in life, and goes over it with David at Hooper's Store. David points out that the first item, "Grow a mustache," is impossible for a bird, so he crosses it off his list.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Cookie Monster tells Maria he’s just been hired as a baker's assistant, but he’s wearing his baker’s toque over his eyes (having heard others say it's "chez elegant" to have the fluffy part covering his face). Since he cannot see, he believes he can identify the baker by asking them a series of questions.

Gordon greets Mr. Hooper in front of Hooper's Store and says he's looking for his little sister Olivia who's coming to visit him and Susan on Sesame Street today. Mr. Hooper gets Gordon's description of her and says he'll keep an eye out.

altLabels.labelEn: Olivia comes to visit her brother Gordon
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Linda is in a rotten mood today. Maria invites her to do some activities to cheer her up, such as getting coffee or seeing a movie.
As he walks down Sesame Street, Bob’s greeting to everybody is "Have a Nice Day."

altLabels.labelEn: Gordon misses three buses because he took time to help his friends
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird sings "Wonderful Me."

altLabels.labelEn: Count von Count falls in love with a Countess who loves to count
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria walks down the street and stops in her tracks when she notices Oscar's trash can, which has been beautified with flowers, a clean picket fence, and a welcome mat. A piano version of the Sesame Street Theme plays from inside.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: As the evening winds down on Sesame Street, Maria tries to study at the Fix-it Shop, though her headache is making it difficult. The Count arrives to count some nails, but instead decides to give her a few helpful tips in nursing her headache.

altLabels.labelEn: The Count counts all the suggestions he gives to Maria about resting
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: A representative from the Jiffy Construction Company (played onscreen by Peter Friedman) applies a notice on the doors to Big Bird's nest, stating that a 20-story apartment building is scheduled to be built on that spot in ten days. Big Bird excitedly tells Gordon, Susan, Linda, and David then realizes he'll soon be out of a home.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird has to move away
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar the Grouch spots Gordon, Susan, and Olivia walking down Sesame Street and tells the viewer it's about time Olivia's visit with her brother comes to an end because, although they haven't met yet, he's heard about how nice she is. Susan and Gordon retire for the night, but Olivia says she's going to stay up a bit longer, when Oscar greets her and begins to introduce himself.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar welcomes Olivia to Sesame Street
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Cookie Monster sees Mr. Macintosh peddling his produce cart around, but Cookie reminds the viewer that he prefers cookies. He imagines himself in Mr. Macintosh's place, now running a cookie cart.

altLabels.labelEn: Linda stars in Joan of Arc
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: David, Maria and Luis wait at the bus stop in anticipation for David's grandmother Grace to arrive from her farm for another visit. Oscar isn't too enthused, since he expects it to be another lovey-dovey reunion sure to make him disgusted.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird suggests that Judy Collins sing a duet with Mr. Snuffleupagus one day. He touts Snuffy's singing skills and envisions the two singing an operatic version of "The Alphabet Song."

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: All seems normal on the street, when Big Bird rushes out of his nest area with various sheets of paper. He announces to everyone that he's written his very own variety show ("Like Donny and Marie, Sonny and Cher, and the Captain and Kangaroo.").

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria, Luis, and Olivia follow a strange noise to Oscar's trash can, where inside Oscar and his Grouch pals are chopping up his piano to use as firewood. Mr. Hooper comes by to drop off marshmallows, but realizes how dangerous it can be to light a fire inside a trash can.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird wears costumes to pose for pictures
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob and Linda wait for her father Andy to arrive for a visit; Bob is especially eager to show off how much sign language he's learned since the last time he came to Sesame Street. Andy (Andy Vasnick) finally arrives at the bus stop and Bob tries to sign how he's been learning sign language, but Linda and Andy crack up for some reason.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon and Olivia can't believe Oscar's yarn about his pet fly, Freddie, entering the job world. Oscar describes the jobs he's had all this week, such as a baker and a drugstore clerk ("They just said that he was a fly in the ointment").

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bert is getting ready to play in his marching band, and has all the instruments laid out on the street. The cast, led by Bob, demonstrates each instrument while singing about a "Big Brass Band."

altLabels.labelEn: Bert's marching band; Oscar's cooking show; Grover drives
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird and Mr. Snuffleupagus wake up as the morning dawns on Sesame Street, Snuffy having spent the night over at Big Bird's nest. The two friends go on a morning stroll to observe just how quiet the street can be at this time and witness a weary David opening up Hooper's Store an hour early.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird and Snuffy wash the dishes for David
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Luis, Susan and Gordon hear rock music coming from inside Hooper's Store. They walk in and find Mr. Hooper dressed like the young, hip crowd of today (wearing a wig, jeans, and a Farrah Fawcett t-shirt).

altLabels.labelEn: Mr. Hooper wants to stay young
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria tries to study for an important test on the steps of 123 Sesame Street but is distracted by The Count exercising nearby. He admits that he doesn’t exercise to keep in shape and feel good; he just thought it was something to count.

altLabels.labelEn: The Count distracts Maria by exercising
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria notices an angry Olivia throw a bag of trash on top of Oscar's trash can as she rushes off. Maria wonders why she is so upset, and Oscar proposes the way to figure it out is through "trashology": looking through her trash for clues, likening it to how one gets their palm or tea leaves read.

altLabels.labelEn: Olivia's bad day; The Count makes everybody angry
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar is hoping to "better himself" and reads some poetry of his for Maria, Danny, Renee, Jeff, and Katie. The kids have to rhyme the last word of each verse, all of which are noisy sounds that Grouches like.

altLabels.labelEn: Maria and the kids help Oscar complete his poems about noise
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird asks Mr. Hooper at his store to help him wrap a surrpise present for a friend; when it comes to wrapping something, Big Bird admits he's "all feathers." He's brought all the supplies for Mr. Hooper to use, but Big Bird wants his present to be absolutely perfect and constantly points out Mr. Hooper's every movement, worrying about how he folds and wrinkles the paper and asking if his hands are clean.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird gives Mr. Hooper a present
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: The kids help Big Bird feed bags of birdseed to his bird friends in the yard. Big Bird becomes hungry and eats out of one of the bags.

altLabels.labelEn: Children help Big Bird feed his bird friends
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria introduces a guessing game with Linda and Timi, who sign things and the kids guess what the signs mean. Big Bird interjects with immediate and incorrect guesses.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon and Debo go up to the roof of 123 Sesame Street, where Gordon has rarely been before. The two wade through the junk thrown all over to see the views, including the sidewalk in front of the building.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Herry Monster is looking after the Fix-It Shop. Luis phones him from the lumber store, asking Herry to measure the piece of wood on the table for him.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar the Grouch has a sale
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: The Count has been placed in charge of Hooper's Store, grateful for the opportunity as there are so many things he can count. He counts the glasses and plates he’s just cleaned, and then the beachballs, dolls and trucks David has out for sale.

altLabels.labelEn: The Count is left in charge of Hooper's Store
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: It's lunchtime in the yard, and Maria and Luis lay out their lunch. Cookie Monster wants to join, but Maria says he has to eat politely.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird rummages through his toybox and finds a two-week old letter that he forgot to deliver to David. Just then, David’s grandmother Grace arrives at the bus stop and claims authorship of the letter that Big Bird forgot to send, which told David about her arrival today.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Olivia takes photos of David sweeping up in the yard when they smell something funny coming from Oscar's trash can down the street. Upon arrival, they find that Oscar has made a mess on the sidewalk, and ask him what's going on.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar falls in love with Hermine
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon drops off his broken mixer at the Fix-it Shop, where Luis tells him his special plans for today. In response to a suggestion from Susan, he is going to build a birdhouse to put up on Sesame Street, and shows Gordon the blueprint he made for it.

altLabels.labelEn: Luis and Big Bird design a birdhouse
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob and Linda play basketball with Jonas and Leslie until the kids' mother calls them for supper. They go home and take the ball with them, so Linda suggests she and Bob play “pretend” basketball with an imaginary ball.

altLabels.labelEn: Linda uses a machine to call her father on the phone
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Herry Monster asks Maria, Olivia, and David to keep an eye out for his sister Herriet Monster who's coming to the city to look for a job, while Herry runs out to pick up some things for her stay. Herriet arrives via bus and greets Sesame Street's residents, giving David a crushing handshake (oblivious strength runs in the family).

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird listens to Maria fielding a phone call at the Fix-it Shop in Spanish, marveling at how well she's able to do it. She lists the benefits of being bilingual, as she can talk to more people and read different kinds of books.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Farley walks down the street and imagines what kind of job he'll have when he grows up. He observes Luis working at the Fix-It Shop repairing a wagon with John, then pictures owning a store like Mr. Hooper, and finally considers being a photographer when he sees Olivia taking pictures of a kid.

altLabels.labelEn: Mr. Hooper is going to a discotheque
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria calls everyone over to see a parcel sent from Hawaii from Buffy. Inside are pictures of young Cody and a letter inviting them to come visit her.

altLabels.labelEn: Trip to Hawaii — Buffy invites her friends to visit her in Hawaii
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird and Mr. Snuffleupagus look at photos of Big Bird's family in his album. Snuffy doesn't have photos of his extended family, as they all live out in Hawaii.

altLabels.labelEn: Trip to Hawaii — Mr. Snuffleupagus is homesick for Hawaii
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: David is shocked to see Hooper's Store is decked out with banners, streamers and balloons. On the storefront, a large sign reads, "The Home of the Hooperburger!"

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria finishes repairing a TV set. She tests it out just in time to see the ending of "The Big Trip," where a contestant dressed as a slice of pizza has just won a trip to Paris.

altLabels.labelEn: Trip to Hawaii — The Big Trip game show
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: In the morning, Bob and Linda meet at Hooper's Store for breakfast, when Bob realizes that he forgot to wake up Big Bird so he can join them. He goes over to Big Bird's nest and wakes him.

altLabels.labelEn: Luis tries to learn sign language
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon and Susan present Oscar with an old, decrepit chair, which he thinks will be perfect for his living room. They move it around in different ways trying to get it to fit into Oscar's trash can, but nothing seems to work.

altLabels.labelEn: Susan and Gordon have an argument
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird is in charge of Hooper's Store while Mr. Hooper is downtown. Maria compliments him on the hot cocoa he's made, prompting Bob and Olivia to order some too, as well as a round of toast for all.

altLabels.labelEn: Trip to Hawaii — Big Bird plans to go to Hawaii
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird encounters Gordon working on his car, hoping to drive it downtown later today. As Bob and Luis offer suggestions on things to check with the engine, Big Bird goes to the front of the car and points out not-so-helpful parts that might be the problem such as the windshield wiper and the headlight.

altLabels.labelEn: Gordon tries to start his car
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird shows the viewer his poster advertising Hawaii with blank calendar pages in the middle of it. Currently on the front is a big number 9 he drew on it yesterday, representing the number of days left until he goes with his friends to Hawaii.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Janice helps Bob remember how to count to five using her fingers.
Susan has a toy firetruck and describes the different parts to the kids and Big Bird, who becomes inspired to become a firefighter.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird pretends to be a fireman
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird rushes over to Hooper's Store with news for Gordon, Olivia, and Mr. Hooper, but he's too overwhelmed to spit it out. He manages to get enough words out to alert them that the bookmobile has just arrived down the block.

altLabels.labelEn: The bookmobile stops at Sesame Street
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar shows Bob his brand new automatic mud detector, which he intends to use during their upcoming trip to Hawaii. He sets out a bowl of mud to show how it works.
Oscar celebrates the yuchhy, rainy day. He's shocked when the others enjoy the rain as much as him.

altLabels.labelEn: Trip to Hawaii — Preparing for Hawaii
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird does some last-minute packing at his nest in preparation for today's big trip to Hawaii! Big Bird is extra excited since this will be the first time he will become airborne - aboard an airplane, that is - while Mr. Snuffleupagus can't wait to see his relatives.

altLabels.labelEn: Trip to Hawaii — Big Bird and his friends take a trip to Hawaii
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Picking up where the previous episode left off, the Sesame Street gang prepares for their plane to make a landing in Hawaii! Everyone is excited except Big Bird, who's still sad that his friend Mr. Snuffleupagus didn't make the flight.

altLabels.labelEn: Trip to Hawaii — The gang arrives in Hawaii; Big Bird hears the legend of the Snuffleupagus Mountain
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Buffy gets up in the morning to set up a small campfire for her visiting friends. After a brief vocalizing, she sits with her guitar and sings "Kapahi-Waking" over footage of the Hawaiian valleys.

altLabels.labelEn: Trip to Hawaii — Big Bird and Snuffy search for the Snuffleupagus Mountain
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird has a chat with a horse named Herb before joining the rest of the Sesame Street gang as they pack Sheldon's truck before heading off to Samson's place. Big Bird would rather stay behind and search for Mount Snuffleupagus with Snuffy, hoping that Maria's guide book will help them in their quest.

altLabels.labelEn: Trip to Hawaii — Big Bird and Snuffy continue searching for the Snuffleupagus Mountain
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Still determined to find Mount Snuffleupagus, Big Bird and Snuffy take some kids along on their journey. They spot "Mount Sleeping Giant," which doesn't look like a Snuffleupagus but like a giant man sleeping on his back.

altLabels.labelEn: Trip to Hawaii — Big Bird and Snuffy find the Snuffleupagus Mountain at last
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird explains to Herb the horse that everyone is going to have a luau for Cody, who is turning one year old today. He's been put in charge to make sure everything goes smoothly, and calls his friends to wake up so they can get ready for the big day in Hawaii.

altLabels.labelEn: Trip to Hawaii — Last day in Hawaii
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Susan, Gordon, Luis, Linda and David hop on a bus to the airport to meet their friends as they return from Hawaii.
