altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

It's nighttime on Sesame Street and Gordon has set up a telescope in the yard, explaining to some kids (including Debbie) what it's used for. He intends to observe the moon, but when he looks through it he sees nothing.

Big Bird and the kids practice writing their full names, as they intend to get library cards and need to sign their names on them. Big Bird also makes sure David can sign his own name, since he needs a responsible adult to help him apply for a card.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Luis, Susan, and Mr. Hooper have difficulty in explaining what "away from" means to the kids. Luis gets the idea to get Oscar involved by knocking on his trash can, then lingering until Oscar yells at him to get away from his can.

episodes.summaryEn: Olivia talks to Big Bird and the kids about what remembering is, and asks them if they can recall their birthdays and addresses. Big Bird scoffs at how easy this seems, but he fumbles when Olivia asks him what his address is.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob, Linda, and the kids (including Janice and Debbie) use magnets to pretend they're fishing. After catching the wooden fish, Linda is still hungry, so they head over to Hooper's Store to order some real fried fish.

episodes.summaryEn: In the early morning, Gordon takes out the trash, and accidentally locks himself out of 123 Sesame Street. Wishing not to disturb Susan, he tries to get through the living room windows, but they are also locked shut.

Big Bird wants to migrate since lots of other birds do it, but Gordon tells him the reasons why some birds migrate, and how those reasons don’t apply to him since he’s got more advantages than the other birds.

altLabels.labelEn: David delivers a sandwich to Maria
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Buffy and Sheldon notice Herry Monster has brought over his giant toy chest near Hooper's Store, looking for his favorite toy to hand down to Cody. It’s not his Little Bo Peep barbell set, his building bricks, or his Mother Goose sledgehammer, which he all casually tosses out while rummaging through the box's contents.

altLabels.labelEn: Cody receives a teddy bear and a sweater
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria and Luis find Cookie Monster out in the yard, with cookies from different parts of the world that he's received from his "cookie pals." He shows them a kuchen from Germany, a biscotti from Italy, a galletita from Mexico, and finally a cookie from Toledo, Ohio.

Herry Monster visits Susan as she tidies up the apartment, hiding and setting aside objects that might hurt little Cody when he comes over to visit later. Herry offers to help, and despite her initial reluctance Susan allows him as long as he's careful about it.

altLabels.labelEn: Susan babyproofs her apartment for Cody
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon comes stomping out of 123 Sesame Street and angrily bangs on Oscar's trash can. He accuses Oscar of waking him up early on his and Susan's day to sleep in late with the sounds of banging pots and pans.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird has his beak deep in a book, so engrossed in it that he almost bumps into Sheldon and Cody who are on their way to the doctor to get Cody his immunizations. Big Bird agrees on how important this is, as he's been reading all about child care and offers to be a consultant should he and Buffy need his help.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird learns about child care
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Grover plays a sounds guessing game with the viewer, hiding various items from their sight as he makes noise with them. After Grover uses a bell and a rattle in his game Big Bird interrupts and tries to ask what Grover is doing with a trumpet, thus spoiling Grover's next sound.

altLabels.labelEn: Bob's piano playing disturbs Mr. Hooper
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: At Hooper's Store, Luis prepares some hot cereal while Mr. Hooper is away and prepares a bowl for Bob as well. When they get ready to dig in, Bob finds it odd that Luis likes his cereal with sugar and milk.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird is eager to introduce the viewer to today's letter - H (going so far as to cut the opening music short to ensure he's heard clearly). As he thinks of words that begin with H, Mr. Hooper adamantly points to himself.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird wants to play frisbee with Mr. Hooper, but he has to stay at his store to prepare a special dish for Cody. Olivia and Gordon also can't play with Big Bird, as they're busy dealing with things that are for Cody as well.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Mr. Snuffleupagus sneaks up on Big Bird and surprises him. Big Bird thinks he and Snuffy should try the same to everyone else on Sesame Street.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Buffy leaves Cody in Big Bird’s watch for a few minutes while she runs to the cleaners. Mr. Snuffleupagus shows up in her absence, and both of them see that Cody doesn’t look amused.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird tries to amuse Cody
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: The adults and the kids discuss some transportation, as Big Bird tries to guess what they're talking about. He thinks they're discussing a noisy, underground worm, but it's actually the subway.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Linda, Bob, David, and the kids greet the Little Theatre of the Deaf (Candy, Pat, CJ, Janice, and Michael) as they arrive on Sesame Street. Candy, a hearing member, explains that they got held up at a railroad crossing and describe what they witnessed.

altLabels.labelEn: Children pretend to ride in different types of transportation
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird and Grover clean the Fix-It Shop window, both in great pain. When Maria comes out she notices the problem: Grover is hanging upside down cleaning the top part, while Big Bird is squatting down to clean the bottom.

altLabels.labelEn: Cookie Monster outsmarts Maria / Big Bird can't sleep
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Herry Monster sees Maria playing with Cody and his toys. He offers to add more toys into the mix and Maria suggests something big that Cody can't swallow, like blocks.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria, Gordon, and others impatiently wait for the mailman to arrive, as he is bringing their goodbye present for Buffy and family, who are about to head back to Hawaii today. The Muppet postman finally arrives and hands Gordon the package; Gordon immediately slaps a bow on it and gives it to the Wolfchilds.

altLabels.labelEn: Buffy and Cody leave Sesame Street
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: David demonstrates ventriloquism to Gordon, Olivia, Maria, and the kids with Victor the dummy, an act he used to do in high school. Oscar gets inspired to do the same after finding out that dummies can say anything the ventriloquist makes them say, especially when "Victor" tells him to scram.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: The Amazing Mumford stops by Hooper's Store for a quick lunch, but Mr. Hooper is occupied making meals for Gordon and Luis. Mumford tries to speed up the process using magic, making Gordon and Luis' orders appear right in front of them.

altLabels.labelEn: Mumford makes lunch at Hooper's Store
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird wants to visit Luis at the Fix-It Shop and notices a new "One Way" sign applied to the lamppost. Since it's pointing to the direction he wants to go, he obeys the sign until he reaches the shop, which appears to be closed.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon has some trouble trying to start his car. Fred the Wonder Horse stops by and, using his "horse sense," checks the motor and expertly detects the problem.

altLabels.labelEn: Gordon tries to start his car
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: As Mr. Hooper sweeps outside the store, a limousine pulls up on the block. A window rolls down and a man pops out, asking if the store makes old-fashioned egg creams.

altLabels.labelEn: James Earl Jones visits Sesame Street
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Slimey doesn't look his best today, so Oscar has contacted a vet to make a house call. Dr. Purrenbark arrives on the scene and is a bit taken aback; he's never treated a worm before.

altLabels.labelEn: The Count celebrates a batty birthday
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Olivia sings "Walk Proud" to the kids (including Debbie and Marlena).

altLabels.labelEn: Maria and Olivia repair a bike
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: David is surprised to see that Oscar has gone into the fruit-selling business (as evident by his "Farm Fresh Fruit" sign on his trash can), and is further baffled that Oscar's fruit has no defects or worms. David gives into his curiosity and asks for a grapefruit, some grapes, and a couple of apples.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird gets jealous of Gordon's niece
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar has applied a new sign to his trash can reading: "Grouch Area - No Singing, Laughing, Playing, Dancing or Fun Allowed." After showing it to the viewer, he goes back inside to retrieve his bullhorn so he can call everyone over to see his new rule.
Gordon sings "When I Was a Kid" while watching a child playing on the tire swing.
Everyone gathers in the yard to see Bert's theatrical presentation - Pigeons on Parade! The crowd is much less enthused about the experience.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: In the evening, Maria plays hot potato with the kids, while Luis and Mr. Hooper lock up their shops. Mr. Ortiz comes down the block and they recall when he helped at Hooper's Store.

altLabels.labelEn: Mr. Ortiz stays with Mr. Hooper
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird and Olivia wait in a long line at Hooper's Store. Big Bird imagines different ways to get served first: he could force his way in, or he could trick the others into going home, or throw a tantrum … but he’s just not that kind of bird.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob meets Linda's dog Snoopy, who understands sign language commands very well. She demonstrates by having Snoopy follow several signs such as "sit," "speak," and "eat."

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird starts off his day with various clumsy actions, making him feel very upset with himself. Susan cheers him up with a song ("Yourself").

Big Bird regrets putting a hole in his washtub, trying to turn it into a musical instrument. (He blows through it and no sound comes out.) He tells Maria of his dilemma as he has some clothes he needs to launder.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird tries to use a washing machine
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird and The Count are in the Fix-It Shop when Luis gets a call from a relative in New Mexico, where he grew up. His grandparents are building a new house, and Luis agrees to go back to the ranch to help.

altLabels.labelEn: Luis and his friends leave for New Mexico.
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki labels the street story as a repeat of Episode 0810. A separately numbered broadcast edition remains a separate inventory record.

episodes.summaryEn: Following a new version of the "Sesame Street Theme," the truck arrives at the ranch in New Mexico where Spanish-speaking people are waiting. Luis greets his relatives with hugs, and introduces them to his friends.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird arrives at the ranch in New Mexico and makes friends with the animals.
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki labels the street story as a repeat of Episode 0811. A separately numbered broadcast edition remains a separate inventory record.

episodes.summaryEn: Everyone wakes up from a good night's sleep to a beautiful morning in New Mexico. Everyone except Oscar, that is - he can't get to sleep without the loud noises of the trucks and buses back home, sounds which the others would rather avoid.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar tries to get comfortable at the New Mexico ranch.
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki labels the street story as a repeat of Episode 0812. A separately numbered broadcast edition remains a separate inventory record.

episodes.summaryEn: Excited by his experiences in New Mexico so far, Big Bird has saddled up some horses and is sitting on a cart. "Well, howdy-doody there, buckaroos!"

altLabels.labelEn: At the New Mexico ranch, Big Bird misses Mr. Snuffleupagus.
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki labels the street story as a repeat of Episode 0813. A separately numbered broadcast edition remains a separate inventory record.

episodes.summaryEn: Buffy stops by the New Mexico ranch, and tells Maria that she's heading out to Taos Pueblo. Maria offers to take her there in the pickup truck.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird, Maria and Buffy visit the Taos Pueblo.
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki labels the street story as a repeat of Episode 0814. A separately numbered broadcast edition remains a separate inventory record.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird finds out that everybody on the New Mexico ranch gets up early because they have work to do. He tries out the chicken feed that a woman is throwing to the chickens, and says it's pretty good.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird wants to help build the new house at the New Mexico ranch.
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki labels the street story as a repeat of Episode 0815. A separately numbered broadcast edition remains a separate inventory record.

episodes.summaryEn: As the opening music plays at a much slower, sorrowful pace, David wonders out loud when everyone will return from New Mexico. He especially misses Maria, who at that point sneaks up on him and gives him a kiss, and the two have a happy reunion.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird wants to know what he's best at
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki labels the street story as a repeat of Episode 0816. A separately numbered broadcast edition remains a separate inventory record.

episodes.summaryEn: David sings "It's Your Body" to the kids.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird tries to run away
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Linda finds Big Bird crying in his nest. She uses a series of gestures to ask what's caused him to cry.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar plays water-related sounds (such as a dripping faucet, a thunderstorm, and crashing ocean waves) on his beat-up tape recorder as Maria and the kids guess what each sound is. He plays one final sound of Maria yelling at Oscar.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird stops by Hooper's Store and asks to have David's bottlecap and Olivia's coffee cup lid. He then asks Luis for the bike tire he's about to throw away, as well as the quarter he lent Bob yesterday.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird collects round objects; Oscar has termites
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird has a pretend tea party at his nest with his dolls, Emily and Dulcy. He wishes Mr. Snuffleupagus were present as well so it would be more fun, but he can't make it due to his tap dancing practice.

Maria hangs out on the stoop reading when Oscar yells at her to beat it. She tells him she has just as much a right to live how she wants as does Oscar, and gets an idea to switch roles so Oscar can experience what it's like to put up with someone like him on the block.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar has perfected his latest invention: the electric spoon, likening it to how an electric knife is used. He rallies Bob as a guinea pig and instructs him to try to eat a bowl of gravy (courtesy of Mr. Hooper) while using the device.

altLabels.labelEn: Linda takes care of the store
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob and Olivia notice a man inspecting the tree outside 123 Sesame Street. He introduces himself as Fowler Scowler, the city supervisor of sidewalks.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar is heading off on vacation to Chagrin Falls. He's renting out his trash can to a fellow named Osgood Wingate III, who responded to Oscar's newspaper ad.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: David, Maria, and Oscar the Grouch imagine how Gordon would look with various different hairstyles. In response, Gordon imagines them all shaved like him.

Olivia, Bob, Gordon, and Mr. Hooper are sitting on the steps of 123 Sesame Street when a dog (who would later be established as Barkley) approaches them. His tag features a name beginning with W, but the rest has worn off, so they try out some W names to call him over.

altLabels.labelEn: Woof Woof meets the residents of Sesame Street
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob sings "I'm Going Somewhere."

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Susan checks on her clock radio at the Fix-It Shop and finds Maria puzzled by a phonograph with a note attached to it. The note asks her to fix it so the machine plays music at the right speed, but the phonograph appears to be in perfect working order when she tests it.

Maria and David have plans to go to the movies tonight, but neither one remembers what time they agreed to meet up at. Maria leaves the Fix-It Shop to find him at Hooper's Store, where he's trying to call her at the shop.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird closes his eyes and identifies the sounds he hears. When David knocks on his door, Big Bird doesn't answer it.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird identifies sounds with his eyes closed
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Olivia and David discover Oscar is building a new high-rise apartment complex for Grouches - Grouch Towers, a stack of various trash cans centered around his own. He handles calls from potential tenants when Olivia points out that unless he's gotten permission from the city to build this structure, it'll have to be torn down.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar forms trashcan towers and singing groups
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Susan sings "Somebody Special."

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar tries to replace his trash can lid
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob, Big Bird, and the kids quiz Woof Woof on how many fingers they're holding up, and the dog answers in the correct number of barks. After the dog counts a few more things, Big Bird asks Bob if he thinks asking Woof Woof to count the tree is a good idea.

altLabels.labelEn: Woof Woof counts; Big Bird plays limbo
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: In the first light of the morning, David groggily makes his way to Hooper's Store. He tells the viewer his grandmother, Grace, is visiting and they spent half the night talking.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Count von Count is caught dancing to the opening theme music before inviting the viewer for a game: to count how many people say "hello" to them. Including himself, the Count counts eleven "hellos" from everybody: Susan and Gordon (exiting 123 Sesame Street), Bob and Linda (discussing their viewing of Close Encounters of the Third Kind), Mr. Hooper (returning to his store from a delivery), David and Olivia (the latter taking a photo of the former), Luis and Maria (working at the Fix-It Shop), and Big Bird (emerging from his nest).

altLabels.labelEn: The Count counts hellos and Barkley gets a name
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird brings Barkley up to Bob's apartment for a surprise visit. Bob is naturally opposed to the idea since Barkley isn't used to being there; he's proven right as Barkley leaps onto his couch with his dirty paws.

altLabels.labelEn: Bob and Big Bird try to train Barkley
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: At the crack of dawn, Olivia sings about how she's "Out with the Morning."

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: David tries to teach Barkley how to roll over, but Barkley doesn't seem to know how. David decides to get on all fours to demonstrate and Barkley mimics his movements.

altLabels.labelEn: David teaches Barkley to roll over
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Herry Monster comes across Olivia, with Honey and Snapper, looking after Mrs. Starbuck's newborn while she runs some errands. Herry reminisces to his youth and sings about what it was like being "Just a Little Baby."

altLabels.labelEn: Biff and Sully dig a subway tunnel
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird chats with Marlena, Jessica, John, and John in his nest, and observes how there may be more than one John in the world, but he's never met someone else named Big Bird. He spins a story for the kids about how he got his name...

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Linda tells Bob and the kids about a letter she received from her father about an upcoming family picnic. She signs about the last picnic they had and has the kids guess what occurred.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird wakes up early and excitedly tells the viewer that he's the first one awake on Sesame Street today. He loudly declares this to the rest of the block, only to be met with yells from surrounding neighbors telling him to keep quiet.

Big Bird and Mr. Snuffleupagus act out the story of "The Three Little Pigs," where Big Bird plays one of the pigs, while Snuffy plays the Big Bad Wolf. Snuffy huffs and puffs and causes a huge mess of Big Bird's nest.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird holds a lecture on the difference between heavy and light. He shows off some light items, including one of his feathers, a balloon, ping-pong balls, lettuce and paper airplanes.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar is upset that Gordon, Susan, Bob and the kids are picking up all the litter left by a windstorm. The Amazing Mumford believes he can help Oscar and magically litters the street again.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Luis shows Big Bird, Sharmaine, and Jeff how to tie a square knot using ropes, demonstrating "over," "under," and "through." Big Bird then asks how to untie a knot, having knotted himself up.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird waits for the sun
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bert wants to show off Brad's new baby tooth, but despite encouragement from his uncle, he won't open his mouth. Maria tries to make him smile and David tries to make him laugh, but he doesn't open up until Bert says that the matter is serious, prompting Brad to giggle.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon welcomes the viewer as he gets ready to go running. Sherlock Hemlock appears and deduces Gordon is waiting for a friend to go running with.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird takes a telephone message for Olivia
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob sings "Don't You Know You're Beautiful?" to a sad Georgie.

Oscar shows Bob and Susan his tape recorder, which he's used to record some of the "lovely" sounds of Sesame Street, including Gordon and Susan's car stalling, Cody crying, and Biff and Sully's jackhammering. He realizes that he also picked up some dialogue from Big Bird talking to Mr. Snuffleupagus.

altLabels.labelEn: The Count counts and sorts items at Hooper's Store
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Barkley hangs around Oscar's trash can, licking Oscar much to his dismay. He tries to pawn the dog onto Gordon, who is busy reading a book.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird prepares lunch for Luis
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird finds it odd when he sees Bob waving his hands while listening to music. Maria, David, and Linda explain that he's practicing conducting for a high school music performance tomorrow.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: The Polka Dot family (Percival, Petula, and baby Petulant) stroll through Sesame Street. The family, clothes and belongings are all covered in polka dots.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: After the oilman has visited Hooper's Store, he's accidentally left some oil on the sidewalk. Mr. Hooper is concerned about folks slipping on it and needs some sawdust to help clean it up.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird munches down on his bag of birdseed and has the feeling that today will be one full of surprises. He suddenly hears voices from above - it's Olivia, Bob, Mr. Hooper, and Luis, who summon him to the roof of 123 Sesame Street for a surprise...

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Olivia is minding after Hooper's Store while Mr. Hooper delivers groceries, when Bert approaches the counter to order a soda water. He'd like it flat, with no flavored syrup or ice cream in it.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon calls out different body parts which the kids then use to bounce a balloon.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Herry Monster watches Luis trying to fix a toy car at the Fix-it Shop. Luis asks Herry if he knows what's inside, and gives him permission to open it up and see.
Using some laundry soap boxes, Bob and Linda demonstrate the domino effect to Lloyd and Marika.

Big Bird has prepared his own lunch at Hooper's Store - a sandwich, carrot sticks and an apple. As he makes himself a glass of milk and other preparations, Barkley, resting under the window, rises up and gobbles up parts of the meal.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird stays at Gordon's in the rain
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria and Mr. Hooper watch as Barkley follows Cody everywhere. They notice he's been doing that all day and wonder why until they see that Cody has a snack in his hand and Barkley tries to sniff at and eat it.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Luis struggles learning a new song on the guitar, and the Amazing Mumford believes magic can help. First, he changes the sheet music to an easier song ("Row, Row, Row Your Boat"), then makes the guitar play a more complicated piece all on its own.

Business at the Fix-It Shop is particularly slow, with not one customer this morning. Luis offers to help Bob with his alarm clock and Gordon with his bicycle, but both men have other plans and don't need anything fixed right now.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar the Grouch advertises the new album Great Grouch Sounds, with such tracks as the sounds of drilling, explosions and babies crying. The album spawns one of Oscar's favorite noises - the sound of his neighbors complaining.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Buffy asks Big Bird to look after Cody for a few minutes. She also asks that they play some physical games so Cody can be nice and tired in time for his nap.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar has interest in becoming a photographer and asks Olivia for her professional opinion of his pictures. Despite the poor quality of the printing and unconventional subject matter (rusted cars and a trash basket, among others), Olivia thinks he has real potential, which discourages him from going professional.

Oscar counts the mismatched shoes in his collection one by one, tossing them onto the curb outside his trash can. Susan complains about the litter, but Oscar doesn't care, saying that it's the only way he can keep them separate and out of his pancake collection.
Maria is going on a two-day camping trip. The Count is present as she says goodbye to Bob and Olivia, then learns there are new things to count in the wilderness.

altLabels.labelEn: Maria and the Count go camping
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird and Cody pick pretend strawberries, while some girls play jump rope. Big Bird encourages Cody to jump with them, but he just scampers off.
Oscar asks Bob, who's waiting for Linda, to teach him some sign language so he can talk to Linda more effectively. He gets Bob to nonchalantly teach him the signs for "away" and "go."
Maria helps Oscar look through his delivery from the Miserable and Nasty department store. He opens the package and shows her his new set of pants, socks and shoes, which are all ratty and torn.
Gordon leads a hoedown in the yard for Susan, Buffy, Sheldon, and the kids.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird calls Mr. Hooper and the kids over to inform them of the new word he invented - "YO," used to describe the action of rubbing one's tummy and hopping up and down at the same time. Mr. Hooper points out the word already has a meaning - it's the Spanish word for "I."

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Herry Monster calls everyone over to witness a never-before-seen feat - he will lift a 4,000 ton weight! He struggles immensely to even move it, but with encouragement from his friends, Herry finds the strength to lift the weight.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar can't stand the cheery greeting Bob gives the viewer. He delivers his own, grouchy message to welcome them: "Goodbye!

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird meets new birds / Oscar's picnic
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: On a rainy day, a leak has developed at the front of the Fix-It Shop. Luis asks Big Bird to put something under the drops while he leaves to get some supplies.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Buffy is taking Cody over to the Day Care Center while she packs up to head back home. Big Bird learns that Maria is helping out there today and wants to help out as well.

altLabels.labelEn: Buffy and family head back home
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Mr. Hooper has many deliveries to make, but he loaned all his empty boxes to Big Bird and Grover. Over at Big Bird's nest, the two have made a building from the boxes, but can't agree whether to call it "Big Bird's Barber Shop" or "Grover's Garage."

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: David observes that Hooper's Store could use some painting. Mr. Hooper, who claims that the store hasn't had a paint job for 35 years, approves the idea but feels too tired to spend his time painting.

As everyone mingles around Sesame Street, Grover is surprised to see the viewer as he hums to the "Sesame Street Theme." He realizes that nobody else has seen them, so he asks the viewer to hide until he tells them to come out.

altLabels.labelEn: Mr. Hooper celebrates the 25th anniversary of his store
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

He is about to dispose of it when he comes up with a better idea: he puts it on his specials board, thinking someone will take it off his hands.

episodes.summaryEn: During the "Sesame Street Theme" (mixed with a whistling march), the cast (Bob, Gordon, Susan, Mr. Hooper, Big Bird, Denise, and Anthony, carrying Oscar's trash can) appears hiking through the woods.

episodes.summaryEn: In the early hours of the morning, Luis strolls over to the Fix-It Shop and discovers that the door is already unlocked. He hears some sounds coming from within and suspects a robber is in the store, and leaves to call the police.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki labels the street story as a repeat of Episode 0964. A separately numbered broadcast edition remains a separate inventory record.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird introduces Mr. Snuffleupagus, who is about to do something really great. Offscreen Snuffy isn't too sure he can perform as he's never done what he's about to do.

altLabels.labelEn: Mr. Snuffleupagus tries to ride on a gigantic skateboard
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki labels the street story as a repeat of Episode 1015. A separately numbered broadcast edition remains a separate inventory record.

episodes.summaryEn: Grover wants to show the viewer what it's like when someone is angry by getting angry himself, but has a hard time conjuring up such an emotion. He asks Big Bird to get him mad, but Big Bird can't bring himself to do it.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki labels the street story as a repeat of Episode 1011. A separately numbered broadcast edition remains a separate inventory record.

episodes.summaryEn: Maria and David wait for Big Bird on a subway platform, having already missed two trains because of his tardiness. Big Bird finally arrives, unable to find much of his beach accoutrements for their trip.

altLabels.labelEn: Maria, David and Big Bird go to City Island
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki labels the street story as a repeat of Episode 0946. A separately numbered broadcast edition remains a separate inventory record.

episodes.summaryEn: It's twilight on Sesame Street. Luis fills a large barrel with water to rinse it out, while Mr. Hooper brings out a bowl of water to wipe down the outdoor tables.

altLabels.labelEn: Mr. Hooper and Maria go out for the evening
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki labels the street story as a repeat of Episode 0938. A separately numbered broadcast edition remains a separate inventory record.

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar heckles Gordon and Susan's plans to make a garden on the street. When they challenge his knowledge of plants, he shows off a plant he's growing - a crabapple tree, though it droopy from having been in his fridge the entire time.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki labels the street story as a repeat of Episode 0997. A separately numbered broadcast edition remains a separate inventory record.

episodes.summaryEn: The Count has gotten up very early to count people as they start their day on the street. He finds he's gotten up a little too early and nobody is awake.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki labels the street story as a repeat of Episode 1000. A separately numbered broadcast edition remains a separate inventory record.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird tries to get Mr. Hooper, David and Susan to play with him, but they're all too busy. Big Bird mopes and tells Olivia he feels like a nobody.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: It's a chilly morning on Sesame Street and Maria freezes as she waits for David. Oscar, looking to start an argument, acts like it's hot.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird stands at the bus stop holding a package and some flowers. He tells Luis that he's going to the post office, then visiting a sick friend in the hospital.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar tries out for a mudball team
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob, Maria, Olivia and Mr. Hooper wait for Linda and her friends from the Little Theatre of the Deaf to arrive back from a trip to Andy's (Linda's father) farm. As they head toward the bus stop, they witness Alphabet Bates making a letter "U" overhead .

altLabels.labelEn: The Little Theatre of the Deaf acts out life on the farm
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria shows the kids how intelligent Barkley is by calling out different letters of the alphabet; Barkley then points each one out on a large board near Oscar's trash can. Oscar isn't as impressed: "If he wasn't a dog, nobody'd care!"

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar wakes up at the crack of dawn and sees Barkley scampering about Sesame Street. The Grouch decides to cause some mischief and starts barking, hoping everyone will think it's Barkley and get him in trouble.

Oscar the Grouch pulls up on the block in his new taxi, which is a ratty-looking cab that is falling apart at the seams. Gordon points out that nobody in their right mind would want a ride in his taxi - exactly what Oscar hopes.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon greets Big Bird as he heads over to Hooper's Store for breakfast, looking forward to not having to make it himself for once. Nobody appears to be around, until he hears a voice from behind the counter.

Oscar asks why Gordon, Maria, Olivia, and Luis are wearing funny clothing: "What is this, a masquerade from a rummage sale?" The cast explains they're wearing jogging outfits to go for a jog through the park.
David and the kids find Oscar watching the skies with his spyglass. He's hired Alphabet Bates to write one of his favorite letters in the sky - U, for such words as unhappy, uncouth, unfair...

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar peers from his trash can at the usual business going about on Sesame Street: the kids cheerfully walk by before coloring on the sidewalk, David and Susan greet each other warmly, Bob finds a discarded brick and throws it away, and Linda returns from a run from the park before joining everybody in Hooper's Store for some breakfast. Oscar can't stand all the bright attitudes today and wishes everyone could be a Grouch like him, and begins to imagine what that would be like...

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird welcomes the viewer and tells them about being a baby and how he used to be fed as one. He then introduces a film about it...

altLabels.labelEn: Telly Monster moves to Sesame Street
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Mr. Ortiz pays a visit to the street, having just bought some paint from a nearby store. He mentions that he's painting his apartment today and everyone jumps at the chance to help out.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon and Susan see the new trashman Bruno carrying Oscar's trash can down the block. Bruno jogs up toward them, panting.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird wants to be an animal trainer
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird sits with Linda in the yard. While she reads, he puts on the radio, knowing it won't disturb her because she's deaf.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird is grooving to his "Rubber Duckie" disco record when Snuffy asks what disco is. Big Bird explains that a disco is a fun place filled with music and dancing.

altLabels.labelEn: Herry goes to the eye doctor
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maurice Monster is puzzled by the nursery rhyme in his book. Bob points out that he's reading each sentence backwards, from right to left, and shows him how to do it the correct way.

altLabels.labelEn: Hooper's Store is used for an on-location movie shoot
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: David anxiously waits at the bus stop for his Grandma Grace who is visiting today. When the bus finally arrives, Mr. Macintosh steps out and tells him he hasn't seen her; he was the only passenger.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Source writes March 14. 1979; period treated as date punctuation, preserving source wording in airDateAsPublished.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird watches as Linda and the kids put together the word "FUN." Once the word is fully formed, everybody has some fun!

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar the Grouch plays a Spanish record for Luis. The track, "Cielito Lindo," features the singers going "Ay, yi, yi, yi!"
Gordon, Big Bird and the kids play Blind Man's Bluff, with Gordon being blindfolded. Mr. Snuffleupagus stops by on his way to his Granny's house for tea and joins the game.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird recites a poem to the kids about his age, "I Am Six."
Big Bird is about to address the viewer on a subject, but he can't remember what it is. He tries retracing his steps (which includes cueing the opening music up again) to no avail.
At Hooper's Store, Timi, David, Maria and Linda have lunch. Timi asks for the salt, pepper and sugar, which are on Linda's side of the counter.

altLabels.labelEn: Weather signs with Timi and Linda
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: In Big Bird's nest area, Big Bird, Mr. Snuffleupagus and the kids dance to a Johnny Carson-style version of the "Sesame Street Theme." Big Bird encourages Snuffy to dance closer to them, but Snuffy claims that he is much too shy to dance in front of other people.

Mr. Hooper alerts everyone that the President of the United States is going to be detouring through Sesame Street today. While everyone cleans up the messy street, Big Bird decides to write a poem for the President.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki labels the street story as a repeat of Episode 1044. A separately numbered broadcast edition remains a separate inventory record.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird finds Snuffy in his nest area, having just come back from his singing lesson. When Snuffy doubts that he's a good singer, Big Bird encourages him to demonstrate.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki labels the street story as a repeat of Episode 0999. A separately numbered broadcast edition remains a separate inventory record.

episodes.summaryEn: Maria, Luis, and Olivia follow a strange noise to Oscar's trash can, where inside Oscar and his Grouch pals are chopping up his piano to use as firewood. Mr. Hooper comes by to drop off marshmallows, but realizes how dangerous it can be to light a fire inside a trash can.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird wears costumes to pose for pictures.
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki labels the street story as a repeat of Episode 1053. A separately numbered broadcast edition remains a separate inventory record.

episodes.summaryEn: Luis finds Oscar using an old CB radio, which Oscar has repurposed as a GB radio (GB for Grouch Band). Using the nickname "Bum Steer," he communicates with fellow Grouch "Rotten Egg" about trading some trash.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki labels the street story as a repeat of Episode 0974. A separately numbered broadcast edition remains a separate inventory record.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird, Bob, Gordon, and Susan find that Hooper's Store is closed. Inside, they spot Mr. Hooper in an oversized gown and mortarboard practicing a speech.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki labels the street story as a repeat of Episode 1025. A separately numbered broadcast edition remains a separate inventory record.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird gathers the kids together in the yard. He's in need of four kids of the same height, so he and Maria have them line up to compare sizes.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob and Susan find "5" signs posted all over the street. This is the work of the Count, who has officially declared 5 as his favorite number.
Maria watches after a Muppet canary for a friend of hers. Big Bird hears her speaking Spanish to it, since her friend also speaks Spanish and Maria feels it would make the bird more comfortable.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Buffy and her family have arrived from Hawaii for a visit, having got in late the previous day. Nobody else knows they're here, and she and Cody sneak into Big Bird's nest where Big Bird is dozing.

altLabels.labelEn: Buffy and her family surprise everyone
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: As rousing march music plays, Oscar calls out for his neighbors to see "the creepiest, crawliest show on Earth!" David, Olivia, Mr. Hooper, and the kids gather around Oscar's trash can as Slimey the Great makes his entrance from a miniature circus tent.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird clotheslines into his doorframe for the umpteenth time as he exits his nest area. He attributes this to his height, and starts wondering what it would be like to be as small as the viewer.
After doing some cleaning in the basement of 123 Sesame Street, Gordon goes over to the garage to clean there as well. Mr. Hooper, Bob, and Olivia follow, having also stored some items inside.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon and Susan draw outlines of Lisa, Frankie, and Louie on giant pieces of paper in the yard. Luis comes by and tries identifying whose outline belongs to who, though he slightly feigns ignorance in guessing whose outline is eight feet tall.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird roller skates around the street to a carnival rendition of the "Sesame Street Theme," dubbing himself "a regular Dorothy Camel." Attempting to show off a trick for the kids, he spins and takes a fall in the yard.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: On the roof of 123 Sesame Street, Buffy, David, Gordon and Luis are doing some exercises. Suddenly, some thunder blares and they try to go inside, but David discovers the door is locked.

altLabels.labelEn: The adults get locked on the roof
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Olivia sings "Imagining."

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: The Count pulls up on Sesame Street in his Countmobile and notices Luis working on an iron at the Fix-It Shop. This inspires the Count to count jobs people have.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria leads everyone in the "Exercise Song."

Big Bird and Mr. Snuffleupagus pretend to play "Goldilocks and the Three Bears," with Big Bird as the bear family and Snuffy as Goldilocks (wearing his Shirley Temple wig). As Big Bird goes out to simulate the bears walking in the woods, Snuffy-locks tries out all three different-sized chairs, which all break under his weight.

Susan strolls over to Hooper's Store, where Olivia, Buffy, Sheldon, and even Cody are cooperating to make breakfast. Susan wonders how she can help out, and is pleased when Olivia suggests she can help eat breakfast...

altLabels.labelEn: Buffy misses Big Bird's tea party
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird is bored with the unexciting life of a bird and wishes to be some other kind of animal. He bumps into Gladys the Cow and decides he'll be like her.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird doesn't want to be a bird
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: David strolls through a rainstorm, singing about having some "Sunshine on a Rainy Day."

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria and the kids play with a ball, which gets stuck on top of the arbor outside Hooper's Store. Before Maria can go get a ladder, Super Grover lands on the scene (or in the trash basket, rather).

altLabels.labelEn: Super Grover rescues a ball / Bert's rooftop pigeon coop
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: In the twilight of the morning, Big Bird gets up early to show the viewers about before and after. He accomplishes this by feeding Barkley his breakfast, putting on his scarf, and listening for the sound of Oscar the Grouch's noisy alarm clock.

Grandma Grace is visiting the street again, having dinner at Gordon and Susan's apartment with Susan, David, Linda, Big Bird, and the kids (who are playing with a Lite-Brite). Suddenly, the power goes out.

altLabels.labelEn: Grandma Grace visits during a blackout
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: As Maria and Buffy sit down for a healthy snack in the yard, Luis brings Barkley over to them to show off the new trick he's taught him - subtraction. He places three dog biscuits down and commands Barkley to not only subtract one at a time, but count (in barks) how many are left.
When Oscar finds himself saying nice things to people, he starts singing about a happy feeling that's creeping into him — the "Happy Blues."
David hears Bob, Susan, and the kids singing and banging pots outside. He calls for a drum beat and plays a musical game where they bang their pots the number of times he calls for.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar feels today is a good day for an argument and tries roping Bob, Olivia, David and Maria into arguing with him. They all turn him down, however.
David guesses from the clues that Big Bird is opening a lemonade stand. He offers to be Big Bird's first customer, but there's one problem - Big Bird doesn't know how to make lemonade.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: At the crack of day, the Count starts his day by counting the various residents stretching and yawning. He then counts the people yelling at Oscar the Grouch for playing his bugle loudly.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird and Snuffy play Little Red Riding Hood
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: While chatting with Mr. Hooper about feelings, Cookie Monster describes the many ways he would feel upon receiving a box of cookies - happy, sad, surprise, anger and scared. After providing him a box, Mr. Hooper reminds Cookie of one last emotion - proud, which he feels when he shares the cookies with his friends.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird sings "If I Could Fly."
The Count beats a large bass drum and counts the beats. Luis comes out of the Fix-It Shop and complains about the noise and constant counting.
Big Bird has finished painting a chair, along with a WET PAINT sign to go with it. He then realizes that the paint on the WET PAINT sign is also wet, so he makes another WET PAINT sign for it.

Linda compliments Bob's V-neck sweater, and she, Bob, Allison, and Randy think of different ways they can make the letter V using their bodies. Big Bird comes along and shows how he can make a V using his beak (swallowing a fly in the process).
Fred the Wonder Horse has received a baby cactus and a card as a birthday gift from his friends back at the O.K. Corral.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird has decided to go camping, and shows the viewer his train of equipment: the tent, a barbecue, and a bag of miscellaneous essentials (including a beakbrush, top hat, dancing shoes, and moose call). He reveals that with Gordon's permission, he will be camping up on the roof of 123 Sesame Street, and starts heading upstairs.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Luis calls Barkley over to play a game with him, Patrick, Becky, and Denise. They imagine doing various physical movements - first crawling through a pretend tunnel, then crossing over an imaginary narrow bridge, and leaping over a stream.
Gladys the Cow livens up Luis' dull lecture about milk with a glitzy musical number about it. This scene would be used as an opening insert in future episodes.
Mr. Hooper blends the word PET and Barkley jumps on him. Maria assumes a safe spot away from Oscar's trash can to blend the word WET.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Olivia comes up on the roof of 123 Sesame Street, where Bert is distraught. One of the pigeons, Bernard, isn't being his usual, active self.

altLabels.labelEn: Prince Charming looks for a princess
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Olivia introduces everyone to her friends, Maurice and Gregory Hines. Maurice claims to have taught his younger brother everything he knows.

altLabels.labelEn: A visit from the Hines brothers
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon wants to clean up the apartment before Susan gets back from work. Big Bird offers to help, but then walks out of the room.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria and the kids notice a crosswalk sign positioned by Oscar's trash can. She teaches the kids to read the "WALK" sign, then waits for it to change to "DON'T WALK."

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird, Bob, David, Linda, Gordon and Susan bid Maria and Olivia farewell as they board the bus to the airport. Once the bus is out of sight, they happily grab their own luggage and prepare to follow them -- all except for Gordon, who isn't going with them.

altLabels.labelEn: Trip to Puerto Rico — Maria's birthday
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: On a sunny morning in Puerto Rico, Maria comes out onto the porch. She spots David across the way from his residence in the country and invites him and the others over for breakfast with the family.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar and Osvaldo are going to go "trashing," but because his push cart is "Grouch-powered," one of them must be responsible for pushing it. They argue over who will push and who will look out for trash, and eventually agree to take turns.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar and Osvaldo float on a Grouch raft (still in their trashcans) toward the dock on a nearby island of the coast of Puerto Rico. The two crawl to the edge of the dock and are pleased to find some peace and quiet away from all their happy acquaintances.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Everyone is setting up for a festival in the town square today. Big Bird offers his services to Luis, who is installing some speakers.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria and friends bid farewell to her family as they board their bus back to the airport. Oscar and Osvaldo also part ways, causing Oscar to miss the bus.

altLabels.labelEn: Trip to Puerto Rico — The return home
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar enjoys the freezing weather on Sesame Street today; he's so cheerful that he sings "Oh, What a Beautiful Mornin'" to himself. Maria comes outside and Oscar has her try to guess why he enjoys the cold while everyone else is miserable: everyone else stays inside to keep warm, meaning that he can be left alone.

altLabels.labelEn: A freezing cold day on Sesame Street
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: David can't find the key to open Hooper's Store and becomes very angry. He angrily tells Big Bird to leave him alone.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Linda demonstrates signs for various modes of transportation for Gordon and the kids.

altLabels.labelEn: Preparing for a visit from Osvaldo
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar pulls up to Sesame Street in the Sloppy Jalopy, with Osvaldo, el Gruñón in the back seat, here for a visit from Puerto Rico. As the two Grouches bicker about Oscar charging a cab fare for the ride, Maria comments, "Ah, friendship."

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird feels as though there's nothing to do today. David suggests he play "The Alphabet Game" by finding each letter of the alphabet in signs around the area.
David comes across Oscar showing Slimey and his worm girlfriend Clammy how to dance to some disco music. David can't tell the two worms apart, as both have orange and yellow stripes.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar, dressed in a turban and armed with a pipe, calls out for people to see him and Slimey perform the Grouch Indian Worm trick; he claims it's two tricks in one. All they need is a shoelace, which Luis reluctantly provides after some goading from the kids.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird and Snuffy go camping
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: On the roof of 123 Sesame Street, Bob and Jessica see Alphabet Bates parachute down from his airplane. He draws onscreen the letter he was going to write in the sky - the letter O.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird shares his nap with Barkley.
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird notices that his bean bag always drops straight to the ground, never going in any other direction when he lets go. He tries this out on other items around his nest and believes he's onto a scientific discovery.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Mr. Macintosh parks his fruit cart on the block and sings "A Singy Kind of Song."
David has made a board to use outside Hooper's Store to advertise the specialty items each day. As he carries it to the store, the "E" in "HOOPER'S LUNCH" falls off, unbeknownst to David.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: David is on the ledge outside Bob's apartment above Hooper's Store (secured to the windows). He's caulking the windows to keep in heat and keep out the rain.

Maria sets up a telescope in front of 123 Sesame Street and explains to Big Bird what it's used for. Big Bird looks through it and is amazed that he can see the buildings from further down the street.
Bob and Big Bird prepare to make a bookcase together. Big Bird has brought a box of Band-Aids for the job, citing how clumsy Bob can be.

Big Bird shows "close to" by calling Barkley over. He then tries to demonstrate "away from" by putting distance between himself and Barkley, but the dog would much rather be close to his feathered friend and follows him.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird has some items set out in the yard divided by a grid: a bench, a stool, a chair, and a shopping cart. He sings "Three of These Things" and asks the kids to find which one doesn't belong.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: David attempts to get Barkley to follow several commands, but fails. He vents his frustration to Linda, who has much better luck when she gives Barkley the commands in sign language.
Gordon witnesses Oscar's scientific creation - Charles, a grouch robot. The robot is able to tell Gordon to "get lost," then turn himself into a heap of trash by falling apart.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird goes to the doctor
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria frets to David, Bob, Big Bird, and Olivia that because she's been so busy at the Fix-It Shop, she hasn't had time to prepare dinner for Buffy and her family, who are scheduled to arrive this afternoon at the airport. Everyone agrees to help Maria by bringing something different to the dinner.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Buffy leaves Cody in Gordon's care while she runs some errands. He and Cody head over to the yard to do some finger painting, which Gordon explains doesn't have to be messy.
Big Bird makes an interesting discovery - when he stands up, his lap disappears. He asks Buffy why this is and before she can answer, he asks several more questions ("Why does a dog have four legs?

altLabels.labelEn: Show and tell at day care
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Olivia takes some action shots of Barkley in the yard when Big Bird comes by with his own camera. He wishes to be a photographer just like her someday, and tries to take some pictures of Olivia.
David feels hungry and makes himself a nice, big sandwich at Hooper's Store. After he sets it out, Maria comes by and starts snacking on it, being very hungry herself.

As a steel drum band plays, the citizens of Sesame Street set up various booths, hang decorations and balloons, and prepare all kinds of foods. Oscar wants to know what all the commotion is outside; it turns out that today they're having a street fair and is told by Olivia and Buffy that there's nothing he can do to stop the festivities.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: As Cody sits in Big Bird's nest, Buffy talks to him about how some people don't know a lot of Cree words. She then sings "Heya Nikosis" to him.
Luis and Olivia stop by Hooper's Store, where David reveals his new assistant: Cody! With help from David, Cody serves the customers and puts the money into the cash register.

Big Bird is feeling lonely today and asks some of the grown-ups to hang out, but they're all too busy. He heads back to his nest, as Buffy, David and Olivia all decide to spend some time with him after all.

Maria, Olivia, and Luis observe the Double Dutch Jump Rope Dancers demonstrating their skills on Sesame Street. Luis has never heard of double dutch, while Olivia claims to be "the queen" of it when she was younger.
Count von Count celebrates a moment he's been waiting a long time for - Cody has turned three years old, which means he's able to count all the way up to 20.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird gets Snuffy a watch
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Buffy and Fred the Wonder Horse sing "Jig Along Home."

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria can't remember where she put the book she borrowed from the library this morning.
Oscar is in the midst of his annual "mess-up time," where he spends the day redecorating his trash can with new dust and grime. "It's hard to keep a respectable place messy," he states.
Big Bird and Cody visit Hooper's Store, where David is dusting the shelves. He's saved the hardest parts for last - the top and bottom shelves, which aren't easy to reach for someone his size.

Big Bird witnesses as David and Bob have an argument. They can't agree on where the new trash basket should go: Bob thinks it should go in front of Hooper's Store, while David thinks it should be closer to the door that leads to Bob's apartment.
Big Bird attaches signs reading "Front" and "Back" to Mr. Snuffleupagus' front and back to help him remember which is which. However, he's unable to see either sign.
Maria, Luis, and David set up the yard for Olivia's surprise birthday party. They run home to change and wrap gifts, while Count von Count volunteers to hang around and put the candles on her cake.

Maria shows David the fresh flowers she just picked, and David discusses how well he's doing in law school; Bob joins in the conversation with news of his new shirt. They happen to be situated in front of Oscar's trash can, and of course Oscar can't stand it and demands that everybody knock off the friendly chatter.
Gordon goes down to the basement laundry room of 123 Sesame Street. He thinks Olivia has come to help him, but she's just on her way downtown to develop some photos.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Biff gets some work done in front of 123 Sesame Street, but feels thirsty. Maria, who is waiting for an important piece of mail to come, suggests he goes to Hooper's Store for lemonade.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar comes up with a game for Gordon and the kids to play, where they act like they're different types of food such as prune Jell-O, melted cheese, and popcorn. Gordon pulls one over on Oscar by pretending to be chewing gum and "sticking" to Oscar when they shake hands.
Linda paces back and forth on the block in a huff. Mr. Hooper and Olivia watch, as he explains that Bob was supposed to meet Linda a half hour ago and hasn't shown up yet.

Big Bird comes across Luis and Olivia preparing a cake and present (a new bowtie) for Mr. Hooper's birthday in the yard. Big Bird can hardly contain his excitement, but the others shush him and ask him not to spoil the surprise.
Big Bird once again has trouble remembering Mr. Hooper's name. He thinks it would be easier if everyone had the same name and imagines a world where everyone shares his name.
Bob and Oscar the Grouch sing "I Love When It Rains."

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar hosts a show on WORM-TV
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird sees the adults all moving various items into the garage. He asks questions about what's going on and learns they're having a garage sale today to raise money to plant new trees in the neighborhood.

altLabels.labelEn: A garage sale on Sesame Street
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird asks Maria to hold some flowers while he draws a picture in the yard. Maria assumes she's being drawn as well as Big Bird describes adding long eyelashes and a big smile, but becomes offended when he starts referring to a long nose and shaggy hair.
Big Bird wakes from his nap and catches a whiff of smoke. He guesses there must be a barbecue in the area, then hears the sounds of a siren.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: In their apartment, Gordon and Susan go over a list of chores that they have to do today. They decide that the best way to get through them is to cooperate.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar's Spanish sign / Elmo and the letter H
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: At the Day Care Center, Maria and Bob supervise as the kids make drawings. Judy has made a picture of Sesame Street covered in trash, which is a gift for Oscar the Grouch.

David and his grandmother Grace surprise Mr. Hooper at the store. Mr. Hooper has a problem - the person originally in charge of bringing sandwiches to the Day Care Center had to cancel and Mr. Hooper agreed to fill in.

altLabels.labelEn: Mr. Hooper and David's grandmother go to the senior citizens' dance
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird mopes that there's nothing to do since a lot of the kids are in school and there's nobody to play with. Maria encourages him to play using his imagination before she heads to the supermarket.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird brings the mail to Hooper's Store and Mr. Hooper proceeds to read a postcard from his friend Harry who's vacationing at the beach. Big Bird encourages Mr. Hooper to imagine himself on a beach since he can't really go and leave the store alone.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird introduces Linda, who will show how to sign the numbers 1, 2 and 3 with the kids. Big Bird doesn't grasp that simply holding up the number of fingers per value is also the sign language way of showing them.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon and the kids think of S words. Oscar gives them one more - "Silence!"

Big Bird sits at Hooper's Store coloring as Mr. Hooper and Maria wish Kathy a good day at school. Big Bird feels a bit left out that he's not old enough to go to school like the other kids, but Kathy says it's visitors' day and he can come along.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: This is the first season premiere to not be sponsored by the number 2.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird finds no one but him is around on the street to welcome the viewer. In song, he counts himself and soon finds he's joined by 19 more friends, making a total of 20 to say hello!

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Ringmaster Big Bird presents his acts to a crowd of Olivia, Mr. Hooper and Luis. Daredevils Frankie, James and David walk across the tightrope without using a net (though he urges the crowd to imagine it's actually up in the air).

altLabels.labelEn: Telly and Max have a problem
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird has brought his Bird Book to the Fix-It Shop to figure out what kind of bird Poco Loco is. He's not a hummingbird, flamingo, or pelican, but he does resemble the "silly parrot" in the book.

Big Bird introduces Linda, who has just returned from touring Japan with the National Theatre of the Deaf. She signs two different haikus, and teaches everyone how to sign "thank you" in Japanese sign language.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird asks Maria, Luis, Gordon and Olivia to hold some random items as he fetches others. Maria figures out that all the items are circus-related.

altLabels.labelEn: P. T. Bunkum looks for an act
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar wonders what he should have for lunch, but ultimately thinks it doesn't matter what he eats. This prompts Gilbert and Sullivan to explain the importance of a healthy diet with a street-wide song about foods ("You Are What You Eat").
Luis welcomes the viewer as he opens the Fix-It Shop for the day. Poco Loco already knows the topics for today - the letters Y and W and "surprise," though he's not sure what the latter means.

Gordon and Susan make their way to Big Bird's nest for a pretend tea party and assume Big Bird's imaginary friend, Mr. Snuffleupagus, will be there too. At the party, they address the empty seat as Snuffy and pretend to give him some tea, though Big Bird is left wondering who they're talking to.

altLabels.labelEn: Gordon and Susan pretend to have tea with Snuffy
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Luis and the kids come across Dr. Nobel Price's latest, concealed invention: the string-winder. Dr. Price describes it for them - it has three wheels, two pedals and handlebars.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Susan tries to read a magazine, but is bothered by Oscar's TV watching. Before long, Susan gets distracted by Oscar's show (a complicated soap opera called Love of Grouch), and Oscar shows interest in an article from Susan's magazine about recycling trash.

Mr. Hooper welcomes the viewer, and is about to explain the word "closed" when Big Bird interrupts him. Big Bird assumes Mr. Hooper is going to talk about the letter L, the alphabet, and rectangles, all of which have to do with the sign on the front door of his store -- but Big Bird can't see the word "closed" until Mr. Hooper points it out.
Olivia sings "Takes a Little Time" to Deena, who impatiently wants her sunflower to grow faster.
Big Bird is upset about being unable to fly. Poco Loco suggests he could flap his wings hard like he does, but that doesn't work.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird wonders where all his friends are on this beautiful sunny day. He asks Barkley where everyone is, and Barkley appears to give him some clues as to what Olivia, Mr. Hooper, and Luis are doing.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird can't stand the mess his nest area is after bumping into various things and knocking over his table. Susan suggests he throw out items he no longer needs, but Big Bird comes up with a reason for keeping everything (old pots for Cody to bang on, a broken hose that Mr. Snuffleupagus uses for a straw, etc.)

Susan and Mr. Hooper discuss how it's Big Bird's turn to feed Barkley; Mr. Hooper is concerned, but Susan reassures him that Big Bird has planned for it. Over at his nest, Big Bird feels as though he's forgotten something.

Big Bird dons a cape and pretends he's "Superbird!" He roams the street looking for dangerous situations to be the hero of, but only does menial tasks such as holding the door open for Susan and watching Willy's hot dog cart.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird gets a superhero outfit in the mail / Telly and the Bus Stop sign
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar is startled to see the viewer: "I thought you were over in Mister Rogers' Neighborhood!"
