He lets the viewer in on a trick he's about to pull on Olivia: he has an ordinary pitcher of regular grape juice, but the glass he has is full of holes. Olivia suspects something is up and correctly discovers the glass is rigged.
Big Bird introduces Luis, Linda and Bob, who show different emotions in their own languages.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar the Grouch greets the viewer very early in the morning and explains that it's his favorite time of day because no one else is awake yet to ask him to play games or sing songs. He revels in the sound of a passing garbage truck, but cringes at the tweets of birds waking up... which makes him grouchy.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird watches Mr. Snuffleupagus take his morning jog through Sesame Street, somehow avoiding the view of all the other adults up at the hour.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Deena wants to play with Barkley (or "Big Bow-Wow" as she calls him), who is currently resting next to 123 Sesame Street. She wakes him up and assumes his growling means he's pretending to be a ferocious lion.
episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: The music played during the limbo game in scene 2 was originally used for part of the extended opening of Episode 1316.

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar asks Susan why he's not feeling so well, especially in his stomach. She learns he hasn't eaten anything all day and recommends having a meal.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: In addition to performing Barkley, Brian Muehl voices Deena's pull-string doll.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird welcomes the viewer, telling them that Granny Bird's birthday is next week and he has a gift to mail her. He asks Gordon to help wrap it, until it's revealed the gift is a live goldfish.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Mr. Macintosh has to go downtown, but needs someone to look after his produce cart. After seeing that everyone on the street is busy, Big Bird volunteers, although he has no idea what he's supposed to do.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird watches Mr. Macintosh's cart
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria wants to go for a walk and invites Telly Monster to join her. As dramatic soap opera-type organ music plays, Telly notices the clouds overhead and thinks rain might occur.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird introduces today's letters, but isn't sure what the number is. Luckily, he and the kids use the Number of the Day Machine to find out.
Countess Dahling von Dahling arrives on Sesame Street with Masha, her dog. Gordon is reluctant to let her count him and the kids, citing the rain that always occurs when she finishes.
episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: The original script for the episode called for the Countess to arrive in a modified version of the Countmobile, which would be referred to as "the Countessmobile."

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird looks over the doors of his nest and welcomes the viewer. He talks to the birds and wishes everyone a nice day as he leaves to do his exercises, humming, "Oh, it's a beautiful day in my neighborhood..."

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar performs "The Loudest Soft Shoe in the World."

Oscar recites a tone poem to Luis and Olivia, "Ode to the City." The poem describes the various noises he enjoys, which he plays on a record. It soon becomes a cacophony of noise that drives the grown-ups away.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Mr. Hooper gives Olivia four dollars to take a cab so she doesn't have to carry a heavy crate, despite her claiming she only needs to go two blocks. She calls for a taxi anyhow and Oscar pulls up in the Sloppy Jalopy.

altLabels.labelEn: Olivia tries to take a cab
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: It's nighttime on Sesame Street, and Telly Monster's latest worry is that it will stay dark forever and the sun won't rise again. Gordon acknowledges how silly this is and tries to reassure him, but Big Bird easily falls for the paranoia as well.

altLabels.labelEn: Telly thinks the night will never end
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: In addition to performing their characters, Karen Prell and Brian Muehl can be heard as some of the neighbors complaining during Oscar's party. Muppet Wiki note: Telly's pupils have turned into red spirals for the final scene, hearkening back to his origin as "the Television Monster."

episodes.summaryEn: Linda acts out different emotions for Bob and the kids to guess, then has everybody learn the signs. Oscar interrupts and tells them he finds the game too noisy and wants everybody to scram, which makes Linda furiously begin to sign back at him.

Telly Monster makes his way to Hooper's Store for some breakfast, but notices a "CLOSED" sign in the doorway. He takes this to mean that Mr. Hooper is closing the store forever, which means nobody will get any breakfast ever again and that Mr. Hooper is out of a job.

altLabels.labelEn: Telly thinks Hooper's has closed for good
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Olivia makes her way to the roof of 123 Sesame Street, which is full of various plants. She hears Big Bird talking to somebody nearby, but can't see who; based on the clues she assumes it's Mr. Snuffleupagus.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird sings about "Wheels on My Feet" while roller skating down the street.

altLabels.labelEn: An evening with Howlie the Owl
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Telly Monster is building a castle of blocks in the yard, but he's afraid to put the last one on for fear that it will fall. Gordon approaches and asks if he can help, and together they sing "Lending a Helping Hand."

Bob returns from his concert tour and Big Bird reports he did a good job watching his apartment while Bob was gone, with some help from Mr. Snuffleupagus. They arrive at Bob's place to find everything is missing.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar has assembled an audience of Gordon, Susan and the kids to judge his "Oscar the Grouch Look-a-Like Contest." Three Grouches, including Osvaldo, el Gruñón, are assembled and they compare how they look to Oscar. Osvaldo resembles Oscar the most, so the judges suggest he be the winner.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Additional performers include Karen Prell (Grouch #2), with Brian Muehl (Grouch #1).

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird, Olivia, and the kids flip through her series of photos and identify the different jobs the subjects are doing in each one (shown on-screen in a close-up). After seeing a painter, teacher, vet, and barber, Big Bird reveals a picture he took of someone else at their job: Olivia, the photographer.
Bob discusses the things that people can do with their fingers, and sings "Five Fingers" to the kids.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird and friends make a clubhouse
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: David's grandma Grace is back visiting Sesame Street, and Big Bird watches as she puts Celia's hair in cornrows. He learns about how the style had started in Africa, and is a tradition that has been passed down through history for about 3,000 years.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Linda greets the viewer, saying, "Hi, welcome to Sesame Street," in sign language. Bob joins her and the two show how to do the signs, with Bob explaining how Linda isn't able to hear the words he's saying.
episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Grouch performers include Michael Earl (purple and light green) and Brian Muehl (red).

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar has entered Slimey in a "Special Pet" contest and asks Susan to talk with the judge when he arrives, since Oscar isn't one for pleasantries. The Muppet judge (Brian Muehl) finds, however, that Slimey isn't all that special when compared to other animals, even after Susan pleads his case.

altLabels.labelEn: Gordon and Susan attend a Grouch movie
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Telly Monster is supposed to introduce today's number, but has forgotten what it is. Big Bird brings in his "Number of the Day Machine" to help, but Telly is certain he'll break it somehow.
In the premiere edition of Ask Oscar, Telly Monster reads a letter from Yucchina Blechman of Sandusty, Ohio, who wishes to know about on and in. Oscar thinks Telly should help with the demonstration.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird has purchased a cabbage from Hooper's Store and drags his wagon of things to meet Mr. Snuffleupagus at Snuffle Cavern. He shows David and Maria the things he'll bring, including a muffler (to keep warm in the drafty cave), Radar, and a large set of directions to Snuffy's place.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird stays overnight in Mr. Snuffleupagus's cave
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob observes all the different kinds of things the kids are sculpting with clay at the Day Care Center, including a castle, a ball, and a house. Oscar intrudes on today's activities as he likes using sticky, messy clay, and wants to show how he's the "Michelangelo of Grouchdom." Oscar lets himself in, hushing Bob not to ruin his inspiration.
Mr. Snuffleupagus sees Linda reading the newspaper in the yard and decides to go speak to her. Since she's facing away from him, he receives no response when he tries making conversation.
A woman arrives on the street and meets Big Bird. She only speaks Spanish, so he goes back and forth between the brownstone and Hooper's Store, where Mr. Ortiz just happens to be working today.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird uses a screen to show "over" and "under" by peeking his head over and under it. He does this several times and finds going under very straining until Olivia points out that both his head and feet can illustrate the difference.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Luis awaits the arrival of Dr. Nobel Price, who has another new invention to show off. Dr. Price, however, feels his latest project is already a failure. ("It's no good, a clinker - to use the scientific word, a 'boo-boo.'") He unveils his creation - "woodies," a bunch of wooden objects of different shapes.

Oscar, carried by Bruno the Trashman, reports for the Weird World of Grouch Sports, covering a Grouch walking race on Sesame Street. Competitors Gordon, Susan, Luis, Maria, and Mr. Hooper disagree over who will win as Olivia snaps photos.

Big Bird gets up early to make sure he's the first one up on Sesame Street. He looks out to see who gets up next by seeing whose apartment lights go on - Bob is first, then Gordon and Susan, followed by Bert and Ernie, Maria, and finally Oscar the Grouch.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Luis and Olivia greet the viewer on a very hot day on Sesame Street. Olivia comments that it's so hot, one could fry an egg on the sidewalk.

altLabels.labelEn: A very hot day on Sesame Street
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Michael Earl voices the radio announcer in the closing scene.

episodes.summaryEn: Under Bob's supervision, Forgetful Jones welcomes the viewer, but has trouble remembering where he's welcoming them to. Bob clues him in by looking at the sign he's next to, which doesn't help (Forgetful forgot his glasses).
episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: The music that plays during Barkley's dream sequence is Wagner's "Liebestod" from Tristan and Isolde.

episodes.summaryEn: While standing under an umbrella in the rain, Telly tells the viewer he and Maria are about to go on a picnic, but Maria says they can't. Telly wonders what the problem could be, whether it's ants, mosquitos, poison ivy, or even bears.
episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: While Telly is worried about running into bears in this episode, one of them would become his best friend years later in the 1990s.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird rushes into the yard to join Linda and the kids for some "action words." Linda shows everyone how to sign the letter J, then acts out various J words and signs for the others to imitate (jump, juggle, and jog). Mr. Hooper brings the tired participants some juice.
episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: A summary from the Sesame Street Script Highlights for this episode includes a segment called Starship Surprise, however the piece doesn't appear in the script or in the final cut of the episode.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird finds it odd when he sees Bob waving his hands while listening to music. Maria, David and Linda explain that he's practicing conducting for a high school music performance tomorrow.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1203. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird roller skates around the street to a carnival rendition of the "Sesame Street Theme," dubbing himself "a regular Dorothy Camel." Attempting to show off a trick for the kids, he spins and takes a fall in the yard.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1284. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: David anxiously waits at the bus stop for his Grandma Grace who is visiting today. When the bus finally arrives, Mr. Macintosh steps out and tells him he hasn't seen her; he was the only passenger.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1263. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar the Grouch pulls up on the block in his new taxi, which is a ratty-looking cab that is falling apart at the seams. Gordon points out that nobody in their right mind would want a ride in his taxi - exactly what Oscar hopes.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1252. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: As rousing march music plays, Oscar calls out for his neighbors to see "the creepiest, crawliest show on Earth!" David, Olivia, Mr. Hooper, and the kids gather around Oscar's trash can as Slimey the Great makes his entrance from a miniature circus tent. Oscar introduces three tricks Slimey will do - a somersault, climbing up to a high diving board, and jumping into a bowl of mud.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1280. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Mr. Hooper blends the word PET and Barkley jumps on him. Maria assumes a safe spot away from Oscar's trash can to blend the word WET.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1311. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon, Big Bird and the kids play Blind Man's Bluff, with Gordon being blindfolded. Mr. Snuffleupagus stops by on his way to his Granny's house for tea and joins the game.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1266. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Maria watches after a Muppet canary for a friend of hers. Big Bird hears her speaking Spanish to it, since her friend also speaks Spanish and Maria feels it would make the bird more comfortable.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1278. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar shows Bob and Susan his tape recorder, which he's used to record some of the "lovely" sounds of Sesame Street, including Gordon and Susan's car stalling, Cody crying, and Biff and Sully's jackhammering. He realizes that he also picked up some dialogue from Big Bird talking to Mr. Snuffleupagus.

altLabels.labelEn: The Count counts and sorts items at Hooper's Store
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1201. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: David and the kids find Oscar watching the skies with his spyglass. He's hired Alphabet Bates to write one of his favorite letters in the sky - U, for such words as unhappy, uncouth, unfair...

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1255. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: The Count pulls up on Sesame Street in his Countmobile and notices Luis working on an iron at the Fix-It Shop. This inspires the Count to count jobs people have.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1287. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Luis shows Big Bird, Sharmaine, and Jeff how to tie a square knot using ropes, demonstrating "over," "under," and "through." Big Bird then asks how to untie a knot, having knotted himself up.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird waits for the sun
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1197. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Maria and the kids play with a ball, which gets stuck on top of the trellis outside Hooper's Store. Before Maria can go get a ladder, Super Grover lands on the scene (or in the trash basket, rather).

altLabels.labelEn: Super Grover rescues a ball / Bert's rooftop pigeon coop
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1293. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: At Hooper's Store, Timi, David, Maria and Linda have lunch. Timi asks for the salt, pepper and sugar, which are on Linda's side of the counter.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1269. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Herry Monster calls everyone over to witness a never-before-seen feat - he will lift a 4,000 ton weight! He struggles immensely to even move it, but with encouragement from his friends, Herry finds the strength to lift the weight.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1225. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar has interest in becoming a photographer and asks Olivia for her professional opinion of his pictures. Despite the poor quality of the printing and unconventional subject matter (rusted cars and a trash basket, among others), Olivia thinks he has real potential, which discourages him from going professional.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1217. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Maurice Monster is puzzled by the nursery rhyme in his book. Bob points out that he's reading each sentence backwards, from right to left, and shows him how to do it the correct way.

altLabels.labelEn: Mr. Hooper allows his store to be a location for a movie
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1262. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: David hears Bob, Susan, and the kids singing and banging pots outside. He calls for a drum beat and plays a musical game where they bang their pots the number of times he calls for.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1298. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar is upset that Gordon, Susan, Bob and the kids are picking up all the litter left by a windstorm. The Amazing Mumford believes he can help Oscar and magically litters the street again.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1196. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Grandma Grace is visiting the street again, having dinner at Gordon and Susan's apartment with Susan, David, Linda, Big Bird, and the kids (who are playing with a Lite-Brite). Suddenly, the power goes out.

altLabels.labelEn: Grandma Grace visits during a blackout
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1295. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Ferlinghetti Donizetti and Deena perform the "Rhymer Rag."

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird guards a freshly painted Hooper's Store
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Olivia notices Oscar the Grouch in the midst of a funk. He explains that he feels rotten because everyone is having fun, but because he doesn't like that sort of thing, he feels different and left out.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Big Bird previously pretended to be Sherlock Hemlock in Episode 0273.

episodes.summaryEn: Bob works on his stamp collection in the yard, when Big Bird arrives. He cites how clumsy Bob can be and brings some pillows he can wear in case Bob drops something on himself.
Big Bird finds it fun to talk loud and decides to spend the day doing so. He makes his way to Hooper's Store, drowning out everyone else's conversations with his loud talking.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird, Olivia, Bob, Mr. Hooper and the kids welcome all the new viewers with the "Hello Hello Hello Song."

At the Fix-It Shop, Luis permits Telly Monster to hang around and help out by holding two pieces of wood together. As Luis gets his tools, the mischievous Poco Loco starts to tickle Telly and make him lose his grip.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Telly Monster sings "If Buses Didn't Run" as he watches Gordon at the bus stop. Once the bus actually arrives and Gordon gets on, Telly's worry shifts to whether Gordon got on the right bus or if he'll ever return.
episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Puppeteer Michael Earl makes an onscreen cameo as the bus driver during scene 1.

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar, aided by his cameraman Frankie, hosts "Grouch Breakfast on the Air" at Hooper's Store. His surprise guest is Mr. Hooper, in that it is a surprise to him that he is a guest on the show.

Oscar's trash can area has been converted into a fast food establishment - "Colonel Oscar's Eat and Beat It" (with "Over 0 Sold" proudly displayed on a sign). Oscar, wearing a string tie and white moustache and goatee, boasts that his joint is the best and will soon be franchised across the country.
Big Bird writes a letter to Buffy and the others chime in with things to write. To their surprise, Buffy and Cody turn up on the block that very moment!

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar blares his trumpet to wake up Buffy and the animals for their morning exercises. Oscar then gets everyone ready for a jog around the block, which is done by having Bruno the Trashman carry his can as he jogs around the block.
episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Oscar wears a Camp Uglyyucchy hat during scene 1, foreshadowing the events that occur the following week.

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar can sense the viewer's presence from inside his can. He emerges in order to toss a tin can on the sidewalk, which he loves the sound and sight of.

David, Maria, and the kids notice a large arrow on the floor of Hooper's Store, with a message telling them to follow it to a big surprise. The arrow points to another and another, leading them across Sesame Street and finally ending at Big Bird's nest.

Oscar and Osvaldo, el Gruñón try to think of a game to play, while Telly Monster is around to make sure it's quiet to prevent waking up Buffy, who's staying over inside Oscar's trash can. Telly rejects their idea of pretending to be a nurse and patient at a Grouch hospital (where they yell instead of speak softly) and thinks it's better if they pretend to be farmers, which is a quiet business.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Telly Monster explains that Linda has invited him over to her apartment for a visit. When he rings the doorbell, he remembers that Linda is deaf, and that she's not going to hear it.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: At Hooper's Store, David says hello to several kids who walk by, but they don't respond. They're all wearing shirts and caps with the letter U on them, and they're headed for Oscar's trash can.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar has bought an old victrola from the annual Grouch Junk Festival. He thinks it's junky because with no electric plug or batteries, it won't work at all.

Oscar asks (or yells, rather) for a rotten piece of wood from the Fix-It Shop. The one provided by Maria is too long, and Oscar uses Slimey to measure it to the right length he needs (five Slimeys long).
episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: In the script for the episode, Cowboy X (in Muppet form) was to appear during Scene 3, drawing more Xs after the game ends.

episodes.summaryEn: Buffy emerges from Oscar's trash can, complaining about the living conditions she and Cody have to endure there while staying. She needs to run to the store and asks Oscar to get her bag.

Mr. Hooper takes a phone call from the pay phone in Hooper's Store; it's his younger brother, Arnold in Chicago. He asks how the family is and wants to know when he'll see him next; Arnold replies he'll see him next when he looks out the window.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Susan stops by Oscar's trash can to see Buffy and Cody. She asks Oscar a series of questions about Buffy and Cody, but is met with a sign popping up from inside reading "NO." This happens more and more, frustrating Susan further until she pulls Oscar out herself.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar asks Telly Monster to watch his can while he goes out grocery shopping. Buffy emerges sobbing, and vents to Telly about the terrible living conditions inside while she and Cody are staying with Oscar.

Maria and her cousin Mercedes are about to do some work in the back room of the Fix-It Shop, when Buffy emerges from the shop's trash can. She explains that Oscar threw a big party in Oscar's trash can last night and she never got any sleep.

On a rainy day, Oscar reports for WORM-TV to ask some passerby their three questions of the day, which will earn them a grand prize. Oscar makes Luis stand out in the rain as he asks the three questions, all having to do with what happens when someone stands in the rain too long.

altLabels.labelEn: A Honker orders food from Hooper's
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Dr. Nobel Price describes his latest invention to Mr. Hooper, which sounds remarkably like the toaster they already have in Hooper's Store. However, Dr. Price's toaster is able to talk (voiced by Kathryn Mullen), but burns the toast to a crisp.

Olivia sees Big Bird and Barkley at the curb near the bus stop. Big Bird says he's bringing Barkley to the vet for a check-up, and Olivia reminds Big Bird that he shouldn't cross the street without the help of a grown-up.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Telly Monster listens to the commotion of Oscar and Buffy's morning routine: the running down of the blaring alarm clock, a faulty water pipe, a cow in the bathroom, and Oscar's china closet falling over. Telly worries about Buffy's well being, but she assures him she's fine as she takes in the trash: "This is just one more, regular old morning at Oscar's."

Oscar isn't enjoying his night, as Buffy and Cody are singing and having fun while staying over in his can. Mr. Hooper locks up the store for the night, then realizes he's left his house keys inside; Luis won't be around to help open the store until tomorrow.

altLabels.labelEn: The adults stay over in Oscar's can
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar still has all the adult guests (with Barkley, and Gordon and Susan who have joined since last night) staying in his trash can, singing "I Don't Want No More of Trash Can Life" and having a great time, which Oscar can't stand. Luis thinks he can help out Oscar, but that requires the Grouch to cooperate.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar gets rid of the guests in his can
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Additional performers include Ed Christie as Dr. Price's right hand.

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar, dubbing himself "The Great Grouchini," calls folks over to see him perform Grouch feats of magic. However, nobody finds any of his so-called tricks impressive as he removes things from his topless hat (a boot, another hat, and the hat's lining).

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar tries to break a record
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird paces outside his nest and tells Maria he's waiting for Mr. Snuffleupagus to return from his first day of Snufflegarden. Maria passes on hanging around, finding the idea silly.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar spends the day with Irvine
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Rehearsal footage of the final scene (filmed for an unfinished Sesame Street documentary) appears in A&E Biography: Sesame Street.

episodes.summaryEn: Luis invites Big Bird to join himself and two kids in some drawing. Big Bird isn't in the mood and wanders off.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Michael Earl voices the unseen bus driver who yells at Osvaldo when he arrives on Sesame Street in scene 2.

episodes.summaryEn: Telly Monster has the numbers 2 through 5 set out in the yard, along with various groups ranging from two to five items each. He's not sure how to match them up, so Gordon, Jessica, Mitch, and Brandon give him some assistance.

Poco Loco hangs out in Big Bird's nest area by himself and answers the ringing phone. The call is from Mr. Snuffleupagus, who only manages to say "Oh dear, I wonder where Bird is..." before hanging up.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Luis arrives at the Fix-it Shop with a small birdcage. He introduces Poco Loco to Bagel, a parakeet that Olivia will be watching for a friend.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Buffy's recording of "Until It's Time for You to Go" heard on Oscar's radio comes from the 1965 Buffy Sainte-Marie album Many a Mile. Muppet Wiki note: The raucous party version of the Sesame Street Theme during the credits would also be used for the VHS release "Oscar's Letter Party," and the CD-I game, A Visit to Sesame Street - Letters.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird tells the viewer to sit quietly so they won't disturb David as he studies. Big Bird starts getting antsy and opts to stand quietly, then walk, run, and hop as quietly as he can, though this still distracts David.
episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: The script called for Maria to sing "The Calypso Symbol Song" during Scene 2.

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar pens a letter regarding the city trash pick-up, as the trash was collected before he had his chance to rummage through and collect anything. He isn't sure who it should be addressed to, when Gordon states that the mayor is the one in charge of the whole city.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird strolls down Sesame Street and notices Maria outside the Fix-It Shop, pacing around and talking to herself. She explains that she's figuring out the right way to ask Luis for a raise.

altLabels.labelEn: Maria asks Luis for a raise
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: The program highlights for the episode mention scenes not present in the final episode, including Oscar the Grouch singing a "STOP" song, and Gordon playing a ball game with Monica.

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar is happy because today, Buffy and Cody are heading back to Hawaii and no longer are staying in his can (allowing his pet pig Spot to get back their room). Telly Monster, on the other hand, hates goodbyes and is sad to see Buffy leave.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: On the stoop of 123 Sesame Street, Gordon shows everybody a WALK sign (which Big Bird misreads as "Constantinople"). Maria and Linda state how one would say the word in Spanish and ASL.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar cuts the opening music short as he's leading The Grouchketeer Noisemaking Band in a ratty version of "The Stars and Gripes Forever." He has the group practice so that they sound just right (or wrong, as the case may be).

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Slimey emerges from his own, miniature can and spots a butterfly nearby. He begins following it as it flutters around the street, eventually going over the fence in the yard.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Oscar sings a snippet of "When the Red, Red Robin (Comes Bob, Bob, Bobbin' Along)" while checking on Slimey during scene 1. Muppet Wiki note: Brian Muehl performs the Bureau of Missing Worms agent and the WORM crew member.

episodes.summaryEn: Bob and the kids ask Oscar for some trash. He is glad to oblige, saying, "I like spreading the trash around.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon phones the Hooper's Store, ordering a big meal to be ready in just three minutes. Big Bird doesn't think David can prepare the food in a short amount of time.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar is having a boring day, until he sees something in the sky. Oscar exclaims, "It's a bird, it's a plane, it's... a trash can?!"

altLabels.labelEn: Close Encounters of the Worst Kind
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Behind the scenes footage of the episode, including the story meeting and shooting, appears on 40 Years of Sunny Days. A graphic erroneously labels it as coming from season 14, in reference to its repeat that year. Muppet Wiki note: Oscar would launch into space again in Episode 1714.

episodes.summaryEn: Timi introduces Big Bird to her sister, Holly. Big Bird messes up her name, calling her Molly and Polly, among other names.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Snuffy would end up getting a sister of his own years later, named Alice. Muppet Wiki note: Big Bird claims to not have a sister, despite the mention of his sister Tondalea in multiple episodes, both past and future.

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon describes what a surprise is as he sets out a sweet potato pie on the windowsill, which he intends to surprise someone with. A hungry Big Bird discovers it, and calls the kids over to share it with him at his nest.
The Count is in distress - one of his seven bats, Cynthia, has gone missing! While he goes to contact the Bureau of Missing Bats, Maria and Big Bird search for her on the block.
Maria invites the Count to watch a new game she has for Nicole and Jessica. She traces a number on each of their backs and they guess which number she's made.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria doesn't like the current heat wave, but Oscar does, saying it's the perfect weather for a Grouch like himself. They briefly discuss their differences until Oscar suggests that she go to Hooper's Store since it's air conditioned.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar has no one to bother, and Fred Rogers visits
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Part of Scene 6, where Mr. Rogers and Big Bird discuss real and pretend, is available on 40 Years of Sunny Days.

episodes.summaryEn: Maria is sprucing up the Fix-it Shop awning when she encounters two odd individuals: Madeline and Cedrick. They are birdwatchers, and have arrived on Sesame Street after being informed of a large, yellow bird that lives there.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: The street plot was directly adapted for a 1985 episode of Rechov Sumsum, where a pair of animal watchers discover Kippi Ben Kippod. Muppet Wiki note: The Old School: Volume 3 DVD release of this episode omits the opening theme song, and replaces the organ-arrangement of it in scene 3 with a new music track. This cut of the episode, with an added credit sequence from Episode 1580, has been released on HBO Kids and HBO Max.

episodes.summaryEn: Telly introduces Maria, Luis and Big Bird to his best friend Aristotle ("Ari" for short), a fellow monster who loves helping, collecting items and is also blind. By the sound of their voices, Aristotle is able to tell that Maria is big, Luis is bigger and Big Bird is the biggest of them all.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob happens into today's Grouchketeer meeting, where Oscar teaches the members about loud and quiet. At first, they bang pots and pans loudly, then quieter and quieter, then not at all, providing enough quiet for Oscar to loudly tell Bob to scram.
Forgetful Jones and Buster the Horse appear set up to paint, only Forgetful has forgotten what they're trying to do. Maria sorts through the clues to help him remember.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: A Dinger was originally scripted to participate in the last two scenes as well.

episodes.summaryEn: Olivia asks Catherine, Andre, and Bahiyyah to find the hidden letter Ts in a picture of a train.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Mr. Macintosh needs someone to watch his fruit stand while he runs to the post office. Big Bird volunteers, then suddenly finds he needs to use the restroom.
Big Bird invites the viewer to listen to the sounds of Sesame Street, which he controls the volume of by gesturing as if he's turning a volume knob.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Frankie assists the Amazing Mumford in his latest show, where he identifies the shapes that Mumford pulls from his hat.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Forgetful Jones visits the Fix-It Shop so Maria can fix his coat. Maria finds that not only is the coat not broken, but Forgetful can remember how to put one on; he's just mixed up the order he's supposed to do what.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar shows Gordon a box of Grouch breakfast food, simply called "X." When prompted about how it's served, Oscar replies with a series of "X / eggs" puns.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird and Snuffy hunt for treasure
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Big Bird ad-libs a reference to Alphonse and Gaston, not included in the script. Muppet Wiki note: A clip from Scene 2 later appeared in Episode 2096.

episodes.summaryEn: A mason, Mr. Jenkins (Ted Ross), does some work surrounding the front doors of 123 Sesame Street. A sawhorse barricade blocks the area, marked with a "DANGER" sign.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar takes temporary residence at David's
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: The names of Oscar's pets Dick, Jane, and Spot all reference the Dick and Jane readers. Muppet Wiki note: This episode was later repeated in Season 15 as Episode 1881.

episodes.summaryEn: Mr. Snuffleupagus arrives on Sesame Street at the crack of dawn, hoping to be seen by somebody as everyone wakes up. It's so early that he falls back to sleep, resting in the yard.
Telly introduces another episode of "Shape Up with Slimey," an exercise program. Slimey leads the kids in various exercises, until Oscar tells them to keep down the noise.
Maria works on a bookcase at the Fix-It Shop, when she's approached by Granny Bird, who is paying a surprise visit to her grandson. She has special gifts for everyone and gives Maria an apple.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Mr. Snuffleupagus feels down because he doesn't feel as though Snuffleupaguses like him are as good as other creatures: he thinks he's too shaggy and slow, and is ashamed of having four legs. Big Bird shows him how his unique attributes make him special and calls him graceful and beautiful.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Olivia learns that Grundgetta is a fellow photographer, and sees that she also uses lights and a camera similar to hers (albeit both are shabby-looking). Grundgetta shows her the key difference when a Grouch takes photos as she snaps pictures of Oscar in his smoking jacket and pipe - they do it without any film.
episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Richard Hunt performs the Muppet letters U and R during Telly's lectures.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird finds Telly, Olivia, Maria and Gordon congregated out in the yard. Telly has gotten a fire bell to warn people of fires, but now thinks it's a silly and useless idea.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: As Gordon fixes the leaky faucet attached to the garage, Telly ponders what it would be like in a world without water. Just as Gordon finishes the job, a downpour begins.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Poco Loco sits in the tree outside the Fix-It Shop, perfectly able to imitate Luis' voice and everything he says. Luis muses out loud about the salad and juice he intends to order from Hooper's Store right after he puts some things away in the store.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob and David watch Big Bird zip around going, "Zzzzzz!" in an effort to practice the sound of the letter Z, believing he will earn fame and adulation if he gets good enough. He hopes to get on such famous shows as "Real Purple" and "That's Ridiculous!," but David shows him how he can make the sound without running about.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Donning a cape, Big Bird declares himself "Helping Bird," the bird who helps those in need. Nobody seems to need his help until he sees Gordon has twisted his ankle while jogging.
Grandma Grace is the new crossing guard in the area. Big Bird wishes to be one too, and has even made up his own pretend street to practice on using his toy cars.

Luis checks out Dr. Nobel Price's latest discovery - a creature he's dubbed "the beady-eyed oinky oink." Dr. Price learns that not only is it actually a pig, but the animal happens to be Oscar's pet pig, Spot. Oscar collects his pig and Dr. Price shifts gears to a new animal he's discovered - the tail-wagging arf-arf.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Telly can't believe his ears when he hears Oscar saying nice things. Oscar thinks he may be sick and contacts Dr. Kvetch.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: This was the first episode taped to feature Aristotle, and his appearance here reflects his early design of having thinning hair. All other appearances would have Ari with a fuller mop of feathery hair.

episodes.summaryEn: On an exceptionally sunny day, Dr. Nobel Price presents his latest creation - shady shadies, which are very much like Olivia's sunglasses.

Big Bird watches as the kids make themselves as small as they can, while Bob measures them with a ruler. Big Bird is able to shorten himself to about three feet, which Bob finds quite an accomplishment for a bird his size, though Big Bird thinks he isn't all that small.

A rainstorm begins as Slimey prepares to be launched into outer space. Maria watches as Telly, filling the "Mission Decontrol" position, attempts a countdown, but counts forwards instead of backwards.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Pleased by the cloudy weather, Oscar feels like taking a nap outside, when two kids pass by and tell him a joke. As he tries going back to sleep, Gordon shows him a photo of a chameleon.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: This was Martin P. Robinson's first recorded episode as Mr. Snuffleupagus, though Robinson has recalled Episode 1601 (taped the next day) as his first.

episodes.summaryEn: Maria watches as Oscar, Grundgetta, and the Grouchketeers try a few dances for an upcoming Grouch dance contest. First, Oscar calls out a square dance while Grundgetta plays an out-of-tune fiddle.

In the Fix-It Shop, The Amazing Mumford demonstrates his new rhyming trick, in which he turns himself into anything that rhymes with something he says. He first says "slide trombone" and turns himself into a telephone.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Brian Muehl performs Buster for this episode.

episodes.summaryEn: In the Fix-It Shop, an Anything Muppet boy (Richard Hunt) has made his own letter L and shows it to Maria and the kids. He has a game to go along with it - he gives clues about different locations that begin with L and the others guess where he's referring to.

After witnessing Herry Monster lifting a large barbell, Telly wishes he could do the same, though doesn't believe he can do it. Bob sings "Don't Be Afraid to Try," encouraging him to give it a try and keep trying until he's able to do.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird and Nico color together on the ground, when Barkley bounds over and sits on their coloring book. They try moving locations to keep him away, but he does the same thing again.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Olivia introduces Big Bird and the kids to her special (romantic) friend, Hal. They give clues as to what Hal's job is (an airline pilot) based on his uniform and how he describes what he rides in.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: The script attributes the role of the pilot to Hal Williams.

episodes.summaryEn: Maria is finishing building a birdhouse for a friend of hers from the country, who is coming to visit Sesame Street today. Biff and Sully enter the Fix-It Shop, where Biff assumes the birdhouse is instead a boat and a racecar.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Jerry Nelson voices the off-screen bus driver in scene 2.

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon notices an incoming rainfall, while Forgetful Jones tries to remember what he was supposed to get when the rain hits. He thinks he needs his lawnmower to cut the newly-refreshed grass, then a bucket to deflood the basement if the stream behind the ranch overflows.
episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: A clip from scene 4 is used in Episode 3611 when Big Bird reminisces about Mr. Hooper's birdseed milkshakes.

episodes.summaryEn: Olivia greets the viewer and reports that David's grandmother Grace will be visiting from the country. Oscar will return any minute in his taxi with her.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Luis needs to step out of the Fix-It Shop for a few minutes and asks Maria to mind the telephone. It only takes Maria a few moments to get overworked between repairs and phone calls.

altLabels.labelEn: Maria's beach daydream; The Count exercises
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria needs to place an important call, but every telephone on the block seems to be out of order, except for Oscar's, which David spots being used in conversation. Maria approaches him to use the phone, but he's too wrapped up in his call with his friend Grumpy arguing over Grouch baseball teams.

Maria, David, Big Bird, and the kids are waiting for the bus to take them to Grandma Grace's farm for the day. They invite Oscar along for the trip, but he has no interest in watching little kids have fun all day.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon plays a guessing game with the kids - he plays sounds off his tape recorder and the kids guess their origin. Oscar chimes in with a sound he wants to hear - the sound of their footsteps walking away from his can area.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria tells the viewer that her cousin Mercedes is coming to visit all the way from Puerto Rico. She states that the Count was supposed to drive her to the airport, but he instead opted to count the parts of his car.

altLabels.labelEn: Snow — Maria's cousin Mercedes comes to visit
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Richard Hunt performs the WORM-TV camera-grouch Jerry, named after Sesame Street cameraman Jerry Gruen.

episodes.summaryEn: On a chilly and windy day on Sesame Street, Telly worries that the wind will be strong enough to blow him away to a strange place he's never been to. Maria assures him this wouldn't happen, but holds onto his hand anyhow.

altLabels.labelEn: Snow — A very chilly day on Sesame Street
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria does some work in Fix-It Shop, when in walks Zero, a penguin cousin of Big Bird's. He's come to visit all the way from the South Pole.

altLabels.labelEn: Snow — Zero the Penguin comes to visit
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: As snow falls on Sesame Street, Maria's cousin Mercedes goes outside to observe it, since it never snows in Puerto Rico. In Hooper's Store, Mr. Hooper gives Big Bird and Zero their take out order.

altLabels.labelEn: Snow — The snow storm reaches Sesame Street
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: The blizzard has put the entire city at a standstill. David tries his best to shovel a path to Hooper's Store, which currently has no heat.

altLabels.labelEn: Snow — Making deliveries in the blizzard
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Zero has made himself an igloo near Big Bird's nest and everyone listens closely to his stories of the Antarctic life, paying no attention to Big Bird. He tries various things to get them to notice him, but with no luck.

altLabels.labelEn: Snow — Big Bird pretends to be a penguin
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: As the kids play in the snow, Bob sings "Snowflakes."

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Mr. Snuffleupagus comes over to meet Big Bird's friends, but no one seems to be around in the chilly weather. Maria's cousin Mercedes makes a mad dash back to 123 Sesame Street from Hooper's Store, barely noticing the two because of her fur hood.

altLabels.labelEn: Snow — Big Bird and Snuffy bring Puerto Rico to Sesame Street
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird wakes up to find Zero's igloo has gotten considerably smaller, as a puddle of water surrounds it. Zero returns from his morning walk, shocked to see what's happened.

altLabels.labelEn: Snow — Mercedes and Zero head back home
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird, Bob, David, Linda, Gordon and Susan bid Maria and Olivia farewell as they board the bus to the airport. Once the bus is out of sight, they happily grab their own luggage and prepare to follow them -- all except for Gordon, who isn't going with them.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1316. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment. Muppet Wiki note: This episode is a repeat of the scenes from Episode 1316, but excludes the parts in which Oscar meets Osvaldo, el Gruñón (since by season 13 Oscar has interacted with Osvaldo multiple times).

episodes.summaryEn: On a sunny morning in Puerto Rico, Maria comes out onto the porch. She spots David across the way from his residence in the country and invites him and the others over for breakfast with the family.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1317. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar and Osvaldo are going to go "trashing," but because his push cart is "Grouch-powered," one of them must be responsible for pushing it. They argue over who will push and who will look out for trash, and eventually agree to take turns.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1318. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar and Osvaldo float on a Grouch raft (still in their trashcans) toward the dock on a nearby island of the coast of Puerto Rico. The two crawl to the edge of the dock and are pleased to find some peace and quiet away from all their happy acquaintances.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1319. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Everyone is setting up for a festival in the town square today. Big Bird offers his services to Luis, who is installing some speakers.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1320. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Maria and friends bid farewell to her family as their board their bus back to the airport. Oscar and Osvaldo also part ways, causing Oscar to miss the bus.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1321. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: In Hooper's Store, David has discovered some broken eggshells sitting on the counter. He wonders who could've left them behind, when Sherlock Hemlock arrives to solve the mystery.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1369. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Olivia and David hear the sound of a racing car nearby and trace the sound to Oscar's trash can. David peeks inside and sure enough spots Oscar zooming around until he crashes into the refrigerator.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1368. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird takes a stroll down Sesame Street, admiring the usual sunny day. Suddenly, he hears something and sees a flying saucer land in the yard behind the fence!

altLabels.labelEn: C-3PO and R2-D2 visit Sesame Street, part 1
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1364. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: After being bothered by the kids, Oscar meets Winkle (Mary Wickes), a woman from upstate who claims to be in "the dirt business" and is looking to sell her wares in the big city. Oscar is immediately invested and promises to watch her bag of dirt as she gets more of her stuff to set up shop nearby.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1430. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird brings the mail to Hooper's Store and Mr. Hooper proceeds to read a postcard from his friend Harry who's vacationing at the beach. Big Bird encourages Mr. Hooper to imagine himself on a beach since he can't really go and leave the store alone.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1443. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird presides over the meeting of the "Small People of Sesame Street," which consists of two kids and himself (he's a member because of his age, not his height). He shows Susan a list they've made of all the reasons being big is best, leading to a duet between him and Susan about the differences between big people and small people.

altLabels.labelEn: The Small People of Sesame Street
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1367. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird has noticed he's the tallest individual on Sesame Street. He encourages the viewer to use their imagination to become as tall as he is, giving them a new perspective of the street.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1363. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird takes care of Hooper's Store while David runs out. Bob phones the store, not feeling well, and asks for a container of orange juice, a bottle of milk and a loaf of bread to be sent up to his apartment.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1427. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird, Bob and David watch a ballet performance of Swan Lake on television. Big Bird is very impressed with the way the dancers almost seem like they're flying and is even more amazed that one can get paid to dance.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1405. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: David is about to make a delivery, when Big Bird stops him to play a guessing game involving a hypothetical visit from a family member. It turns out that his grandmother Grace is visiting the street today!

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1421. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon witnesses Oscar's scientific creation - Charles, a grouch robot. The robot is able to tell Gordon to "get lost," then turn himself into a heap of trash by falling apart.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird goes to the doctor
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1339. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird tells Susan that he's awaiting the arrival of his friends C-3PO and R2-D2, but isn't sure where the bus stop that their bus will arrive at is. Susan shows him the bus stop sign nearby, and soon the next bus pulls up.

altLabels.labelEn: C-3PO and R2-D2 visit Sesame Street, part 2
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1396. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird helps Mr. Snuffleupagus get ready for a big cabbage-eating contest later today. They practice by feeding him cabbage after cabbage after cabbage...

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1371. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird presents the letter D, then a dog - Barkley, who pounces on his child audience.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 1365. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Telly becomes worried when he sees a firefighter arriving on Sesame Street, as he believes that wherever there's a fireman, there must be a fire nearby. The fireman reassures Telly that there is no fire, and that he's here to visit the Day Care Center to teach the kids about fire safety.

altLabels.labelEn: A fireman visits the daycare center
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria hastily greets the viewer, as she has a lot of work to do today at the Fix-It Shop. She hopes she doesn't get any interruptions as she heads into the back room and starts sawing.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar the Grouch explains to Susan and Gordon that he and Spot haven't slept in two nights because of renovations going on in his can. He doesn't know what will happen if he doesn't get any sleep tonight, so when the Robinsons suggest he stay at someone's apartment, Oscar offers their own place up.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar has dinner with the Robinsons
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon, Susan and Mr. Hooper have been invited to Big Bird's nest for a tea party and to finally meet Mr. Snuffleupagus, or so they believe. While they wait for Big Bird they try to guess what kind of excuse will keep them from meeting whom they think is Big Bird's imaginary friend.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: This episode was later re-aired in Season 15 as Episode 1898, omitting scene 1 due to the death of Mr. Hooper. Muppet Wiki note: In scene 4, Bob, Gordon, and even Big Bird refer to Gladys only as "Cow," despite the character already meeting them many times before.

episodes.summaryEn: Buster and Fred, dressed as cows, approach Olivia, asking if she knows where Gladys the Cow is. They're helping with a song of hers and the lack of local cows forces them to play some.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Mr. Hooper discovers the store has no more eggs, bread or orange juice, and the breakfast crowd will be due soon. A Honker appears to run the counter while Mr. Hooper gets some groceries.

Big Bird has opened up his own version of the Fix-It Shop right outside to the original. Susan comes by with her broken toaster and forbids him from touching it, since he isn't even aware of how to fix things.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Big Bird had previously started a lemonade stand in Episode 1300.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird presents David, who makes the form of the letter Y with his body; his outstretched arms turn into a hug for Big Bird.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: A child (Sonia Bailey) narrates as a scene unfolds in front of the Fix-it Shop. Barkley barks at the ringing pay phone outside the shop, getting Linda's attention.

Big Bird is getting a new telephone installed in his nest (having dropped his last phone in a goldfish bowl). The phone man (Richard Hunt) arrives to install the phone, but Big Bird can't make up his mind whether it should be hung over or under the guest birdhouse already nailed to the post.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: The Canary Brothers were previously seen in Episode 1576.

episodes.summaryEn: Olivia sings "Hand Signs" as Linda demonstrates different signs for the kids.

Mr. Hooper opens the front window of Hooper's Store to listen to the sounds of the street, including traffic, the kids playing in the yard, and the Sloppy Jalopy. He's startled by the sound of a roaring lion, which turns out to be Poco Loco.

Big Bird leads the kids on a "circle tour" of Sesame Street, pointing out various circles around the block. A telestrated circle appears as Big Bird shows off the various round objects, from his alarm clock to the lid of Oscar's trash can to the wheels of Susan's bicycle.
Maria wants to find out what breed of dog Barkley is and has gotten a book about dogs to reach a conclusion. She, Big Bird and the kids sift through the book and find he greatly resembles a sheepdog.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Olivia and Luis bring some old books over to Big Bird's nest, which he has turned into a library for the kids. They notice one bookshelf of his is crooked - one leg is shorter than the other.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar is going on vacation to Camp Killjoy near Swamp Mushy Muddy. Maria helps him make sure he has all his various items he'll need (such as mud skis and boxing gloves to use while feeding porcupines).

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Telly wants to demonstrate what it looks like when someone is angry and intends to get Oscar, an expert, to help. He pauses before knocking on the can, believing that since Grouches like being angry, Oscar will instead thank Telly for the annoyance instead of being angry.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Young Gordon and Olivia are portrayed by Billy Mack and Jasmine Winslow.

episodes.summaryEn: Bob welcomes the viewer and notices that his watch has stopped. As he wonders what time it is, the pay phone outside his apartment rings.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird brings Ralphie a quart of milk from Hooper's Store. He offers to help him carry it home, since it may be difficult in his wheelchair.

This week on "Ask Oscar," a viewer wants to know if Oscar is able to recite the alphabet while jumping and patting his stomach at the same time. Oscar instead recites the alphabet as Telly does the other actions, pretending not to remember some letters just to make Telly suffer.

Gordon exits the carriage house and finds Big Bird attempting to whistle like kids can, but is frustrated. Gordon encourages him to keep trying and assures him that with practice, he'll be able to whistle.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: A new stove has been delivered to Hooper's Store, but it's much too heavy for Mr. Hooper, Bob, and Gordon to move. Herry Monster effortlessly brings it inside, then asks Gordon if he can help him cross the street.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Aristotle and Monica are about to have some pie, but remember to wait for Big Bird, who rushes over to show off his special pie-eating tie. He remembers that the two are blind and can't see it.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird is the early bird once again on this morning and hears the loud sounds of the Honkers. He tells them in a whisper to honk quieter so they don't disturb the neighbors.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird and the kids pretend to be cowpokes riding around on their horses. Big Bird invites Bob to join them, but he's got other plans already.

Telly comes into Hooper's Store for an oatmeal breakfast, believing starting the day out right with a good breakfast will prevent anything wrong happening in the rest of the day. David and Mr. Hooper discover they're out of oatmeal and argue over whose fault it is.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Telly assumes the letter Linda has received from Timi is bad news, until they read it together with Olivia: Timi will be coming to Sesame Street for a television gig, performing sign language translations on air. They then see Timi in the Sloppy Jalopy with Oscar the Grouch, when it's revealed that she'll be working for him on WORM-TV!

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Additional performers include Cheryl Blaylock as the unseen stage manager for WORM-TV.

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar learns some grouchy signs from his book "Signing for Grouches." Timi overhears him and suggests that she and Linda avoid his can, knowing he intends to just get them angry. Linda is certain she can handle Oscar and shuts her eyes as he signs, preventing him from having any effect.

altLabels.labelEn: Timi signs another day of WORM-TV programming
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Richard Hunt performs Baby Grouch, and the puppet built for the role would eventually be used for Irvine for all future appearances starting in season 14. Additionally, Martin P. Robinson announces the Grouch Weather Show for scene 4.

episodes.summaryEn: The grown-ups (Linda, Maria, David, Mr. Hooper and Timi) prepare for the Sesame Street Olympics, a mock-Olympics event they'll be doing with the help of their friends from the National Theatre of the Deaf. The opening ceremonies commence with the troupe acting out the lighting of the Olympic torch.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon and Bob are about to take the kids to the Day Care Center, when they see it's about to rain. Oscar pulls up in his Sloppy Jalopy and offers them all a ride to avoid getting wet.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird sees everyone reading newspapers in Hooper's Store. He asks David about some of the stories in today's paper and is appalled that there's not a single item about Sesame Street.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: At night, Telly observes the street is empty, then notices the lights on in the Fix-It Shop and assumes Luis must be working late. He leads the viewer to the shop so they can keep him company.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Though he claims Telly is the first to know his secret, Luis' writing hobby was previously referenced in Episode 1668, which was taped the day after this episode was recorded. Muppet Wiki note: In the script, the horse is identified as Fred the Wonder Horse. While Jerry Nelson utilizes the same voice and personality, a different horse puppet is used instead.

episodes.summaryEn: Telly can't make up his mind on what to have for breakfast. Big Bird offers him some birdseed and milk, which doesn't seem to suit him, nor does Oscar's yucky concoction (cold oatmeal with sardines and chocolate sauce), or Gladys the Cow's plan to eat grass and hay in the field.

David and Grandma Grace are surprised to hear samba music coming from Oscar's trash can. Oscar and Grundgetta are practicing for a dance competition, so Grace suggests she and David cut a rug to demonstrate.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Simon Soundman enjoys listening to Gordon's flute lesson with Bob. He wants to play along with them and demonstrates the various instruments he can imitate.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar enters the Grouch Auto Show
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob narrates as a Honker tries to talk to Darlene, who is deaf. Linda helps the Honker understand the situation and she helps introduce the two.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar has been sent Osvaldo's pet dog, Peligro, to give him some disobedience training. Maria isn't impressed by Peligro's lack of action as she's seen those tricks before, so Oscar reveals the newest trick - counting wrongly.
Maria asks a Honker about how they can express different feelings, since she's never quite sure how to interpret their honks. She paints a hypothetical situation that makes the Honker sad.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Additional performers include Brian Muehl, heard voicing a vendor during Oscar's basketball game.

episodes.summaryEn: Olivia helps the kids retrieve their frisbee from the arbor and sings "Reach Your Hand Up High."

David prepares a grilled cheese sandwich, when the Count enters the store and reveals he's just joined the local volunteer fire department. He counts the many things Hooper's Store has in case of fires, including the smoke detector, which goes off when David starts burning his sandwich.

Mr. Hooper observes Bob's music lesson with Marika and has a confession for Bob - he's always wanted to play the tuba and has been secretly practicing in the garage for the last two years, though he has little to show for it. Bob asks him to play a simple scale, but Mr. Hooper blows a horrid version of "Taps" instead, attracting Oscar the Grouch who asks for more.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: The Count presents the number 12 in several ways by counting 12 eggs in Susan's carton and 12 numbers on Olivia's broken clock. He asks Gordon to do 12 push-ups while he's out doing his exercise routine.
Mr. Hooper prepares for a visit from his brother, Arnold. He arrives moments later and calls attention to Mr. Hooper's small plant, which he'd noticed on his last visit.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)
