episodes.summaryEn: Herry Monster discovers that by just asking, he's able to join a group of kids playing.

altLabels.labelEn: Bob reads to the Two-Headed Monster
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: David deals with several cases of very fragile glassware in Hooper's Store. He must keep them safe from Maria (whose groceries can potentially bump into the boxes), Barkley (playing with his ball) and Big Bird (who skates through the store).

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria reluctantly allows Forgetful Jones to help her out in a situation - her friend is arriving any minute, but she has some work to do in the Fix-It Shop and needs Forgetful to keep watch. She gives him the important information he needs - her name is Sue, she'll have a guide dog with her (she's blind) that wears a harness, and that she'll wait at the stoop for Maria's return.

altLabels.labelEn: Maria's blind friend, Sue, pays another visit
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar has received many letters for "Ask Oscar" and Telly doesn't think he'll be able to tend to all of them. Telly has had the idea to send a response to the letters not read on air, but he knows Oscar would never go along with that.

altLabels.labelEn: Spot is Pig of the Week
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Luis and Jason run into Linda on their way to the zoo. Jason names the various animals they intend to see by making the signs for the others to guess.

As twilight begins, Telly greets the viewer and tells them what he just overheard - something is coming to Sesame Street, only Telly doesn't know what that something is. He notices lights going on, some going off, and kids running off.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Simon Soundman orders three turkey sandwiches and some milk at Hooper's Store using sounds. He's then shown to be having lunch with fellow sound-makers - a Honker and Dinger.
Mr. Snuffleupagus strolls down the block with the feeling that today is the day somebody on the street will see him. He discovers Slimey, who trembles with fear.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Olivia finds Big Bird pacing by the pay phone. He admits that he's supposed to have lunch at Mr. Snuffleupagus' place, but dreads having to eat cabbage again and doesn't know if he can bring himself to tell Snuffy this.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird calls Snuffy about lunch
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: A clip from Scene 1 later appeared in Episode 2096.

episodes.summaryEn: An unseen Howard Cosell-type announcer gives the play-by-play as Barkley tries to find shelter from a downpour. The Fix-It Shop is closed, a racket of pots and pans falling in Hooper's Store (caused by himself) frightens him away, and Oscar refuses to let him into his can.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Akim looks after Hooper's Store while her uncle David steps out for a minute. Bob orders a large meal and Big Bird wants to help Akim prepare the food.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Telly makes sure Maria sticks around to see the live show about to begin. Oscar appears from his can with his dummy, Crummy.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Aristotle demonstrates his great remembering skills for Maria, who initiates a remembering game. She hands him some items (a cowboy boot, a toothbrush, and a football) and he has to remember what they are a few moments later.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: A Muppet mail carrier (Richard Hunt) brings the morning mail to the residents of Sesame Street, including Maria, Susan, and Mr. Hooper. He's very pleased to see how much joy the mail brings everyone, except Bob, who is delivered a package of spring-loaded snakes from Oscar.

Bob and Big Bird play a guessing game using some clues a friend has loaned him. Big Bird guesses that his friend might be a mailman or a firefighter judging by the hat and badge, but finally guesses a policeman when Bob handcuffs himself to Big Bird.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird and Bob become handcuffed to one another
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Telly wants Oscar to teach him about subtraction, but Oscar is otherwise occupied with his elephant Daphne, who's fallen ill. Telly gets his lesson anyhow as Daphne slowly eats the five peanuts she's allowed to have in her condition.

Telly has been instructed by Oscar, as a part of his Grouchketeer duty, to learn the word printed on his sign - "NO." Telly doesn't know what the word means and becomes frustrated by Maria, Olivia and Bob's responses (thinking they're telling him "No" in response to his question). When Oscar asks if he's learned the word yet, Telly sadly admits, "No." Oscar gives him his approval, leaving Telly befuddled.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: A clip from scene 2 later appeared in Episode 2096.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird greets the viewers, and says that he is going to a place called Camp Echo Rock! The entire cast shows up to sing "Big Bird's Going to Camp."

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: The week of "Camp Echo Rock" episodes were taped over a 6-day period in August 1982 at Bear Mountain in New York. Muppet Wiki note: This was the only episode of the story arc not to be repeated in season 16, due to the street scenes with Mr. Hooper, a point after which it had been explained on the show that the character had passed away.

episodes.summaryEn: It's the first morning at Camp Echo Rock and Aunt Mae heralds it by (badly) playing “The Reveille” on the bugle to wake everyone up. Big Bird wakes from his makeshift nest and briefly forgets that he's not on Sesame Street anymore and he, Mickey, and the kids get up on time for breakfast... except for Rusty, who would rather sleep.

episodes.noteEn: Mr. Hooper's death is explained to Big Bird. Aired Thanksgiving, November 24, 1983; sponsors J, M and 5. The first-scene excerpt precedes the death discussion; it is not a synopsis of that later scene. Muppet Wiki note: All of Big Bird's drawings of his adult friends, including the famous Mr. Hooper picture, were drawn by Caroll Spinney, Big Bird's performer and a cartoonist in his own right. Muppet Wiki note: The staff considered, but ultimately rejected, the use of flashbacks with Mr. Hooper, citing that it would confuse children because, "for them, if something moves, it's alive." Later, Episode 2073, which aired the next season, featured a montage of freeze frames of Mr. Hooper. Conversely, in Episode 3611, aired in 1997, video flashbacks of Mr. Hooper are used when Big Bird reminisces about him. Muppet Wiki note: Researchers instructed the staff to not reference Mr. Hooper "going to the hospital," for fear that a child might worry if a loved one gets sick and goes to a hospital. They were similarly instructed not to say he died of sickness or due to old age. Muppet Wiki note: Several episodes made posthumous mentions of Mr. Hooper. Muppet Wiki note: Spinney admitted in 1984 that he was hesitant about Stiles writing the script. "Anyway, I was initially apprehensive because the writer who was assigned to this script is a very funny writer, a real yuk-yuk writer, but I was absolutely delighted with the depth and the warmth that he got into it."

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: In addition to performing Dr. Price, Brian Muehl provides the barking for his invention during scene 1.

episodes.summaryEn: Luis greets the viewer in Spanish. Forgetful Jones asks him what he just said.

Telly enters Hooper's Store, shopping for picnic snacks for all his friends, including Aristotle (and several others). David notices that Telly has written “banana” after every name on the list, and tells him to count the number of friends he has, which equals the number of bananas he needs (and the number of dimes he owes David).

At the Fix-it Shop, Luis writes an intergalactic action story on a typewriter, but repeatedly removes and crumples the paper he uses, then notices that Oscar has been watching him. Oscar has brought in a non-working flashlight for Luis to fix.
On his way to the department store, Gordon runs into Big Bird who asks to go with him. Grundgetta (poking out of Oscar's trash can) overhears them and attempts to guess what Gordon’s buying today.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird, Grundgetta, and Gordon go to the department store
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar hosts WORM-TV's Mystery Number Movie of the Day. Midway through their showing of The Mud Above and the Mud Below (a film of pigs set to organ music), Oscar dials the phone number of a lucky viewer who can win a year's supply of trash if they correctly guess today's number of the day - 6; Maria ends up being the unlucky contestant.
episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Grouch performers for the first scene include Martin P. Robinson (purple) and Richard Hunt (gray).

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird’s toe hurts because he’s stubbed it on a tricycle. He tells Olivia about this as she passes by, and she absently replies “That’s good!” He also tells Gordon when he jogs by, and Gordon responds “Terrific!” Big Bird observes that they didn’t listen to him, and doesn’t think Linda will listen to him because she’s deaf, but she understands him because he gestures towards his foot.
episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: During the "Forgetful Maria" scene, she calls Gordon "Roscoe."

episodes.summaryEn: David overhears Big Bird addressing the viewer on four ways one can count backwards from 10. David believes there's only the one way and demonstrates.
Bob finds Oscar typing away in his trash can. Oscar, wearing a writer's outfit, tells him that he's working on a play about trash to be performed today on Sesame Street.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar writes a play about trash
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: On Ask Oscar, Telly reads a letter asking about the importance of listening. Oscar drives Telly crazy by blatantly paying little attention to everything he says, forcing Telly to repeat the details over and over.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird trains Barkley to count to six by barking, but doesn't have much luck. He then imagines Barkley performing for a small audience as the world's smartest counting dog; wearing a mortarboard, he will bark up to any number when asked a question.
Telly Monster spots a kite stuck in a tree and tries blowing it down. When it doesn't work, Luis comes by and tries to jump to it, but he's not tall enough.
Bob and Susan sing "Little Baby Pigs," a country counting song, to the kids.

Dr. Nobel Price's latest "breakthrough" is a healthy meal one can start their mornings with. It just so happens to be "called" breakfast and the doctor asks the viewer to have it every day so they can grow up to be as smart as he is.
episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: The original script draft for the episode began with a scene not used in the final episode, where Oscar plays "Three of These Things" using himself and the Honkers.

episodes.summaryEn: It's early morning on Sesame Street and most of its residents are still asleep when Olivia investigates a large object covered in a tarp. Dr. Nobel Price comes running into frame declaring it as his new invention: a Balloon-a-Tune.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird shouts into Oscar's trash can, chiding him for something mean he said earlier. Bob asks Big Bird what he's angry about, but Big Bird insists he's not angry.
While Oscar looks for some Grouch literature at the library, Gilbert and Sullivan and the cast sing about what else he can find "At Your Library."

Big Bird tries to present today's sponsors, but Mr. Snuffleupagus gets in front of Big Bird and blocks his view of the audience at home. He teaches Snuffy the difference between front and back and requests Snuffy stay in back of him.

Mr. Snuffleupagus shows Big Bird his outfit for a pageant about the alphabet at Snufflegarden, where he's playing the letter X. He sings his part in the show, then heads off. Maria and Luis miss seeing him as they move a board, and Luis thinks Big Bird's imagination has gone too far when Big Bird mentions Snuffy is the letter X today.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird sees Mr. Snuffleupagus looking distraught as he stands by a several-foot-high trash can. Snuffy explains that his mommy wanted him to take out the trash before he came over to play, but he was so anxious to play that he forgot to leave it behind and brought it with him instead.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: The original script indicates additional segments between scenes 3 and 4 following the "Cousin Canny" cartoon, including "Beat the Time" with Cookie Monster, , Scanimate film #10, Simon's Song, and Pinball #10.

episodes.summaryEn: Bob begins a talk about the letter U, when the letter (performed by Richard Hunt) springs to life and starts egotistically talking about himself. As he lists off various words he begins and can be found in, Bob cuts him off to say there's not a lot of time for this talk.
Big Bird is hiding under a sheet in the middle of Sesame Street, trying to fool people. Susan comes out of 123 Sesame Street and recognizes him by his feet, so he crouches down.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria and Big Bird encounter Mrs. Honker and her young child. The mother proudly boasts (with Big Bird translating) how advanced her child is at such a young age, as the young Honker is able to count to 10.
Don Music wheels his piano into the library. He tells Maria he's looking for song ideas, then notices she's reading a book about France.

altLabels.labelEn: A day at the library with Don Music
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria and David try to catch the bus so that David can make a surprise visit to his grandma Grace on her birthday. David explains to Telly what a surprise is, and Oscar voices his displeasure of the situation.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Forgetful Jones approaches Luis working at the Fix-It Shop. To Luis' surprise, Forgetful greets him and speaks in fluent Spanish.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: "Do you ever have days when you just really want someone to hug you and kiss you and tell you that they love you?" Telly asks the viewer while seated in Hooper's Store. He's feeling that way today, but is too shy to ask Maria and David.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: David finds Forgetful Jones in need of some help. He claims Maria asked him to bring something up to Bob's apartment while she fixes his sink, but he can't remember what he needs.

Bob, Susan, and Gordon come outside at the crack of dawn, tracing the loud sound of an alarm clock to Oscar's trash can, where Telly Monster is waiting. He explains he's done this because of the story Sleeping Beauty, where the kingdom was put to sleep for 100 years.

Susan, Olivia, David, and Bob prepare to have a picnic in the park for an outdoor concert. Grundgetta brings them something else they might need - her portable radio, which broadcasts a Grouch weather report indicating rain.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Richard Hunt voices the weather Grouch on the radio in scene 1.

episodes.summaryEn: Forgetful Jones needs David's help in remembering what he came to buy from Hooper's Store. Forgetful has some clues to help the two out, namely a big pile of his cookware (even the kitchen sink).

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird has invented a new "B game" he wants to play with Susan, Olivia, and David. He holds a beach ball and tells them it serves as a clue for what he's going to do.
Luis listens to the radio for a bit before having to return to work. Elmo stops him from turning it off so he can dance to his favorite song.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Additional performers include Martin P. Robinson as the news reporter heard on Luis's radio.

episodes.summaryEn: After an encounter with Forgetful Jones, Maria imagines what it would be like to be just as forgetful as he is. Back in the present, David arrives to remind Maria about their lunch date, to which Maria responds, "Well golly, I guess I forgot!"

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: This episode would later be rerun as part of season 17, re-numbered 2105. In the re-airing, the Snuffy scene is cut due to the grown-ups meeting Snuffy by that time.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: In today's edition of Ask Oscar, Telly reads a question regarding the difference between quiet and loud. Oscar talks quietly to Telly, then shows off a pile of junk, which when tipped over, will cause it to fall.

episodes.summaryEn: Tough Eddie won't let Bobby, who's new in the neighborhood, play with him and Telly. Gordon convinces Eddie to give Bobby a chance and sings "Let Him Play," reflecting how when he was about Eddie's age he was welcomed into a new group of kids.

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: The original script for the episode includes two scenes not present in the broadcast episode. One scene involved Akim dealing with a string-tied Forgetful Jones, and later a scene in which she meets Forgetful's twin brother, Rememberful Jones.

In turn, when David reads a letter from his friend Bill, Big Bird says he's never seen him before and suggests that David made him up.

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: The end credit sequence for this episode was used for the HBO edit of Episode 1952. Muppet Wiki note: Brian Muehl performs the Grouches that appear as Grandma imagines what they would do with sour milk.

episodes.summaryEn: David waits for Telly to make a decision on what he wants for breakfast. Telly finally settles on fried eggs, but David says the store is out of them.

Linda and Timi meet a poor Honker who has hurt his nose and can't honk to communicate. They educate him on sign language and teach him to sign the entire alphabet, which can help him learn to spell words he can't sign.

Grundgetta presents the number 9, which she needs to ask a question that any non-Grouch will be unable to answer: what grouchy nursery rhyme involves the number nine? Maria and Luis are stumped, but two kids correctly guess that it's "Pease Porridge." Maria doesn't think the rhyme is all that grouchy, when Grundgetta retorts, "When was the last time you ate cold, nine day old pease porridge out of a pot, sister?"
The Honkers are in deep honk conversation when they notice the viewer and start honking even more and waving. Olivia comes by and asks what they're doing; they're so noisy.

episodes.summaryEn: Bob talks about a daydream he was just having and sings "Use Your Imagination."

Luis gives Telly Monster a plan on how to get Oscar the Grouch to help show one of today's letters - R. Telly loudly begins his talk to get Oscar's attention and asks Oscar not to help at all. The reverse psychology works, as Oscar produces a myriad of R-word items, thinking it will mess up Telly's talk.

episodes.summaryEn: Olivia sings "Who, What, Where, When, Why, How?" to two Anything Muppets in the yard.

episodes.summaryEn: It's night time on Sesame Street and the camera pans over to Oscar's trash can. Nearby pops Oscar the Grouch, its chief resident, who tells the viewer he's not going to reveal where Big Bird and everyone else are.

altLabels.labelEn: The adults begin to believe that Snuffy is real

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: This is the only season premiere episode from the first 20 seasons that was not included in Noggin's Sesame Street Unpaved package.

episodes.summaryEn: At the Library, teen staffer Micki tries to find a book for the Two-Headed Monster. She brings them a copy of "The Three Little Pigs," but one head doesn't like pigs.

episodes.summaryEn: Crystal approaches the outside window of Hooper's Store where she takes issue with David addressing her as "little girl." David says it's just a figure of speech and attempts to take her order, but Crystal is struggling with her backpack. David suggests she put it down, but Crystal is offended that David thinks she can't handle a heavy backpack; in fact, she's probably stronger than him.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar holds a Grouchketeers meeting, teaching them some Grouchy words, such as "rotten," "yucky," and "terrible." Buster the Horse appears and teaches him another word - "abominable," which he passes onto the kids. Maria is pleased he's learned a new word and gives him a kiss of congratulations, making him furious.

After having breakfast with Linda, Maria strolls through the yard, where Crystal and Mario have set up a picnic for some visiting Martians. When Maria asks how they know this, Crystal counters, "How do you know they're not?" They set out a welcome sign written in an alien language, some food, and juice.
episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Additional performers include Martin P. Robinson and Richard Hunt as the Martians. Muppet Wiki note: The footage of the Martian spacecraft landing on Sesame Street is recycled for the opening scene in Episode 2053.

episodes.summaryEn: Don Music has difficulty writing a song about one body part. Luis and some kids come over, and he asks them for help suggesting a body part.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: At Hooper's Store, the Amazing Mumford is ready to do his finest new trick - making the three ice cream sodas on the counter disappear. However, his trick instead makes the kids disappear one by one.

Big Bird drops by into Hooper's Store early in the morning and asks why David is there so early. He claims he's usually up early, but likes to come into store first thing and refill all the salt, pepper, and sugar shakers.

episodes.summaryEn: From outside his nest area, Big Bird opens the door and presents "The Small World of Mr. Snuffleupagus!" He joins the audience of kids as they watch Brianna help Snuffy form short words that start with the small letter "i." Snuffy concludes the presentation by stating, "It may not seem like much, but it's one small step in becoming a big-time reader!" to much applause.

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: In addition to performing his characters, Jerry Nelson is heard as the Monster on the Spot announcer.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

Uncle Wally explains that he couldn't hold the letter if he wasn't going to sing about it.

episodes.summaryEn: Luis proudly shows the viewer how well he's gotten at using his left hand while his right arm is in a cast. He pantomimes some actions, then uses his left hand to answer the phone, where an irate Oscar complains.

At the Fix-it Shop, Luis fiddles with a broken air tank he was planning to use to blow up some balloons for a party tonight. He asks Big Bird to watch the shop while he goes out and gets a new tank; while Luis is away, Snuffy comes by to fetch Big Bird for their play date in the park.

altLabels.labelEn: Luis breaks his arm — Luis needs help blowing up balloons
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Martin P. Robinson and Richard Hunt are among the performers voicing Grouches at Oscar's party.

episodes.summaryEn: Maria encounters a new face in the neighborhood - Shelley the Turtle, who has a problem. He can't tell Maria what it is because he has another problem: he's shy.

altLabels.labelEn: Shelley the Turtle looks for a home
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Micki welcomes the viewer to the Sesame Street library. Forgetful Jones walks in with a paper bag, saying it's to help him remember why he's come.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird reminds the viewer that Luis' arm has healed and his cast is gone. He wheels over a wagon full of activities so they can make up for all the playing they missed while Luis' arm was broken.

episodes.summaryEn: David is using the computer in the Fix-It Shop to manage supplies he's buying for Hooper's Store when Elmo (Richard Hunt) comes in and wants to play a game. David plays a few rounds of a rhyming game with him on the computer.

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar welcomes the viewer and shows off his great new invention: "Grouch earplugs." He's able to block out the pleasantries that he assumes Gordon and Susan are telling each other, when in reality the two are arguing about the important things they have to do today. Eventually, the couple makes up and figures out a compromise, and when Oscar's curiosity gets to him he removes the earplugs at the wrong time, hearing Gordon and Susan saying nice things before they leave.

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Elements from this episode's script are carried over from past shows, including Episode 1016, Episode 1081, and Episode 1157.

altLabels.labelEn: Having fun with a paper towel tube

episodes.summaryEn: Uncle Wally shows off a drawing of a friend he wants Bob and Big Bird to meet - Mrs. Snortleoutagus, who greatly resembles Big Bird's friend Mr. Snuffleupagus. The two go off to fetch their respective quadruped friends, while Bob laughs at how ridiculous this all sounds.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Luis introduces the viewer to his friend Carlos (Alexander Burgos), who is visiting all the way from Cuba. He wants to learn some English, so Luis is showing him around Sesame Street to help him out.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird is helping Maria fix a cuckoo clock, explaining to the viewer how it works by imitating it (popping in and out of the Fix-It Shop front door). Big Bird thinks some bird-to-bird talk will help fix it, but Maria thinks of something else.
episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Richard Hunt performs the cuckoo.

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar explains to Gordon that Slimey is thinking of becoming a carpenter, hence why he's currently hammering a nail into a piece of wood. Gordon wonders if he's too small, but Oscar counters that carpenter ants make out all right.

episodes.summaryEn: Bob sits in the yard with some kids and Elmo (Richard Hunt), playing a guessing game with sounds. Each player closes their eyes while someone else makes a noise (ripping paper, tapping a tin can, squeaking a balloon, or hitting a block) that the others have to guess.

altLabels.labelEn: Elmo makes noises / Big Bird and Snuffy's pictures

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon and Bob prepare to practice playing music outside when they hear the loud sounds of a trumpet, piano, and drum coming from the direction of Oscar's trash can. When Telly takes his turn, the entire machine short circuits, illustrating another busted C word - computer.

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar and the kids prepare his pet pig Spot for the Pork Stakes, a race that's about to occur in his trash can. After they make sure Spot is wearing his lucky number 2, David joins them as they watch the pigs race through mud, splattering everyone in the process.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Today is the first day of Oscar's Grouchketeer School, where Grouchketeers can learn to become better Grouchketeers. He describes it to Susan (blowing a dusty old book in her face) and the first lesson begins - the alphabet.

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: In addition to playing Telly, Martin P. Robinson performs a lady Anything Muppet waiting for the bus.

David wraps up the game after a few rounds, but he tells Elmo that he doesn't need a computer to play the same/different game and takes him to Hooper's Store.

Bob readies his apartment for Eugene, a young monster neighbor who will be sleeping over tonight while his parents are away. Although Eugene acts jovial when he arrives, he does admit that he misses his parents.

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Performers include Martin P. Robinson (as the Rockhead), Pam Arciero (as Aunt Shirley) and Kevin Clash (as Aunt Geraldine).

episodes.summaryEn: At Hooper's Store, Telly muses over what to have for breakfast as David serves Olivia her eggs. She is about to put some pepper on them, but Telly worries she might put on too much or something might be wrong with the shaker.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird observes Maria, Gordon, and Bob going about their business in the yard. He hopes that soon, one of them will leave so he can talk about subtraction, but none of them have any plans to move yet.

Big Bird goes into Hooper's Store and starts loudly counting backwards from ten to one for David; he then uses the store's phone to call Ernie and do the same. When David asks why, Big Bird explains that he wants to teach everyone how to count like that, as he likes it better than counting forwards because no matter where you start, you always end up back at 1.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria tests out a scale she's just finished repairing and delights that it works just fine. Forgetful Jones thinks the device is still busted, mistaking it for a clock.

Gordon sets aside some food, drinks, and other necessities next to a chair beside Oscar's trash can. Oscar asks him what he's doing, to which Gordon explains that he has agreed with Big Bird to meet Mr. Snuffleupagus today, and has planned everything so that he won't miss him.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: On Ask Oscar, Telly reads a letter with lots of "yes or no" questions. Oscar decides that being a Grouch, he will always answer each one with "no," using a sign to demonstrate it.
Big Bird and Mr. Snuffleupagus see Slimey inching his way to the park. Big Bird notes that Slimey is big enough that he can do it all by himself now.
episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: The Rockheads list the sponsors at the end as Q, Z, and 2, though none of the segments in this episode feature Z or 2 in a prominent role.

episodes.summaryEn: Uncle Wally stands on the sidewalk wearing a pair of rabbit ears, which he tells Bob were borrowed from Jill the Jackrabbit (a friend he met in the country) so he could find out what it's like to hear like a jackrabbit. As Wally hops off munching on a carrot, Bob finds the whole thing amusing... until he comes across Jill (Pam Arciero) as she looks for Wally.
Bob greets the viewer, when Uncle Wally comes by holding a gag dog leash. He claims it's holding his dog, Spot.
Telly shows Big Bird the early stages of his marble collection (just one). Big Bird wants to get a better look at it and reaches into the jar, but becomes unable to remove his wing from it.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Today, Slimey is helping Maria out in the Fix-It Shop, but she's not sure what he can actually do; everything she fixes is very big. Micki comes in with her deflated basketball, unsure of where the air leak is.

altLabels.labelEn: Slimey helps at the Fix-It Shop / Telly's magic words
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria shows Luis a postcard they've received from Forgetful Jones while on vacation. He tells them he's gone bike riding (which they picture him doing wrong) and roller skating (which he's done using his hands).
episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: In addition to performing Forgetful, Richard Hunt voices the offscreen "Monster on the Spot" announcer for Telly's report.

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar gathers all his "friends" (Susan, Gordon, Luis, David, Bob, Willy and three of the kids) to take a picture for his Grouch club. He asks them to move closer and closer together, until they're all concealed behind the lamppost.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: This episode's street scenes are remakes from previous episodes. The main storyline about firefighters was written for Episode 1086, with Big Bird in place of Telly. The first scene is remade from Episode 0904 and the last scene is a remake from Episode 0967.

episodes.summaryEn: Maria finds Oscar in the process of making a list to plan out his day. However, his list is not things he intends to do; it's things he's not going to do.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Mr. Snuffleupagus doesn't understand the difference between "here" and "there," so Big Bird sings a song to help him.
All is quiet on Sesame Street when suddenly, a spaceship lands in the yard. Pink and orange Martians materialize, and spot something in the distance...

altLabels.labelEn: The Martians cause trouble for Big Bird
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: The part of Scene 1 with Martians observing the computer would be used as a standalone segment in international productions, including Plaza Sésamo and Sesamstrasse.

episodes.summaryEn: Buster the Horse greets Gladys the Cow as his "sister," to which she objects. She launches into a song about how they're different, while Buster and his fellow horses sing about how they're the same.

altLabels.labelEn: Gordon agrees to visit Snuffy's cave
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Telly Monster wasn't ready for the viewer to arrive so soon. He wanted to surprise them with a poem, but he needs a word that rhymes with "street." Bob comes by listening to his walkman and suggests "beat" as a rhyme, but Telly has trouble contextualizing it in a poem about Sesame Street.
Oscar recruits Maria to help him with his Grouch exercises, namely chin-ups. He asks her to count them in Spanish, then asks her to hold up a broom to use as a bar.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar shows Gordon a box he has, which when opened produces a number of grouchy sounds. Each sound comes with a physical element, such as sawdust flying when a saw is heard or water squirting with a fire siren.
episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: In addition to performing the talking plant, Martin P. Robinson voices the sportscaster heard on Big Bird's radio. Muppet Wiki note: At the beginning of scene 4, Oscar can be heard singing a version of "Penthouse Serenade" to himself, replacing the titular penthouse to a junkyard.

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar starts today's Grouchketeer meeting, with new member Snuffy, who sports a giant trashcan lid for a hat. Oscar imagines that a lid that big must come from a giant trashcan, with giant trash!

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: After waking up, Big Bird welcomes the viewer and awaits his morning mail. He wonders what it would be like being a mailbox, and the scene transitions into his imagination.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird is exercising in the yard when he addresses the viewer: "Sometimes I wonder what it would be like to be really strong, like Wonder Woman or Herry Monster." He then imagines himself as Superbird, with a deep superhero voice and wearing a cape, gloves, and chest emblem. He carries a pile of bricks to Olivia, karate-chops some boards for her shelves, and opens a peanut butter jar for David.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Scene 2 is a rewritten version of a scene from Episode 1053. Scene 3 is a revised version of a scene involving Farley in Episode 1075.

episodes.summaryEn: Forgetful Jones and Olivia sing a song about sharing.
Oscar refuses to say "hello," but Telly tricks him into saying it by having him read "Hola" (the Spanish translation) on the sign that he gives him.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Kevin Clash provides the announcement for the Monster on the Spot segment.

episodes.summaryEn: Bob finds Oscar about to lead the Grouchketeers in a workout session he calls "Oscarcise." He calls himself the "Grouch Jane Fonda," then puts on a dance music record and everyone counts backwards from 11, completing the workout. Bob doesn't understand, so Oscar explains this is an exercise to strengthen an important body part - the mouth, so they can yell "Have a rotten day!" Bob spoils the fun by pointing out they also learned to count backwards from 11.

Big Bird welcomes the viewer and announces that today is the Sesame Street Pet Show, where neighborhood kids will bring their pets to his nest for everyone to see. Piri passes by walking his dog Max (who he nicknames "Cool"), and explains to Big Bird the responsibilities of owning a pet.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: The puppy held by Olivia in the last scene is Ed Christie's own dog, Lucas.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird skates down the block when he notices a woman he's never seen before skating past him. She introduces herself as Geri Jewell and explains that she may speak and move differently than Big Bird because she has cerebral palsy, but it doesn't keep her from doing other stuff.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Barker Oscar the Grouch introduces "Slimey the Wonder Worm," who will do a subtraction act. Oscar has two bananas and removes one, asking Slimey how many are left; Slimey forms his body to the shape of the number 1.

Forgetful Jones happens by Oscar's trash can and spots a sign on the can, but he doesn't know what it says. Oscar tells him it says "KEEP AWAY." He's continuously bothered by Forgetful, who keeps forgetting what the sign says.

altLabels.labelEn: Forgetful forgets how to read signs
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar asks Maria and Luis where his friend Carlos (Alexander Burgos) is, as they are going to tour the city seeing some Grouch sights. The two are skeptical of this, but Carlos thinks it will be fun.

altLabels.labelEn: Carlos goes on a Grouch tour
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: The front door to Hooper's Store hasn't been closing properly, so David helps Luis remove it from the hinges, then bring it to the Fix-It Shop for further inspection. Just as they get inside, Snuffy shuffles in and Big Bird calls his attention to the missing door.

altLabels.labelEn: Hooper's Store gets a new door
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Forgetful Jones is welcoming the viewers when Bob walks by carrying some books, and Forgetful tries to guess where he's taking them. Bob gives him some hints, but upon putting everything together, Forgetful assumes he's going to the laundromat.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: A painter (Ellen Greene) asks Oscar to keep an eye on her "WET PAINT" sign while she goes to get another paintbrush; Oscar reluctantly complies. David comes by and sees the sign, assuming it's part of Oscar's latest scheme, which Oscar denies.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird, Luis, Olivia, and Shay are at Gordon and Susan's apartment for dinner, waiting for Gordon to come home with Telly Monster. As Susan prepares "Susan's Special Stew," the lights suddenly go out.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: This episode was later repeated in season 18 as Episode 2247. The repeat omitted scene 4, as Snuffy has since been officially revealed to the cast by then.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird and Maria welcome the viewer when they come across Piri looking at the "Hooper's Store" sign, wondering why David's store would be called such. Big Bird doesn't understand why Piri can't remember Mr. Hooper, not taking into consideration the fact that he has only been on Sesame Street for a short time.

altLabels.labelEn: Remembering Mr. Hooper / Oscar's stop sign
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Big Bird's memories of Mr. Hooper, seen in still images, include Mr. Hooper taking Big Bird to the beach (though the image used is from a fantasy sequence in Episode 1443), assisting him with his lemonade stand (Episode 1300), teaching him how to pronounce his name (Episode 1307), and the Hooper Family Album. The letter is not specified as the time Big Bird went to camp since the week of episodes had originally aired during season 14, and had been repeated earlier during season 16 with Hooper's scenes being cut.

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon presents one of today's letters - Q (Richard Hunt). The letter is joined by his bothersome "little brother" U (Kevin Clash), who follows him everywhere.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar is giving away free old shoes. Susan wishes to take an old saddle shoe, but says it needs its match.
Piri teaches Big Bird and the kids how to do a moonwalk. In response, Big Bird teaches them how to do some beakdancing.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: As Maria greets the viewer, she becomes distracted by the sounds of Oscar laughing. He's revisiting his first grade reader book and recites some of it.
Susan and Telly are talking on the stoop of 123 Sesame Street when Susan notices Piri limping by. She inquires what the matter is, and he brushes his pain off as a splinter.
Big Bird wishes Luis, Gordon, the kids, Mr. Macintosh, Barkley, Olivia, and the viewer good morning. He sings "Good Morning Mr. Sun" afterwards.

Mr. Snuffleupagus tries to come up with ways he and Zoe are the same, but finds that Zoe lacks the many attributes of a Snuffleupagus. He comes to realize they both have two big, beautiful, dark eyes and is relieved.
Big Bird comes across a sad Honker, depressed that he doesn't know what to do. Big Bird takes this to mean what kind of job he wants.

altLabels.labelEn: The Grouch of the Year Award
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Forgetful Jones and Olivia are sitting together when Forgetful addresses her as "Maynard." Olivia is upset he can't remember her name and tries to teach him things to think of when trying to remember her name (something you eat - an olive, something you scream - "Eee!", and something you say when you can't remember - "Uh.") Forgetful eventually nails the pattern down until he finally addresses Olivia as "Potato Chips Wahoo-uh!" "Just call me Fred," Olivia mutters.

altLabels.labelEn: Snuffy imagines himself as a cloud
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Susan is shocked to hear Oscar say that saying "hello" makes him feel happy. He explains through song that when one says hello, it's soon time to say "goodbye" ("Hello, I Must Be Going").
Everyone is setting up a party for Telly Monster's birthday, but Telly is nowhere to be found. Meanwhile, Telly is seen sitting on a bench in the park.

altLabels.labelEn: Telly tries to wait out his birthday
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: David is strolling along the street when he finds Forgetful Jones wearing a pair of earmuffs around his hat, naturally forgetting where they're supposed to go. David gives him a few hints, and Forgetful tries putting them on his nose and eyes until David finally corrects him and puts them on his ears.
Olivia sees Oscar leading Slimey in a workout session. Slimey practices shaking his head (to say "no") and moving back and forth (to inch away from bothersome neighbors).

While reading "How to Be a Great Detective," Telly learns about employing disguises. He dons a dark beard and attempts to listen in on Olivia and Maria's conversation about the weather, but he's instantly recognized.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Dr. Nobel Price shows David his latest invention - the Question-Answerer, a device that can answer any question. However, the only answer it is able to give is the word "COLD," regardless of what question is asked.
Gordon, Susan, Bob, Telly Monster, and the kids gather around Oscar's trash can to hear Oscar tell them a story, particularly the day he first arrived on Sesame Street.

altLabels.labelEn: How Oscar came to Sesame Street
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria checks in with Oscar to see what's new in the world of Grouches. He informs her that he's looking for a job, but finds nothing suitable in the want ads of his newspaper.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob gets up early to go for a morning jog around Sesame Street. While he's gone, Maria, Susan, David, and Luis (with his guitar) gather under his apartment window to surprise him by singing a new song he's written.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Performers for the movie patrons in scene 2 include Pam Arciero (Grouch and Reddish-Magenta AM) and Kevin Clash (monster).

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird has been left to watch the STOP sign belonging to Mrs. Robinson (Rosetta LeNoire), the crossing guard. He tests it out on Luis, Maria, and the kids, finding they stop when he flashes it.

Oscar conspires with a Honker to play a trick on Telly in the guise of a game. Oscar points out the letter C on the Honker's hat and if Telly correctly guesses the C word they're thinking of, they'll buy him an ice cream cone; a wrong answer means he'll be pelted with old paper.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar and a Honker trick Telly

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon prepares his breakfast, which Elmo tries to turn into a game of some sort. He realizes that since he's already had his breakfast, Gordon will have to play it alone.

episodes.summaryEn: While cleaning his nest, Big Bird tells the viewer that everyone has gone downtown except for him and Susan, who is busy watching a football game. He also states that Barkley is around, but can't find him.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird reveals to Snuffy that something special is going to happen today: all his grown-up friends will finally get to meet his best friend face-to-face! Big Bird explains how tired he is of hearing everyone humor him about his "imaginary friend," and a flashback montage is shown of the adults admonishing Big Bird, who insists that the Snuffleupagus is real.

episodes.noteEn: Season 17 premiere; the adults finally meet Mr. Snuffleupagus. Sesame Workshop independently dates this change to 1985. Muppet Wiki note: The flashback montage in Scene 1 features clips from (in order of appearance) Episodes 1585, 1940, 1726, 1854, 1780, 1934, 1697, and 1705. Muppet Wiki note: This episode marks the debut of a revised, up-tempo version of the music that often accompanies Snuffy when he enters a scene. This also reflects a change in Snuffy's character, who doesn't quite do or say things as slowly as he used to from this point on. Muppet Wiki note: The episode's plot was established as early as July 1985, as Big Bird alluded to it during a promotional interview for Follow That Bird, saying "pretty soon, I think everybody's gonna meet him, I'm hoping."

episodes.summaryEn: In the early morning, Snuffy stops by Big Bird's nest, unable to sleep from the thrill of meeting everyone yesterday. A thought then occurs to him - he wonders if it really happened, or if he just imagined it.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Snuffy wants to introduce Big Bird, Maria, Bob, Luis and Gordon to his new friend, but isn't sure how to do it since he just recently became friends with the grown-ups himself. Maria explains how easy the process can be, so Snuffy tells the group how to gently address his friend Mr. Anteloper - whom Snuffy reveals to be a stuffed toy.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon is sitting on the stoop of 123 Sesame Street and reminisces with the viewer (in a flashback montage) about a time where he sat by Oscar's can and waited all day for Mr. Snuffleupagus. He decides he could take a walk over to Snuffy's cave so he could get to know him better, and brings the viewer along with him as he follows directions as written on a note.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Telly Monster speaks in whispers as Gordon is asleep nearby in the yard, having stayed up late grading papers. The two were supposed to have lunch together, but Telly doesn't see how this can work if Gordon is sleeping.
episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: This is the first episode since season 11 to use scrolling credits. (Seasons 12 through 16 used static credits.) Muppet Wiki note: The original script for scene 4 also had Maria pointing Big Bird toward another listing, which is the closing sponsor announcement. Big Bird doesn't find this funny either, but Maria responds, "I know, but it had to be said."

episodes.summaryEn: Bob comes across Oscar's trash can, which has now been converted into an ice creamery. Oscar advertises his nine different flavors, all beginning with the letter S - Salami, Salmon Salad, Sardine, Sauerkraut, Sausage, Scallion, Sour Cream, Spaghetti and Spareribs.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird and Snuffy declare today as "Best Friends Day," and plan to celebrate together with a picnic in the park; Snuffy had even brought his baseball mitt to play catch. episodes.noteEn: Gordon and Susan adopt Miles, as identified by the episode plot label. Muppet Wiki note: The story of Miles' adoption is often cited as one of the landmark moments for the series, along with the death of Mr. Hooper, Maria and Luis's wedding, and Gabi's birth. As such it was included as one of the few historical moments visited by Grover and Elmo in the anniversary special The Street We Live On. Muppet Wiki note: Over 20 years later, in 2006, Sesame Street revisited the issue of adoption with the addition of Marco, the son of Gina. The story of Marco's adoption was addressed in episodes 4130, 4131, and 4132. Muppet Wiki note: A portion of scene 2 appears on Sesame Street: 20 and Still Counting.

episodes.summaryEn: Everybody on Sesame Street prepares for Miles' arrival in their own ways. A deliveryman (Martin P. Robinson) drops off extra diapers and baby food for David at Hooper's Store, while Maria and Luis set up a play pen by the tire swing, much to Barkley's delight.

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: This episode can be viewed at the University of Georgia.

episodes.summaryEn: Susan and Gordon welcome the viewer to Sesame Street, and explain their process of baby-proofing the apartment in order to keep little Miles safe. They're taking any breakable objects and placing them on the shelf out of Miles' reach.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: "Explorer Jones" and the kids (including Tatyana Ali) pretend to be explorers. They're looking for the alphabet, but Forgetful doesn't know what it looks like.

altLabels.labelEn: Dr. Price invents the square ball

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon asks Piri, Big Bird, and Mr. Snuffleupagus to watch Miles while he goes to get his dry cleaning. Big Bird and Snuffy try to find ways to keep Miles amused, but their joke telling and dog imitations don't work very well.

altLabels.labelEn: Uncle Wally recalls his sailor days

episodes.summaryEn: The Count recruits Maria to help him in "Counting Toes."

It has just finished raining on Sesame Street, and Telly finds himself admiring the pitcher of rainwater he just collected. He tries to tell Oscar, who doesn't see why he should care about how important water is.
Oscar hands Telly Monster the sheet music for his new song, "Q is for Quick," accompanied by his pet elephants. Telly sings it through once, but Oscar thinks it should sound faster.

Telly Monster and a few kids hear some unique vocalizing; sounds they've never heard before on Sesame Street. They approach what Telly describes as "some kind of bird," a simplification the voice objects to, who introduces himself as Placido Flamingo from Santo Domingo, world famous opera star.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird, an Anything Muppet kid (Pam Arciero), Desiree, Elmo, and Gladys the Cow welcome the viewer one word at a time. However, Buster the Horse, who is supposed to say "Street," isn't present.

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: The film footage used for Telly's imagination is originally from one of .

episodes.summaryEn: Forgetful Jones explains to Maria that he’s labeled all his body parts so he won’t forget them, but she points out that he’s labeled them incorrectly (“Hubba-wha?” he responds). She puts the "nose," "ear," "cheek," and "finger" labels in the right places, but Forgetful lets her have his spare “nose” sign.

Big Bird greets David at the door of Hooper's Store and says he can't tell him anything about the surprise waiting for him inside. But, through a series of unsolicited and inadvertent clues, David figures out that it's his Grandma Grace.

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar the Grouch loves the early morning because there are a multitude of sounds he gets to enjoy (such as garbage trucks, street construction, radios, barking, etc.).

Mr. Snuffleupagus wants to play football with Slimey, but Oscar thinks the size difference will make the game unfair to Slimey; he suggests hide and seek instead. Snuffy looks everywhere on Sesame Street and can't find Slimey.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird observes Uncle Wally and the kids as they prepare to climb up a mountain. They check to see if they have all of their supplies while Big Bird glumly watches.

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Kevin Clash, Bill McCutcheon, and Martin P. Robinson are among the voices heard during scene 3. The names called out include John-Boy and "Ralphie-boy!"

episodes.summaryEn: At Hooper's Store David greets Jiffy the turtle, who comes in for breakfast. Jiffy speaks very slowly, so David makes sure Gordon and Linda have everything they need - this could take a long time.

episodes.summaryEn: Maria and Luis welcome the viewer in Spanish, then Big Bird - or rather, "The Amazing Birdford," greets them. Big Bird has borrowed the Amazing Mumford's magic kit and is learning how to become a magician.

Oscar hosts "Real Grouches," the show that showcases talented Grouches from around the world. First, Romeo Scuggs shows how he can play his screechy violin in-between shouting "Scram!" Then, Luba Merquit performs a song on a screechy blackboard.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Biff supervises as Sully drills the sidewalk outside 123 Sesame Street. Gordon comes to the window, begging them to stop, as baby Miles is going to be taking his nap.

episodes.summaryEn: Maria greets the viewer, when a panicked Telly alerts her that something has happened to Desiree. Maria goes over to investigate, and Elmo says her tooth has come out.

Big Bird and Snuffy pretend to explore Sesame Street, imagining it's their first time seeing it. They observe an "umpadumpus tree," meet some friendly native "Sesame Streetians" speaking "Sesamese" and attempt to communicate with them and learn their customs, and encounter a wild animal (Barkley).

episodes.summaryEn: Uncle Wally and Bob are up very early to go jogging with Gordon. Bob remains groggy and falls asleep standing up as Wally and Gordon converse.

episodes.summaryEn: Maria, Gordon, and the kids see Forgetful Jones has a new, large hat. He was given it by Clementine, claiming it would be so big he'd never forget it.

Big Bird explains that if Snuffy goes looking for him, he'll see the note left, reading, "Dear Snuffy, Big Bird and Bob went to a..." with Gladys the Cow and the letter V beside it, to which she would moo after the note is read and point to the letter V - reading "moo-V."

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird brings Luis a floppy disk to load on the computer in the Fix-It Shop while Snuffy looks on from outside (he couldn't fit through the door). The disk contains an encyclopedia of "upagusses" which Big Bird finds fascinating.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird and the Birdketeers show the viewer how "You Can Be a Birdketeer."

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Additional puppeteers include Martin P. Robinson as Scuzette and Kevin Clash as Bertha. Muppet Wiki note: Producer and director of the episode Lisa Simon later commented that the show "went too far" by featuring a human punk rocker for the show. Joan Ganz Cooney, who watched from home long after the episode had gone through the writing and production process, suggested that the Tanya character never be used again, stating that it "was not an image the show wanted to promote." Simon continued, "We were trying to keep current. We have to keep in mind that it really isn't a New York show."

episodes.summaryEn: Dr. Nobel Price yells out on the street to everyone about his new invention. Maria and Luis come out of the Fix-It Shop to see his new alphabet, which he calls the "Price-phabet." He explains the only difference it has from the regular alphabet, is that the letter Z is replaced with a little smiley face named Fred, which makes no sound.

episodes.summaryEn: Barkley follows Big Bird as he carries a basket over to the yard. Inside the basket is Rhymena the Rhyming Cat (Pam Arciero), which David finds unbelievable.
Olivia discovers a door in the middle of Sesame Street with an "entrada" sign on it. Dr. Nobel Price boasts this is another invention of his, but Olivia points out the door doesn't go anywhere.

episodes.summaryEn: At the Fix-it Shop, Jason watches Maria attempt to fix a clock. He offers to help but she doesn’t think he could help her around the shop.

episodes.summaryEn: Telly prepares Elmo to welcome the viewer, but Elmo doesn't know what the word "welcome" means. Telly finds he can't describe what it means to him, so he runs off to find someone who can help him.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird has asked Gladys the Cow to help say hello to the viewer, but she balks at a cow of her talent being wasted on such a menial task. episodes.summaryEn: Susan asks Telly to go to her car and retrieve Miles' toy from the front seat. Telly runs back and forth, asking questions about how to open it, which key to use, and which plaything to bring back.
In song, Big Bird shows Elmo the difference between "Big and Small."
Slimey enters the new worm movie theater to see Gone with the Worm. Oscar encourages him to spoil his appetite on movie snacks, and peeks in to watch as well...

episodes.summaryEn: Snuffy sets up a proscenium in the yard with help from Daniella and Naoika, and Bob tries to guess what's going on. Big Bird enters with a script, asking for advice on which voice he should use to read it.

episodes.summaryEn: Luis is swamped with work at the Fix-It Shop, and Maria is too busy reading her book - The Adventures of Captain Swashbuckle - to help. She walks in and sees David, who explains to her he doesn't speak Spanish, but since Piri called in sick he decided to call an agency who'll bring him someone who speaks Spanish, of which he is awaiting.

Linda comes by to congratulate his rare instance of excellent memory in sign language.

episodes.summaryEn: David procures 12 ping-pong balls for Telly. He asks why Telly would need so many, and Telly begins his lengthy explanation: he's going to visit his Granny Monster, who has a ping-pong table at home.

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Oscar repeatedly uses the word "abominable" during his scene - a word he previously learned the year before.

episodes.summaryEn: While planning to clean out his nest, Big Bird realizes he needs to return some books to the library, so he and Snuffy walk on over before it closes. Upon arrival, they see that they're quite busy today.

Slimey turns the apple again and again to mimic the Earth's rotation, going faster and faster making Oscar dizzy.
episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Some of the wishes on Big Bird's list written but not mentioned include: Muppet Wiki note: I wish Herry Monster would join the "Y." Muppet Wiki note: I wish that Christmas was tomorrow. Muppet Wiki note: I wish that I could fly. Muppet Wiki note: I wish that Maria could make birdseed chili. Muppet Wiki note: I wish all the graffiti in New York would vanish. Muppet Wiki note: I wish that it were spring.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird notices Gordon bouncing baby Miles on his lap in the yard when he asks Gordon to play. Gordon explains to Big Bird that he can't play at the moment because he's busy playing with Miles.

Oscar sees a little bit of Grouch in this child after all, and encourages Miles to keep playing and suggests more things for Miles to imagine the boxes as.
