episodes.summaryEn: Biff and Sully take a break from doing some building work out on the street. As Biff tries to trade lunches with Sully, they see Barkley run past, followed by Linda with his leash, unaware of where he went.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Forgetful Jones is at the Fix-It Shop to remind Luis about taking him to lunch in honor of today's holiday - Take a Cowboy/Cowgirl to Lunch Day. To Luis' surprise, Forgetful is able to remember every little detail when Luis agreed to take him last week (even what Luis wore), explaining he made sure to mark the date on his calendar.

altLabels.labelEn: Take a Cowboy/Cowgirl to Lunch Day
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: This episode was later repeated in Season 20 as Episode 2505. Muppet Wiki note: The date on Forgetful's calendar for Take a Cowboy/Cowgirl to Lunch Day is marked on February 13 - the exact day the episode originally aired in 1987. Muppet Wiki note: Additional performers include Martin P. Robinson (Pumpkin cowboy), Pam Arciero (horse), Michael Elizabeth Huston (Grouch cowgirl and Green cowgirl), Jerry Nelson (Lavender cowboy and sheep), and Fran Brill (Lavender cowgirl), with Richard Hunt (sheep).

episodes.summaryEn: Maria greets the Count, but tells him she doesn't have time for him to count her toes or anything like that. He assures her that lately, he's focusing less on counting and more on writing poetry.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: A tango flavored version of the theme plays (instead of the regular opening music) as Luis carries some empty boxes over to the Fix-It Shop and accidentally drops them after walking into the closed door, thinking it was open. He complains about it in English and Spanish, which captures the attention of Placido Flamingo, who performs his "Naughty Door Opera" about a similar experience he went through.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria stops by Hooper's Store to get a newspaper from teenage helper Jason (Alexis Cruz), running into Barkley along the way. At the Fix-it Shop, the Amazing Mumford reveals he will attempt a trick he's never tried before: he will make Barkley quack like a duck, and make a Muppet duck bark like a dog.

altLabels.labelEn: Maria falls victim to the Amazing Mumford's trick
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: In later episodes, when Maria encounters Mumford, she tries to keep her distance from him, often citing his duck trick as the key reason for her not trusting him. One such example occurs in Episode 2341.

uploads.extentNoteEn: The file label marks this episode incomplete within the block.

episodes.summaryEn: Nikya assists the Two-Headed Monster as he presents the number 2 by counting each of their body parts that come in pairs.
Forgetful Jones thinks of ways of remembering, as visions of Maria, Luis, and Gordon appear with a musical, vaudeville message - "Write It Down."

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Biff tells the viewer that they're going to play a fun game today. Elmo wants to play, so Biff initiates a guessing game with Elmo regarding the game they'll be playing.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Everyone is gathered in the yard to talk about times when they were afraid.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: The music box tune that plays to substitute the Count's thunder and lightning is "I Could Have Danced All Night," which he and the Countess would parody later as "I Could Have Counted All Night."

episodes.summaryEn: As Big Bird and Snuffy color, a young girl approaches them and says something in Spanish, but the two can't understand her. A Honker arrives and knows how to speak Spanish.

Gordon, Susan, Elmo, and Telly Monster are going to cooperate and make up a story one word at a time, which Oscar scoffs at. Barkley seems to derail the proceedings by barking, but Susan incorporates his barks into the story any way.

Maria and Elmo are having some grape juice together, as Elmo slurps his up quickly. He then wants to play a "clink-clink" game with Maria, where she must repeat the sounds he makes by clinking his glass.
Big Bird needs ten cents to buy a special present before he and his friends can play. He has four pennies, Snuffy has four as well, and Jeffrey has two, all totaling ten cents.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Dr. Nobel Price sets up a film projector in order to conduct an experiment to find what kind of movies Barkley likes. Bob and Linda aren't sure dogs like movies, but Dr. Price is determined to find an answer, considering moving to Hollywood to pursue a career in dog-targeted cinema.

altLabels.labelEn: Dr. Price looks for movies with canine appeal
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob plays a guessing game with Big Bird about what he has behind his back. Given the clues, Big Bird is able to correctly guess it's a toy firetruck, and he dances around humming the victorious Rocky theme.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Hoots the Owl plays some jazz for Athena before they must leave to open Birdland. Athena wants to hear more and begs for one last note.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: A portion of the opening scene was included in Being Elmo: A Puppeteer's Journey. Muppet Wiki note: One of the outfits Hoots wears in his old photos is a brown vest, which the character would eventually always wear beginning in Episode 2342. Muppet Wiki note: Kevin Clash performs Tooter in scene 3, telling Olivia it's "five minutes to curtain." Muppet Wiki note: The jazz version of the "Sesame Street Theme" used during Olivia and Athena's duet was originally recorded for the Tonight Show-inspired scenes from the VHS Learning About Numbers.

episodes.summaryEn: David prepares a bowl of hot cereal with cinnamon and raisins. Oscar comes by for breakfast and David offers the cereal, even though Grouches don't go for that kind of food.
Simon Soundman is out for a stroll on such a lovely day. He suddenly finds himself party to Susan's hectic rush to meet Gordon at the bus stop.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gladys the Cow comes to the Fix-It Shop to have her clock repaired. Luis hears it making a normal "tick-tock" sound, but Gladys claims it's supposed to go "tick-tock-moo." Luis makes an adjustment and the clock makes the sound.

Chip and Dip take offense when Bob can't tell the two apart. He sings a song about his perspective of the situation ("You Are You"), but promises to be more mindful of their differences in the future.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Olivia plays a pattern game with Zoe using some more kids and a few Honkers.

Oscar and Grundgetta prepare to watch the Amazing Mumford perform a Grouch magic trick he learned from the Great Trasherini. Gordon, though he is about to leave with Susan on a date, agrees to assist in the trick as Mumford changes lovely-looking shapes into Grouchy ones.

altLabels.labelEn: Mumford turns Gordon into a Grouch
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon goes through a stretching routine in the yard during the early morning and explains to the camera that he like so get up this early because there's very little traffic and it's a pretty time of the day. He invites the viewer along for a jog, which is set to a spoof of the Chariots of Fire music, and consists of a montage of Gordon running through the city.
episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: The original script for this episode contains several original street scenes involving Maria, Elmo, Oscar, Gordon, the Grouchketeers, Big Bird, Barkley, Bob, and Mr. Snuffleupagus. Of the eight scenes originally scripted for the episode, only the scene involving Telly and Micki appears in the broadcast version. See Unproduced Sesame Street episodes for the unused material. Summary quotes the first listed insert because this page does not label any row SCENE 1. Its notes document extensive script-to-broadcast changes.

episodes.summaryEn: Linda is seen looking around for something... but what is it? Meanwhile, Gordon comes out of 123 Sesame Street about to do some errands, kissing Susan before he leaves.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Susan and Forgetful Jones watch Gordon play ball with Miles and some kids. Oscar the Grouch points out that Miles is growing, and watching him play ball reminds Oscar of a special time when he was a little Grouch...

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird and Mr. Snuffleupagus agree to play hide-and-seek and both conceal themselves behind the garage steps, not realizing nobody will be seeking them. Big Bird decides to be the seeker and Snuffy joins him, only now they have no one to find.

Maria comes out of 123 Sesame Street and finds Olivia at the bottom of the stoop, dressing as if it's going to rain. She tells Maria she's getting ready to take some pictures of Fluffy's birthday party in Oscar's trash can.
episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Performers heard during Fluffy's birthday party include Kevin Clash and Richard Hunt. Most of the other crowd noises heard during the party were originally recorded for the Riverbottom Nightmare Band.

episodes.summaryEn: Telly is hesitant to open a letter he's received, as he doesn't know who sent it to him. He thinks it might contain such bad news as Elmo telling him he broke his toy fire engine or Mr. Macintosh saying he's all out of broccoli.
Olivia welcomes the viewer and invites them to go shopping with her. Placido Flamingo appears and presents her with the new opera he's written, explaining what an opera is in song.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Throughout most of the episode, Olivia refers to Placido as "Maestro Flamingo" rather than saying his name.

episodes.summaryEn: Maria disposes of some trash on a nice, quiet morning on Sesame Street, when Oscar's trash can loudly emits the sound of an alarm clock. Oscar, annoyed by the sound, tosses it from the can and Maria catches it.
episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Many of the scenes are remakes form older episodes, or would later be remade for future shows. Scene 1 is originally from Episode 0707, scene 5 is a rewritten version of scene 3 in Episode 1062, Mumford and Luis' scene originated in Episode 1213, and scene 2 would later be remade for Episode 2984 (with Roxie Marie replacing Sully).

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird and Mr. Snuffleupagus are preparing for their big adventure in Big Bird's nest. Snuffy is wearing a backpack and brought his bathing trunks in case they go swimming, a telescope in case they climb a mountain and want to look down below, and a bulb horn in case they come across a lion and want to let him know that they're there.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird and Snuffy adventure across the street
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird shows Snuffy his notebook, which he uses to draw pictures. He drew a picture of Snuffy with the words “Snuffy always smells,” to which Snuffy takes great offense.
Big Bird and Mr. Snuffleupagus sing about "Playing Pirates" as they pretend to look for imaginary treasure.
Olivia wants to take some pictures of the inside of Oscar's trash can. Oscar at first refuses, but permits her to do so provided she leave him alone afterwards.
Maria and Lauren find rectangles hidden in a picture of a sorcerer's workshop.
Bob and Elmo (who had just slept over at Bob's place) look out on the morning and greet the viewer. Elmo notices Linda walking Barkley to the yard to read her newspaper.
episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Scene 2 is a rewrite of an Episode 1131 scene, while scene 3 is a remake of a scenario from Episode 1145.

episodes.summaryEn: Elmo doesn't understand why Maria would speak to Barkley in Spanish if he can't understand it. She tells him that he may not understand the words, but he can understand the emotional tone of what she's saying.
episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: During his scene with David, Don's framed picture of Joe Raposo sits near the counter of Hooper's Store rather than on his piano. Muppet Wiki note: Don's attempt at soft music includes snippets from "As Time Goes By," "Call Me Irresponsible," "The Shadow of Your Smile," and "I Left My Heart in San Francisco."

episodes.summaryEn: On the steps of 123 Sesame Street, Gladys the Cow talks with Susan and the kids about a dance audition, when Sherlock Hemlock and Elmo (learning how to be a detective) announce that they're on the case to solve who left a footprint on Sherlock's newspaper. They compare everyone's shoes to the oddly-shaped print and discover it belongs to Gladys, who admits she must have stepped on the newspaper when she was practicing for her audition.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Susan discovers three letter X's in a row on the doors to Big Bird's nest. Likewise, Oscar the Grouch has three X's on and around his trash can and David spots three more written on the sidewalk.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Telly is in a frenzy trying to find things relating to today's sponsors - K, P, and 2. Bob tries to introduce him to Pete Seeger and his grandson Kitama, but Telly is too busy to fully engage.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Scene 3 is a recreation of a performance from Pete Seeger's first appearance on Sesame Street. Muppet Wiki note: During scene 3 Oscar refers to Pete Seeger as "Mr. Cigar," a play on his name. He previously referred to him accidentally as "Pete Cigar" in Episode 0108, while Big Bird had called him Mr. Cigar in Episode 0203.

episodes.summaryEn: The Miami Mice arrive at the Fix-It Shop with a problem only Maria can solve - Tito's sunglasses have broken. He refuses to de-shade so Maria can properly fix them however, as it would ruin their fashionable reputation.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: As Telly recalls which monster friends Mr. Attenbird describes, the scene briefly cuts away to a segment featuring each one. For Cookie Monster, it's his visit to the carnival, for the Two-Headed Monster it's arguing whether to sleep or practice the trumpet, and for Grover it's arriving to serve his customer at Charlie's Restaurant.

episodes.summaryEn: Tanya helps Elmo count to five in Spanish. He then asks for a "hug in Spanish," pleased to see it feels the same in Spanish and English.

Elmo pretends to mail a package, with Oscar acting as representatives of both the Grouch Post Office and the information booth. After visiting both windows to get the information he needs, Oscar tells him they can't send his package - the post office is closed.
As Maria tries to read, the Count annoys her by counting every time she blinks.

Bob tends to some of his crocus plants, noting that spring is in the air at last. Telly comes by with a problem - he planted his own crocus bulb in the winter, but he's discovered a nasty green thing is starting to take up space in the flower pot.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: The Count and the kids, all dressed in athletic gear, get ready for the big counting marathon, where they count to 40 together.
episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Voices for the cheerleading bats include David Rudman, Pam Arciero, Kevin Clash, and Jerry Nelson.

episodes.summaryEn: Luis helps Gladys the Cow by tuning her radio to her favorite station, “Moo-Moo-Moo FM” (as she's all hooves). He tunes the dial to “Moo FM” where they hear only one moo, then to “Moo-Moo FM,” which has two moos.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Today on Ask Oscar, Oscar answers a query from Elvira Nasty from Sludge Falls, IL, who wants to know what the word "important" means. Oscar explains it's important for him to be a Grouch, so he starts listing all the important (and terrible) things he wants to happen to Elvira.

Oscar and Grandpa Grouch have returned from collecting trash at the dump and toss their findings onto the Fix-It Shop workbench, to Maria's chagrin. They intend to bring it all over to Oscar's trash can, so Oscar pulls out a small box to carry the trash.

The Count counts Big Bird’s feathers (again) when Maria passes by on her way to a two-day camping trip. When he learns there are new things to count in the wilderness, he decides to join her (to her dismay), and leaves Big Bird in charge of counting things around Sesame Street while he's gone.

altLabels.labelEn: The Count and Maria go camping
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: This episode's plotline is a direct remake of Episode 1219.

episodes.summaryEn: Mr. Snuffleupagus is about to greet the viewer when the Count interrupts him, telling him that his fur is not neat. He assembles a team of eight fur combers (with large combs) to comb every part of Snuffy's fur.

David discusses exercise with the kids as Bob and Big Bird run around the block. The runners stop by Hooper's Store and Big Bird learns what "perspiration" means when they see how much Bob is sweating.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Uncle Wally sorts through a box of old things to see if Oscar would be interested in anything. He comes across some of his cowboy stuff and recalls to Maria and the kids about his youth working as a cowboy, helping herd cattle.

altLabels.labelEn: The Amazing Mumford reverses Maria's age
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon spots Big Bird and the kids preparing a present for Granny Bird's birthday. Big Bird shows off the small birdhouse that Maria made for him intended as a guesthouse for Granny, and the kids wrap it with wrapping paper - a real "wrap party." Maria announces the sponsors.
episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Big Bird's reference to the "wrap party" is an inside joke - this was the last episode recorded for season 18.

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar introduces David to Slimey's new pet stick, Sticky. David believes a stick can't be a pet as it's not even alive.
Bob notices Uncle Wally and the kids waiting on the stoop, holding pennants with the letter A on them. Wally says they're waiting for a parade, and a parade consisting of sparkly letter As passes by.
Susan welcomes the viewer, when she hears The Count yelling, "EXTRA! EXTRA!" He's delivering copies of The Daily Count, a newspaper of his own creation.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria presents Oscar with a box of things she's throwing away - a chipped jug, and a holed bucket and sock. Maria realizes she can find alternate uses for them (the jug as a lamp, the bucket as a flowerpot, and the sock as a puppet).

Luis finds Big Bird waiting at the bus stop, intending to migrate south like most birds do. Luis points out that other birds aren't as domesticated as Big Bird, who has food and warmth right on Sesame Street.
episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: The street scenes involving Big Bird are remakes of scenes from Episode 1126, while the Oscar scenes were originally written for Episode 1066.

episodes.summaryEn: Bob and his band (Gordon, Miss Trump, and the kids) will demonstrate fast and slow at Elmo's command. They play "Pop Goes the Weasel" slowly as Elmo dances slowly.
episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Scene 3 is a rewrite of the first scene from Episode 0757, with Elmo taking Grover's place. Muppet Wiki note: The group that makes up Bob's band in this episode were all previously seen in Episode 2229, and are seen again in Episode 2424.

episodes.summaryEn: Forgetful Jones finds Bob and the kids about to do some singing. He wants to join in, only he can't remember what singing is, and confuses it for jumping, then kissing, and yelling instead.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar and Grundgetta are about to pretend they're flying on Grouch Airlines in the yard, using crates and cardboard as their airplane and "out of control tower." Elmo wants to play with them, and the Grouches struggle to come up with a good excuse for not letting him. Elmo conjures up his imaginary luggage, plane ticket, and every other supply he would need on the plane when Oscar says the flight is only for Grouches; Elmo just decides to make-believe he didn't hear that and boards the plane.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Elmo likes watching the Two-Headed Monster and wishes he could join him in the fun. With Susan's encouragement he approaches the monster and asks if they're willing to be a three-headed monster.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: In the original script draft, the scene with the New York Mets was slightly different. Big Bird was present during the scene (rather than in just voiceover), with the context that he wrote to the team to visit and help Snuffy practice for the Snuffleupagus Little League team. The script also called for catcher Gary Carter to be part of the group. The scene was also intended to be part of the street story, as the episode would close with an additional scene where the Mets try to get Snuffy to sign a season contract, but Snuffy feels he's not ready; he only knows how to write in print, not cursive.

episodes.summaryEn: The Count has written his own version of "Sleeping Beauty," in which he and Gladys the Cow will be starring. As he makes the costumes, Gordon and the kids help measure her body.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: At the Library, Micki gathers Telly, Maria, Luis, Bob, and the kids for story time, hosted by Linda and her friend Ed. Micki interprets as Linda and Ed tell the story of "Jack and the Beanstalk" in sign language, cueing the kids to guess some of the characters' signs and pretending to be said characters.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird uses soup cans to play pretend telephone with Mr. Snuffleupagus, who doesn't quite grasp the concept. When he finally gets into the swing of things, he's unable to hear Big Bird's call; he's imagining he's on the Moon.
Sully arrives on the construction site to find Biff a sobbing mess. Biff has felt sad ever since Sully went home after work yesterday because he missed his best pal.

Elmo greets the viewer and shows off his plastic zoo set, saying hello to all his toy animals. Gordon and Miles observe him playing with it, and Gordon notices how he's typically put all the animals in zoo cages.

altLabels.labelEn: Gordon brings Elmo and Miles to the zoo
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Count von Count introduces Luis to his grandparents, who also love to count. In song, they demonstrate that while the Count's counting elicits thunder and lightning, Grandpa Count's counting brings snow, and Grandma Count's counting brings rain.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Sitting at Hooper's Store doing her homework, Gina welcomes the viewer and notes that she needs a job so she can earn some money to buy her mom a birthday present. While she puts her headphones on to listen to some music as she works, David comments to himself that he could use some extra help around the store.

altLabels.labelEn: David hires Gina to work at Hooper's
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

uploads.extentNoteEn: The file label marks this episode incomplete within the block.

episodes.summaryEn: On today's edition of Ask Oscar, the Count fills in as co-host (Telly is at the dentist). Oscar, however, is not up to answering any questions today as usual.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird comes across the Amazing Mumford in the midst of perfecting his latest trick - getting his portable radio to sound like his duck and vice versa (with the magic words "A la peanut butter sandwiches on AM/FM quackers!"). He plans on performing the trick at the Magicians' Convention in Las Vegas and rushes off to his travel agent to claim his ticket, asking Big Bird to look after his duck.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: The content played on the radio includes "Il signor Bruschino Overture," "Quale insolita gioia nel tuo sguardo" from Aida, "Witchcraft" by Frank Sinatra, "Panama" by Van Halen, "Ladron de Tu Amor" by Louie Ramirez, and Jon Stone as a newscaster, as well as a few instrumental pieces used for the show over the years.

episodes.summaryEn: Maria and David stand by as Slimey reads "The Earthworm's Book of Magic." Oscar explains that his pet worm is going to try a new magic trick, but Maria and David need to keep it down so he can concentrate. Slimey's first try produces a puff of smoke which enlarges his book.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 2192. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Susan, the kids, and the Two-Headed Monster are singing some songs when the monster makes a song choice - "Macaroni." They sing it in their monster language, and Susan points out it's better known as "Yankee Doodle." The Two-Headed Monster prefers their gibberish version and wants everyone to sing along with him. He likes it so much they end up singing it over, and over, and over...

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 2148. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Maria and Luis welcome the viewer in Spanish, then Big Bird - or rather, "The Amazing Birdford," greets them. Big Bird has borrowed the Amazing Mumford's magic kit and is learning how to become a magician.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 2144. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Luis tells Big Bird that his friend, singer Rubén Blades, is coming to visit today. Big Bird gets excited, then disappointed when Rubén arrives without his band; he thinks Rubén won't be able to sing now.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 2211. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: At Hooper's Store, Forgetful Jones struggles to remember some important information, but he succeeds: he remembers to say "Howdy" to the viewer, the street's name, his name, and that he's supposed to show the viewer around Sesame Street today! Linda comes by to congratulate his rare instance of excellent memory in sign language.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 2180. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: At night, Maria, Olivia, and Bob are getting ready to go home and go to bed. Meanwhile, Oscar the Grouch waits in anticipation (with the viewer) for what happens once they get inside and turn off their lights: the nocturnal jazz musician known as Hoots the Owl starts playing his saxophone and bothering everyone.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 2164. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: At Hooper's Store David greets Jiffy the turtle, who comes in for breakfast. Jiffy speaks very slowly, so David makes sure Gordon and Linda have everything they need - this could take a long time.

altLabels.labelEn: Jiffy the turtle / Barkley the cow
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 2142. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Miss Blechman is visiting Sesame Street and pesters Luis to try and guess what she does for a living. Given her clues of working in a classroom, receiving apple cores from young Grouches, and dirtying up her blackboard, Luis knows that she is a Grouch teacher and is there to see Oscar, who was her best pupil.

altLabels.labelEn: Miss Blechman visits Oscar, her favorite student
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 2159. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Luis is swamped with work at the Fix-It Shop, and Maria is too busy reading her book - The Adventures of Captain Swashbuckle - to help. Luis ends up bringing three boxes of supplies in while she neglects her work, but he shows how Maria can still help: Luis will read the book as she puts all the supplies away.

altLabels.labelEn: A day with books on Sesame Street
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 2173. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Telly Monster is going to talk to the viewer about the word information. While he tries to think of how to explain it, various folks use the word while asking Telly some questions: an elderly Muppet man asks where 123 Sesame Street is, Big Bird tells Telly about something interesting in his newspaper, a Muppet reporter inquires who to ask about living in trash cans, and Maria remembers she can look up the library's phone number.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 2220. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Maria welcomes the viewer as she fans herself with a magazine, upset by the extreme heat today. Oscar calls her over and shows her the new Grouch fan he installed above his trash can.

altLabels.labelEn: A hot day on Sesame Street
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 2201. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Maria, Gordon, and the kids see Forgetful Jones has a new, large hat. He was given it by Clementine, claiming it would be so big he'd never forget it.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 2152. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Uncle Wally and Bob are up very early to go jogging with Gordon. Bob remains groggy and falls asleep standing up as Wally and Gordon converse.

altLabels.labelEn: Oscar thinks Slimey has run away.

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 2151. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: David has been looking after a potted plant for his friend and is on his way to return it. On his way there, he hears arguing coming from Big Bird's nest.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 2143. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Mr. Snuffleupagus wants to play football with Slimey, but Oscar thinks the size difference will make the game unfair to Slimey; he suggests hide and seek instead. Snuffy looks everywhere on Sesame Street and can't find Slimey.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 2140. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Maria, Elmo, and the kids find Shelley the Turtle sitting next to Oscar's trash can. They all try to think of ways to get him to poke his head out, such as pleading, jumping, or screaming, but nothing happens.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 2187. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird greets David at the door of Hooper's Store and says he can't tell him anything about the surprise waiting for him inside. But, through a series of unsolicited and inadvertent clues, David figures out that it's his Grandma Grace.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 2138. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Bob and Big Bird are just about to go to the movies when Bob takes notice of Big Bird's clever note for Snuffy. Big Bird explains that if Snuffy goes looking for him, he'll see the note left, reading, "Dear Snuffy, Big Bird and Bob went to a..." with Gladys the Cow and the letter V beside it, to which she would moo after the note is read and point to the letter V - reading "moo-V."

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 2153. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: A cheerful young lady named Amelia Adams (Teri Garr) applies to attend Oscar's New School for Grouch Research. Oscar (dressed in a tattered cap and mortarboard) doesn't believe that she's fit for such a school, but Amelia is persistent as she's gone to just about every other kind of school.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 2223. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird and Snuffy pretend to explore Sesame Street, imagining it's their first time seeing it. They observe an "umpadumpus tree," meet some friendly native "Sesame Streetians" speaking "Sesamese" and attempt to communicate with them and learn their customs, and encounter a wild animal (Barkley).

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird and Snuffy pretend to explore Sesame Street
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki marks the street story as a repeat of Episode 2150. This remains a separately numbered main-series installment.

episodes.summaryEn: Everyone gets things ready on the street as Maria's mother, Mrs. Figueroa, will be stopping by for a visit. Bob and Luis hold up a "Bienvenida" banner and Maria dresses in her finest, claiming her mom is big on neatness; Luis is particularly struck by how she looks.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: This episode marks the first use of Maria's maiden name of Figueroa, as well as the first indication of Maria and Luis becoming romantically paired.

episodes.summaryEn: Bob finds it odd that there's a "COLD" sign in the door of Hooper's Store. He goes inside and finds Elmo taking care of things while David is out.

As Luis works on Dr. Kruger's toaster at the Fix-It Shop, Gina and Big Bird frantically bring in a small kitten they found abandoned in the vacant lot on 12th Street. They've put her in a shoebox to rest and say she has no sign of a mother, and is so small and weak she can hardly even walk.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria stops by the Fix-It Shop in the early morning to check on Luis and the stray kitten; she wakes up Luis when he doesn't notice his alarm clock going off. He asks her to get some solid cat food to see if the kitten is strong enough to eat any.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Hoots the Owl stops by the Fix-It Shop to see Gatita, the cat Maria and Luis have been taking care of this week. The two have each bought the same kind of baskets, blankets, and scratching posts.

altLabels.labelEn: Maria & Luis — Luis and Maria develop feelings for each other
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird observes Maria and Luis trying to fix his cassette player in the Fix-It Shop. The two each have an idea of what to do, first using pliers then a screwdriver, but neither works.

David finds Telly hiding behind the Hooper's Store newsstand, worrying about something as usual. He explains that Meryl Sheep is putting on a production called "Cinderella's Shoe" and he's worried that she might ask him to play a part, believing any number of ridiculous misfortunes could befall him onstage.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Elmo gets up early in the morning to listen to the various sounds, such as traffic and birds singing. His favorite sounds are the ones made when he eats his breakfast in the yard.

Telly Monster studies his "Spanish for Monsters" book and learns the different ways of greeting someone in the morning, afternoon, and night. The book gives the friendly suggestion of using them when meeting to a Spanish-speaking individual today.

altLabels.labelEn: Telly uses Spanish throughout the day
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: In a scene originally scripted, but later cut, Susan and the kids check out a presentation of Slimey's newest photography pieces. However, because he is so small, all the photos are at foot-level. They correctly guess the feet of Susan, Snuffy, Big Bird, and Barkley, before they see a picture of the empty sidewalk - a "self-portrait" of Slimey since he has no feet to capture.

episodes.summaryEn: Elmo tells Uncle Wally about a recent sleepover he had at Bob's apartment. A flashback shows Elmo observing Bob through his morning routine of washing his face and hands, brushing his teeth, shaving, and brushing his hair.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar brings to order the first meeting of the Grouch Explorers Club, though the other members (Grundgetta and two Grouches) don't know what it means to explore. Once Oscar explains their club's purpose, the others all split off to explore in different directions.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Additional performers include Richard Hunt (gray Grouch and MATH Doctor) and Camille Bonora (purple Grouch, umbrella salesperson, and Goldilocks).

episodes.summaryEn: Linda has invited Telly to have lunch outside Hooper's Store. She tells Telly that she's going to get some food, and Telly is able to tell what she said by the gestures she used with her signs.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird pretends to be Guy Smiley and surprises Maria by making her the subject of "Here is Your Puerto Rican Life!" His reunion includes such guests as her aunt and uncle (played by the kids), some cocquís (also the kids), and a coconut tree (Elmo). Big Bird then surprises her with a lovely paper clip charm bracelet, and leads them all for a post-show party at Hooper's Store (on Maria's dime).
Big Bird plays a guessing game with the kids using toy cans that make the sounds of different animals (including Mr. Snuffleupagus).

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: In the yard, Elmo learns how to write and read his name with help from Bob.

altLabels.labelEn: Elmo plays with his new goldfish, Barkley
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird sits in front of a closed Hooper's Store, explaining that he wants to have breakfast but he doesn't have any birdseed. David comes to open up Hooper's, but unfortunately he can't find his keys.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar is about to eat an anchovy-sardine-jelly sandwich when Elmo comes along wanting to play. Oscar refuses, because he's a Grouch and only does grouchy things.

Uncle Wally bumps into Bob on his way to Big Bird's nest, carrying a "WALK" sign. Wally is substituting for Big Bird at today's Birdketeer meeting, being made "head bird." Bob watches and Uncle Wally teaches the Birdketeers how to follow the sign.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Ronald Grump, the Grouch building tycoon, approaches Oscar with a new idea - a two-story can-dominium called "Grump Tower." In exchange for Oscar giving up his property to build the tower, Grump gives him a spot in the tower, as well as three bags of trash. Maria thinks it's a rotten deal, which only encourages Oscar further.

altLabels.labelEn: Ronald Grump builds the Grump Tower
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: The Gruppys are performed by Camille Bonora and Pam Arciero.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird notices Luis fixated on watching Maria doing some repairs inside the Fix-It Shop. He recalls when she first started working there and not knowing much about fixing items, but he now beams with pride over how great she is now.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: During the first scene, Luis tells Big Bird that when Maria started working at the Fix-it Shop, she didn't know how to fix a thing. This contradicts Episode 0832, her first day on the job where she tells Luis that she was always interested in fixing things. Muppet Wiki note: While writing his note to Hoots, Big Bird briefly mentions Snuffy's little sister Alice, who would debut on the show later in Episode 2410.

episodes.summaryEn: Meryl Sheep wanders down the street repeating "quiet" and "loud" in their respective volumes. Oscar the Grouch queries and learns it's for her new "barnyard production." Oscar practices with her and gets high marks; he's especially good at the loud parts.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob creates a new game where he asks Big Bird questions that all have "No" as an answer; Big Bird responds by saying "No," while holding a sign with the word. After the game, Big Bird continues to say "no" to everything Bob asks.

altLabels.labelEn: Maria can't get Irvine to go back to sleep
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Susan sings "What Can You Add to the Song?," asking the kids to make different noises.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird and Snuffy are playing cowboys, but have a conflict on how to yell: Big Bird would rather say "yee-haw" twice, while Snuffy would rather say it three times.

altLabels.labelEn: Maria & Luis — Maria and Luis realize they're in love
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Telly has a "Monster on the Spot" interview at the Fix-It Shop with Maria and Luis, who just found out that they love each other. They explain that they'll still love each other tomorrow, despite Telly's concerns about harsh weather interfering with their relationship (and their health).

altLabels.labelEn: Maria & Luis — Maria and Luis love each other
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Telly learns from David and Gina that today, Hooper's Store is having a sale on balls, crayons. and hats. As Telly worries over what he should get, a pair of lads buy everything on sale.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Additional performers include Kevin Clash (monster and cow) and David Rudman (Lavender AM boy and rabbit).

episodes.summaryEn: Bob welcomes the viewer as the Count finishes up his latest painting, Five Beautiful Bats. Bob doesn't understand; the painting is of five cats, not bats.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar has written a Grouch cookbook and wants Bob to be in a photograph for it, looking as if he enjoys the mudpie he's made. As Oscar snaps the photo, he suggests Bob wave to the camera.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Grundgetta has prepared a special gift for lovebirds Maria and Luis - a scrapbook of various bits of trash from some of their dates (such as a paper bag and popped balloon). At first, the couple isn't thrilled, but realize the items bring them pleasant memories, which Grundgetta can't stand.

Snuffy introduces the viewer to his little sister Alice Snuffleupagus. He explains that today is the day he's going to introduce her to his best friend Big Bird, and begins describing him: he has two legs, feathers, and likes to sing to himself.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird observes Maria and Luis in the yard, casually reminding the viewer that they're in love. Luis tries to teach Maria his T'ai Chi exercises, but she doesn't want to do it.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Luis had previously practiced T'ai Chi in Episode 1372.

episodes.summaryEn: Maria is showing Telly a frog puppet her mother sent from Puerto Rico to give to her niece. She asks Telly to give it a try, but Telly is unsure as he doesn't know much Spanish; considering the puppet is a Puerto Rican coquí he believes it should speak some of its native language.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Uncle Wally trades his tuna fish salad for Bob's peanut butter and jelly sandwich when suddenly Big Bird and the Birdketeers arrive and bestow upon Bob the Golden F Award. He's been given such an honor for having many things beginning with F, such as his foot, face, and the fish in his salad.
episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Among the things Elmo talks about in his letter in scene 3 is his new shoes, which he previously bragged about in Episode 2271. It was also a running gag in the Sesame Street Live show "Big Bird's Sesame Street Story."

episodes.summaryEn: Maria, Luis, Gordon, and the kids attend a pageant written by and starring Big Bird, with Telly in the cast and Hoots the Owl on saxophone. It's written especially for Maria and Luis, with each verse emphasizing a different word of a sentence: when put together, the message turns out to be, "When are you getting married?" Maria and Luis don't have an answer for this.

altLabels.labelEn: Maria & Luis — Love in the Fix-It Shop
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Don Music pitches a new song to Meryl Sheep, hoping she will sing it in one of her productions. The song is directly about the beginning, middle, and end of itself.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Additional performers include David Rudman (neighbor Steve in scene 3).

episodes.summaryEn: Luis shows Linda, Gina, and the kids Gatita, the kitten he keeps at the Fix-It Shop. Linda teaches them all the sign for "cat," then Gina sings "Pussycat, What's on Your Mind?"

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Elmo learns what a dinosaur is from Big Bird and one of his books. Big Bird suggests they pretend to be dinosaurs, and Elmo begins to stomp around and make meowing noises until Big Bird points out dinosaurs don't sound like that.
The Amazing Mumford enters the Fix-It Shop in emotional distress - his wand broke in half while trying to perform a disappearing cup trick. Maria tapes it back together and Mumford tests it out.
Big Bird prepares a speech about some, more, and all. Before he begins, he sips from his glass of milk in various increments until it's all gone.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird and Snuffy are trying to play baseball when Alice gets in their way. Snuffy tells Alice to go far from him, which is also near Big Bird.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: As nighttime falls on Sesame Street, Gordon recalls (in song) about when he was "Afraid of the Dark" as a child, accompanied by brief flashbacks.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Chet O'Brien voices an unseen neighbor heard during scene 2, asking for Hoots and his band to turn down the racket.

episodes.summaryEn: At the crack of dawn, Big Bird listens to the sounds of the morning. One such sound is from Hoots the Owl, who's fallen asleep with his sax in his beak.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Additional performers include Camille Bonora as Maxine and David Rudman as Laverne.

episodes.summaryEn: At night, Sonny Friendly appears in Bob's apartment to play the "Name That Sound in the Middle of the Night" game. Bob declines, until he learns the prize is a trip around the world on a jet plane.

altLabels.labelEn: Bob plays Name That Sound / The Count watches the Fix-It Shop
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird enters Hooper's Store, feeling sad. David and Gina explain that it's okay to feel sad and it helps to talk about what's wrong.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gladys the Cow sees Elmo sipping down a glass of milk. Gladys begins boasting about milk, what gets made with it and where it comes from - cows like herself.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Snuffy uses himself and his baby sister Alice as examples of big and little, comparing his body parts to hers. Although Alice is little, she has a mighty big sneeze.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Olivia points out lovebirds Maria and Luis walking down the street, then presents the word LOVE by writing it on a pad of paper. Oscar can't take hearing all about love, even though he himself loves trash ("That's different," he argues).

Maria watches as Telly plays into Oscar's latest trick on him. Oscar has a painting of a silly-looking monster and has Telly yell, "Come over here and see the funny looking monster with the silly look on his face." This will attract people to see it and Oscar will pop up from his can to show everyone.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar passes by the Fix-It Shop and, deciding to do something nice today, says hello to Luis who's busy counting nails. Oscar inadvertently makes Luis lose his place, then begins using this to his grouchy advantage.
Grundgetta leads the Grouchketeers in a round of "One of These Grouchy Things" using pictures of dead flowers.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Today is Luis' birthday and Big Bird's gotten him a tie and a poem he wrote; he just needs help wrapping his gifts. At the Fix-It Shop, Maria offers to help and wraps his gifts in a box.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird's gift for Luis / Elmo watches for stars
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Olivia has cleared out some junk from an old trunk of hers and brings the box over to Oscar's trash can. He doesn't appear to be home, but Ruby appears and asks to rummage through the box.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: This is the last taped episode of Alaina Reed performing Olivia.

episodes.summaryEn: Juliet welcomes the viewer when the Miami Mice pull up on the street and give their own welcome in Spanish - after doing a fashion check, of course. Juliet learns what they said and gives it a try, and is deemed cool by the mice (even donning a pair of shades herself).

Luis comes across the new Meryl Sheep School of Acting in the yard. Meryl explains that the school will teach everyone to "act in ways they never dreamed of acting." She's one of the teachers, but today has invited guest lecturer Professor Cluckinella (Martin P. Robinson) to teach how to act like a chicken.

altLabels.labelEn: The Meryl Sheep School of Acting
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Snuffy tries to get Alice to welcome the viewer, but she takes his instructions too literally and ends up playing and running around instead.
Maria and the kids search for Barkley, who doesn't want to take his bath. They find him hiding behind some crates in the yard and Maria tries to lure him out with a dog biscuit.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Susan watches as Oscar, with a rubber bulb horn on his face, receives a lesson in speaking "honk" from a female Honker. He hopes that since the language is so noisy, he'll be able to say grouchy things and make a lot of noise in the process.

Telly has planned to introduce a crowd of kids (including Farley) to the "CH" sound, but doesn't have anything that starts with the sound. The kids point out that they're children, which begins with "CH."
Telly Monster introduces the viewer to their special guest today, Richard Stoltzman, who plays a jazzy version of the opening theme song on his clarinet for Telly, Bob, and the kids.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Luis encounters an upset Telly, who has just learned that the Count intends to give up counting. Even though he loves counting a lot, the Count wants to try new things and admits it's not good to keep doing the same thing over and over; before long, he's begun counting reasons to stop counting.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob comes across Big Bird and Mr. Snuffleupagus in the yard, circling around a large pumpkin sitting on a table. They want to draw a face on it, but can't seem to find the front.
Gina has prepared some special items for lunch at Hooper's Store. However, everyone who passes by is instead attending a special luncheon at Birdland.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Additional performers include Martin P. Robinson (dog), Camille Bonora (Old Mother Hubbard and Little Miss Muffet), Richard Hunt (seagull and Papa Bear), and David Rudman (woodpecker and Little Red Riding Hood).

episodes.summaryEn: Biff greets the viewer from the rooftop of 123 Sesame Street, where he and Sully are repairing the building's TV antenna. They have with them a small TV set to check their progress with.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Additional performers include Camille Bonora (Lavender girl).

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird has just finished writing a play and needs some actors to perform it. Meryl Sheep suddenly appears beside him and angles for a part.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird's Little Bo Peep play
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Snuffy and Jessica play a game involving reading "OPEN" and "CLOSED" signs. Snuffy says Oscar will help them out in the game, but he wants no part.

Bob comes into the library and learns that Slimey is writing his own book in order to add a section to the library for worm readers. Sure enough, as soon as he's finished, Linda puts the book on a miniature shelf and a fellow worm checks it out.

altLabels.labelEn: Animals at the library / Snuffy makes art
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Additional performers include David Rudman (brown horse and sheep), Kevin Clash (grey horse), and Pam Arciero (Little Bo Sheep), with Martin P. Robinson (sheep).

episodes.summaryEn: Maria and Luis are about to close up the Fix-It Shop when they find themselves as the contestants on Sonny Friendly's Traveling Game Show - "The Love Game!" Luis is willing to play when he learns the grand prize is a trip, despite Maria's warnings of how Sonny's prizes and games can be. Sonny asks the two of their feelings when they kiss, which both Maria and Luis refuse to answer since it's a private matter.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: The Traveling Game Show announcer is addressed by Sonny Friendly as Don, referencing announcer Don Pardo. In other episodes, the announcer is named Gene, referencing an even busier gameshow announcer, Gene Wood.

episodes.summaryEn: Snuffy welcomes the viewer to his recently opened business: "Snuffy's Store," where he sells "everything you need" - cabbages and spaghetti. Gordon, his first customer, doesn't need any of those things but Snuffy begs him to buy something anyway.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: David plays a musical game with the kids - "Walk This Way."

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird and Snuffy send a letter
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Two additional scenes were present in an earlier draft of the script that were later cut. In one scene, Oscar shows David his new "trashometer," which can detect how many bags of trash are by his can. David tests the machine out by subtracting the trash bags until there are zero, which the machine reflects, but Oscar claims it isn't working. He finally gets the machine to function as it blares a loud siren where there are no trash bags, incentivizing others to bring him trash to shut off the noise. In the other scene, Big Bird recites a poem about the calf, with some visual art cards.

episodes.summaryEn: Telly welcomes the viewer as he struggles to write the letter X. Maria shows him how to make a proper one and assures Telly that with practice, he'll be much better at writing.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: This episode was later repeated in Season 21 as Episode 2680.

episodes.summaryEn: Luis and Maria sit on the stoop enjoying some coffee when suddenly a newspaper is hurled toward them, creating a small puff of dust. The smelly paper - a copy of The Daily Grouch - belongs to Oscar, who notes it's the only newspaper used to wrap fish with before it's sent; sure enough, they find a big stinky one inside the pages.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: This episode was later repeated in Season 21 as Episode 2653.

episodes.summaryEn: Gina rushes to Hooper's Store, asking David if she can get off work today. She excitedly tells him her favorite rock group, Little Jerry and the Monotones, is going to be visiting today and shows him a letter from Little Jerry himself informing her of it.

altLabels.labelEn: A visit from Little Jerry and the Monotones
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Kevin Clash performs Big Jeffie in this episode. Muppet Wiki note: In this episode, the band appears as a trio, with Chrissy and Rockin' Richard replaced with another Fat Blue Monotone named Richie (performed by Richard Hunt). This was his only appearance with the group. A photo of the trio as they appeared in this episode can be found in the Rock & Roll! VHS in Jackman Wolf's studio, a video also featuring a prominent story with Little Jerry and his band. Gina has the same picture, only autographed, in Episode 2595.

episodes.summaryEn: Snuffy and Alice display the capital and small letter A. Snuffy shows some "A" words and has Alice repeat them before trying to cue her that her name also begins with A. "Well, we've got a ways to go, little Alice, but you're off to a good start," admires Snuffy.

altLabels.labelEn: Making rhythms with the Honker and Dinger
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Uncle Wally shows off his train conductor hat and tells Big Bird and the kids about one of his many odd jobs as a conductor for the G and G Railroad, named such because it only stopped in towns beginning with G. He demonstrates how an average ride would go, and has Big Bird and the kids repeat all the G-named towns he would call out. They all then mimic the motions of a train, with Wally as the engine and everyone joining in as his train cars.

episodes.summaryEn: In the early morning, an announcer (Martin P. Robinson) introduces the first episode of "Dreams of Our Lives," a window into the dreams of the residents of Sesame Street. First up is Big Bird, still asleep in his nest.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird discovers a pair of sleeping birds near his nest. They wake up and introduce themselves as Peter-Paul and Marilou.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird volunteers to be the contestant on Sonny Friendly's latest traveling game show, The Air Game! He's instructed to come up with one thing air can do and write his answer down on a piece of paper.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: The script for scene 3 features a bit at the end that does not appear in the final episode, where the Two-Headed Monster passes by and mistakes Linda and Maria (wearing the sweater built for two) for his Aunt Fanny.

episodes.summaryEn: At Hooper's Store, Gina reintroduces the viewer to Hiroshi, an art student who's working on a sketch of Gina. Oscar drives the Sloppy Jalopy out of the garage and intends to keep it on the street from now on, where more damage can be done to it.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar tells the "Grouchketeers at home" that he's expecting Grouch visitors from Grouchytown, who have never been anywhere else before.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria finds Telly and Juliet preparing a birthday poem for Telly's aunt. The two panic that if the card is so good, Telly's aunt might rush outside to show people and slip in a mud puddle.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: This episode marks the first appearance of a dramatic violin music sting that plays whenever Telly and/or Juliet would have their worries build up into bigger scenarios. This underscore would only last for a few years, remaining with Telly after Juliet's departure and appearing as late as season 29.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird and Birdketeer troupe 1-2-3 deliver a program ID spot for Good Day Sesame Street. From a cozy living room set, Buster the Horse and Gladys the Cow introduce their morning show and the topics we'll be seeing today.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Susan is slightly baffled by Meryl Sheep's latest role - as the number four. She hasn't got her costume on, but she's surrounded herself with fours of things and a picture of the number so she can fully immerse herself in the number.

altLabels.labelEn: A rock garden on Sesame Street
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Telly Monster hosts an edition of "The Wide World of Sesame Street" from inside Linda's apartment to watch her and Barkley. Her alarm clock rings, but she is unable to hear it.

altLabels.labelEn: The Wide World of Sesame Street covers Linda
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird welcomes the viewer, joined by a small group of tourist birds visiting from the country. They've never seen an apartment before, so Big Bird intends on taking them up to Bob's.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: The scene with David, Juliet, and Telly at the bus stop was removed in its repeat episode (2771) due to the retirement of David. Muppet Wiki note: Additional performers include David Rudman (as the toucan), with Martin P. Robinson (as the parrot) and Camille Bonora (as the grossbill). Muppet Wiki note: In a continuity error, the dust jacket from Bob's book is removed for the final scene.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird is especially happy because Maria and Luis are going to take him to the park to play today. Maria comes over with some unfortunate news - she and Luis have some important work to do (such as fixing David's toaster and making an important phone call) and can't take him to the park.

altLabels.labelEn: Maria's pregnancy — Maria announces her pregnancy
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Luis sees that Oscar's trash can is surrounded by leafy, tropical plants and marked with a "HOT" sign on it. Oscar explains today is "Hot Day," where he turns up the furnace in his can.
episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Scene 2 was originally written to be used in Episode 2474.

episodes.summaryEn: Herry Monster eagerly waits outside the Library, ready to get some books to take home and read. Tico points out the sign telling him it'll be opening at 9am (a couple of minutes from now).

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Scenes 2 and 3 are reworked from Episode 0955. Scene 4 is adapted from Episode 1135.

episodes.summaryEn: Maria takes care of Natasha, and shows Telly how she can interpret her different cries when feeding and burping her. David comes over to bring Maria some milk, and Telly makes an order in baby talk by mimicking Natasha's cries, going into hysterics over his joke.

altLabels.labelEn: Maria's pregnancy — Taking care of Natasha
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Among the songs Ruby rejects during the final scene are "Put Down the Duckie," "Just One Me," and "The Ten Commandments of Health."

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar tries to get rid of a seagull that has followed him from the dump and won't leave. He asks Luis and Linda to try to communicate with the gull in Spanish and sign-language since the bird doesn't respond to his shouting, but neither method works either.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Luis finds Oscar and his new pet seagull Stinky just as he left them asleep in the previous episode. Luis' whispering wakes Oscar up, making him and Stinky very angry; being a Grouch, speaking loudly doesn't wake him up.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Additional performers include David Rudman (taupe Grouch), with Martin P. Robinson (green Grouch).

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird has a photo of Mr. Snuffleupagus he intends to hang in his nest, but can't find it; he's unaware it's been taped to his tail feathers.
Gina and Telly watch "Magic Mike" playing imaginary basketball. While Gina heads back to work, Mike teaches Telly how to imagine his own game.

altLabels.labelEn: Telly and Gina prepare for a concert
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: It's a very warm day today, as Telly and Uncle Wally observe. Gordon's attempts to tinker with their electric fan are fruitless, when they all feel a refreshing breeze.

altLabels.labelEn: Learning about air with Herb Wolf
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Snuffy and Alice say the " big and little alphabet," where Snuffy recites the alphabet (represented in capital letters) and Alice repeats the letters (seen in lowercase).

altLabels.labelEn: Maria's pregnancy — Luis anticipates taking care of the baby
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Scene 1 would be used as a stand-alone insert in future episodes, usually editing out the beginning and ending music tag.

episodes.summaryEn: Sherlock Hemlock is in the mood for a mystery. He listens and hears the sounds of a large animal sniffling, some wind, and a door slam.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Elmo talks about what an adventure is, and says that he's had adventures on the beach and at the park, while sometimes he pretends he's somewhere else. He wants to have an adventure right there on Sesame Street, but Gina doesn't think he'll experience anything out of the ordinary.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Elmo has Gordon read him a letter he received today. The letter tells Elmo that a friend will be visiting him at Hooper's Store at 4 o'clock.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob happens upon Elmo poking his toy dinosaur, Ziggy, to "wake" him up. Bob notes that Ziggy isn't sleeping - he's just not filled with air.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Air-date anomaly: source explicitly says February 28, 1989, also assigned to Episode 2562. The otherwise regular Monday-Friday sequence would place 2557 on February 21. Preserve the published date pending independent confirmation; do not silently correct it. Muppet Wiki note: Additional performers include Camille Bonora (mommy bird) and David Rudman (baby bird), with Kevin Clash (daddy bird). Muppet Wiki note: The mommy bird is made from the Little Bird puppet.

episodes.summaryEn: Luis welcomes the viewer, and mentions that Maria is at the clinic where she is about to get her check-up. He also says that a friend has tagged along...

altLabels.labelEn: Maria's pregnancy — Maria goes to the maternity clinic
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Telly has a capital and lowercase G set out (as well as several back up versions) in order to talk about the letter. Gina, Hiroshi, Maria, and the kids, who were all supposed to bring some G-word items, have all brought the same thing - galoshes, which Gina notes are really the only G-word things handy around the house.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: David finishes painting a sign to put up in Hooper's Store reading "David's Peanut Butter," advertising peanut butter he's made himself. Hiroshi comes by and has a sample, but is much more engrossed in the sign.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gina finds Telly, a Honker, and the kids having a "goodbye ceremony" for his broken toy fishing pole. He recalls the fun times he's had with it via brief flashbacks (including fishing in Maria's bathtub, hooking a pretend shark, and he and the Honker fishing for Gina's donut in the yard) before Gina helps respectfully place it in the trash afterwards.

David wants to get some new things for Hooper's Store, such as new chairs, a new counter, new register, and a new milkshake maker (as insisted upon by Gina). He shows Elmo the catalogue from a store downtown they intend to buy these things from.

altLabels.labelEn: David and Gina attempt to renovate Hooper's
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria is tossing and turning in bed, waking up Luis. Her pregnancy food cravings are kicking in, only she can't figure out what it is exactly she's hungry for.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird tells the viewer that nobody else is available to play with him. He doesn't mind and sings about all the fun he can have on his own ("I've Got Me").
It has been recommended that Maria drink four glasses of milk per day while pregnant. This fact has been relayed by Luis to Telly, Bob, and a Honker, who all give her some glasses of milk.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: The "Pomp and Circumstance" recording used in this episode previously appeared in a season 3 animal film segment about an octopus.

episodes.summaryEn: Today, Hooper's Store is having a sale on tuna fish. Gina stacks the cans in a pyramid formation on the window counter for display, counting all 40 as she does so.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria works at the Fix-It Shop and chats with a visiting Honker, who has their rather cranky baby with them. Duane and Ingrid arrive on the block to Maria's surprise, having not seen them since their honeymoon.

Maria comes across Meryl Sheep in the yard set up to autograph her latest book: Sheep Poems, full of poems she's written about herself (naturally). Encouraged by Barkley, she reads one selection entitled "My Sheep Dog," about her days as a little lamb and the sheep dog named Bo Peep that kept her safe.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird goes into Hooper's Store, where David is very frustrated with the tons of work he has ahead of him. Big Bird constantly disrupts him to ask for various items (a table cloth, a plate, and a whole cake).

altLabels.labelEn: Luis misses the baby moving inside Maria
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Hiroshi has a bonsai tree with him in the yard, and explains to Big Bird why they won't ever be able to climb it or sit under it for shade since it'll never grow as big as most trees. It is, however, the right size for Slimey to sit under.

David, Maria, Hiroshi, and Shalon notice a sign on Oscar's trash can, which says "Oscar's Subtraction Show." He has four chairs set up outside it, and tells them all to sit down as his show begins. Everyone is skeptical at first, but Hiroshi persuades them to give it a try.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Additional performers include David Rudman as the Owl-Stars bass player.

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon and Susan show Miles a picture with a duck, cow, and pig embedded within. The Amazing Mumford arrives and tries to make things easier by magically transposing the animals from the picture and onto the street.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Additional performers include David Rudman (cow) and Martin P. Robinson (pig).

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird tries to form the kids into two lines, but finds the groups are uneven whenever he sorts them by gender, shirt pattern, and other attributes. Suzy (who's in a wheelchair) offers an idea - making one line.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird plays with the kids
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Mrs. Figueroa, Maria's mother from Puerto Rico, is making a return visit to Sesame Street. Big Bird explains that they will be discussing Maria's latest trip to the maternity clinic, which Luis has documented down to every last detail with his photo camera.

altLabels.labelEn: Maria's pregnancy — Maria's mother visits Sesame Street
