episodes.summaryEn: David welcomes the viewer and Gina reads in the newspaper that the famous director, Birdnardo Birdtolucci, is coming to Sesame Street to film his latest masterpiece. Gina is excited for him to come, but doesn't notice he's been behind them the whole time.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Telly is going to write a story and has prepared for the unforeseeable by stocking up several dozen pencils, erasers, a bunch of pads of paper, and two typewriters. Maria and Luis try to convince him he's going overboard again.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob plays a musical exercise with Elmo and the kids, having them sing the notes he plays on the piano. Elmo gives it a try and plays a complicated, unfocused arrangement just for Bob to repeat.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Uncle Wally and his barbershop singing group of horses, the Kentucky Derbies, sing "One of Us Here is Not Like The Others" and has the viewer guess which one is different. Wally is the only one that isn't a horse, but Buster points out that he's also the only one not wearing a derby hat, so there are two possible answers.

altLabels.labelEn: A television birthday card for Gordon
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: The original script for the episode contained an extra scene that was not recorded: Big Bird and Snuffy try to color, but find their red crayons are broken. Big Bird is inspired to imagine another Blue Bird adventure, in which he apprehends the Crayon Breaker (Linda) at a local day care center.

episodes.summaryEn: Luis can't find a solution to fix a broken clock. He imagines it's able to talk (performed by David Rudman in an Ed Wynn voice), where he finds one of its "tick tock screws" is loose.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Martin P. Robinson voices the Monster on the Spot announcer.

episodes.summaryEn: Elmo has gotten up early to be able to surprise everyone. He hides behind Oscar's trash can and unsuccessfully tries surprising Bob, Luis, and Linda, who are otherwise caught up in their activities.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Count von Count phones the Miami Mice to make an urgent visit to Sesame Street. The mice are disappointed to find that all they're needed for is to be counted by the Count.

While gushing over how nice it is today, Maria habitually picks a piece of lint from Oscar's shoulder. He gets angry and she puts it back, which is exactly what he expects to happen as he enjoys complaining about it.
Shelley the Turtle talks to his friend, Rudder Rabbit, on the Hooper's Store payphone. He tells Gina that Rudder will be arriving from 3rd Street any moment.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Additional performers include David Rudman (as Rudder, the cow, and pig #3), Martin P. Robinson (as pig #1), and Pam Arciero (as pig #2).

episodes.summaryEn: Bob is giving a music lesson to a new student - a meek woman named Masha (portrayed by Tracey Ullman). She struggles with singing the basic scales, but with some encouragement from Bob, she improves each time and gains her confidence.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Telly is reluctant to say "hello" to the viewer, because the sooner he says "hello," the sooner it means he'll have to say "goodbye." Bob doesn't see this as that big a deal, so Telly begins practicing "hellos" and "goodbyes" to become just as indifferent to it as Bob is.
Big Bird narrates that today started out like any other, normal day on Sesame Street: "a Grouch was grouching... a bird was tweeting (tweet tweet tweeeeet)... a Cookie Monster was Google Bugling..."

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: After singing "Five Little Monkeys Jumping on the Bed," Placido Flamingo disrupts Bob from singing "The Eensy Weensy Spider" with Telly and the kids, claiming no one can lead a song but him, even if he doesn't know any non-opera songs. Bob finishes the song and Placido thinks it's nothing compared to the opera he's performed: "The Spider's Feelings." He thinks they can perform it today and assigns everyone roles, including Bob as the titular spider.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: This episode was later repeated in Season 22 as Episode 2787 during a summer 1991 rerun with new inserts placed in.

episodes.summaryEn: Snuffy tells the viewer that Alice will be giving them the welcome today. They've been practicing a lot and Alice finally greets the viewer, saying "Wigwamm-froo-SMOSSmee-Sreep!" Snuffy considers this a close-enough attempt and beams with pride.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: The scene with Oscar and Maria was removed in its repeat episode (2768), as it features Maria in her pregnancy.

episodes.summaryEn: Maria welcomes the viewer on a rainy day. Elmo points out to her all the different types of sounds, like the rain hitting the pavement, Oscar's trash can lid, and Maria's umbrella.

episodes.summaryEn: Snuffy comes by to pick up Big Bird for a picnic in Central Park with Mommy Snuffleupagus and Alice. However, as Susan reports, Big Bird has come down with the flu and is unable to go.

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: A shot of Big Bird picking up the phone in scene 5 was used as part of a montage for the song "Hands" in season 23.

episodes.summaryEn: Wide World of Sesame Street host Telly doesn't know who today's feature is and divines from the clues around him that he's following a day in the life of Miles. episodes.summaryEn: Gordon, Susan, Gina, and Uncle Wally convene outside Oscar's trash can to surprise him on his birthday. Susan has baked his favorite cake (mud chiffon upside down), Gina has a present (a 1918 tomato can for his collection), and Uncle Wally has a broken record (of "Telephone Rock").

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Scenes 1 and 2 are remakes of scenes from Episode 0967, while the egg storyline was originally written for Episode 0937.

episodes.summaryEn: In the morning, Big Bird and Mr. Snuffleupagus wake up from their sleepover and notice Ruby nearby wearing a blindfold. She tells them she's conducting another experiment: she wants to see if she'll know when the sun comes up without seeing it.

altLabels.labelEn: An artsy day on Sesame Street
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon exits 123 Sesame Street to find a beat-up phone booth just outside, complete with a couple of localized telephone poles and Ernestine the Telephone Operator seated at a switchboard. episodes.summaryEn: Gina is heading off to bed, but remembers she has to write in her journal first. She tells the viewer about some entries, such as a visit from Little Jerry and the Monotones and her first day working at Hooper's Store.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gina will be babysitting Oscar's niece, Irvine, while he and Grundgetta go to the "Everything in the Wrong Place Ball" (as Gina observes by the two's odd attire). Once they leave, Gina begins reading Irvine the story of Grumpelstiltskin, one of several Grouch books Oscar has left for her.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird hears saxophone music coming from the art studio. He assumes it's Hiroshi playing the sax, but it's actually Hoots.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Telly welcomes the viewer and announces that both David's and Miles' grandmothers are visiting. He then gets confused when Gordon tells him "Susan's mother" will be watching Miles while they go out.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird shows Snuffy a picture he's drawn of himself as a baby. Snuffy doesn't remember ever seeing Big Bird look like that, when he's reminded that he was born after Big Bird.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gina explains to Big Bird that the party set up out in the yard is for Maria's baby shower, and invites him and Mr. Snuffleupagus to come. Though Gina says it's okay that he doesn't have to bring something, he insists on getting Maria a gift... but what will it be?

episodes.summaryEn: Telly assumes Luis is going on a trip when he carries a suitcase into the Fix-It Shop. Luis informs him that Maria's baby is due soon and he's preparing for their eventual trip to the hospital by having a suitcase ready at work and in their apartment.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Martin P. Robinson voices Sonny Friendly's game show announcer. episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird is the ringmaster of the (makeshift) Sesame Street Circus! With Chip and Dip providing the music, Big Bird presents the first act - Anna, who tames three wild tricycles (pedaled by Gordon, Miles, and another child).

episodes.summaryEn: Luis has a book all about pregnancy and correctly finds the things Maria is currently experiencing are normal in her current stages. She jokingly wonders if the book has anything about saying "hello" to the viewer and getting a kiss from Luis.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gina plays and sings "Follow the Leader" with the kids.

episodes.summaryEn: Today Luis and Maria are decorating the room where their soon-to-be-born baby will be living, with the help of Hiroshi and Big Bird. While the grown-ups leave, Big Bird witnesses the rocking horse actually moving on its own!

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: David welcomes the viewer, and recalls that he heard on the weather report that it was going to rain. He notices Ruby standing outside in the yard, and suggests that she come into Hooper's to get away from the rain.

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Scenes 4, 5, and 6 of this episode have been used in some of the international co-productions of Sesame Street, such as Sesamstrasse.

episodes.summaryEn: Maria and Luis are looking forward to the arrival of their baby. They fantasize about what it will be like to raise their child as they sing "My Baby" - Maria thinks it will be a boy, while Luis thinks it will be a girl.

episodes.summaryEn: Luis leaves the Fix-It Shop for the day and makes sure things are okay with Maria. She finds a note he left in the toaster she's checking on, saying that Uncle Wally will be helping take care of her today, which she finds unnecessary.

altLabels.labelEn: Maria's pregnancy — Uncle Wally takes care of Maria
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Martin P. Robinson voices Jack, Sonny's game show announcer.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird tells the viewer that last night, Maria had gone into labor and is now at the hospital with Luis to have their new baby! He wants to know if it has arrived yet, and if it's a boy or a girl.

episodes.noteEn: Season 20 finale; Gabi is born, as identified by the episode plot label. Muppet Wiki note: This was Northern Calloway's final episode as David. After the episode aired, Calloway left the show due to medical reasons with the explanation that David moved away to live with his grandmother and ownership of Hooper's Store was turned over to Mr. Handford. Calloway died the following year. Muppet Wiki note: Though the book is missing its dust jacket, Gordon is reading Under the Sunday Tree by Eloise Greenfield to Miles during scene 2. He had previously read from it in Episode 2610. Muppet Wiki note: Scene 6 and a portion of scene 7 appear on 40 Years of Sunny Days. Muppet Wiki note: Baby Gabriela is played in this episode by an infant boy: Dick Maitland's son Bryan Maitland. Dick's wife portrays the nurse who brings the baby into the hospital room.

episodes.summaryEn: Everyone is out on Sesame Street having fun and saying hi to each other, when Big Bird notices a rabbit he doesn't know. Bob suggests they go say hi to him.

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: The four songs in this episode that spoof those from The Music Man were principally written by Paul Jacobs (music) and Sarah Durkee (lyrics), with Norman Stiles co-writing the lyrics for both "Trouble" and "Seventeen Ice Cream Cones." Jeff Moss contributed "Hello, My Name Is." Muppet Wiki note: A clip of this episode would be seen in the episode "Camping Out" from Pee-wee's Playhouse.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird greets the viewer and notes that Barkley seems happy today, especially when playing fetch with his new toy ball. However, he misses his jump and hurts one of his legs, which makes him sad.

episodes.summaryEn: At the Fix-It Shop, Maria works on a fan while Prairie Dawn uses the shop's computer to write a new pageant. Prairie finds it hard to work when Maria puts on some loud, Spanish music.

episodes.summaryEn: Hoots the Owl greets the viewer as night falls on Sesame Street and tells them they'll be staying up late to see what nighttime is like on the block. He says goodnight to Big Bird and Bob, who will be a guest later on his talk show.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: This episode was later repeated in season 23 as Episode 2897, omitting Oscar's musical number (as the opening refers to the infant Gabriela) and a scene during Bob's guest appearance. Muppet Wiki note: Scenes 2 and 5 would later become used as inserts for future episodes, with the "People in Your Neighborhood" piece omitting parts of the intro and close. Muppet Wiki note: Hoots' call-in viewers from scene 6 are performed by Martin P. Robinson (Owlfred), Camille Bonora (Owlissa), and Jim Martin (Owlexander). Robinson also performs Carlo, the offscreen announcer for Hoots' show. Muppet Wiki note: In the original script for the episode, Chip and Dip (featured as a part of Hoots' band) were going to participate in "The People in Your Neighborhood" with a verse about the night life of alley cats. Bob's role on Hoots' show was also originally written for Linda, with Uncle Wally present to translate.

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon welcomes the viewer when Elmo enters running around chanting, "Elmo got a letter! Elmo got a letter!" He asks Gordon to read it to him, and it turns out to be from David, who has left Sesame Street and moved to the country to help his grandmother on her farm.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird welcomes the viewer and notices Susan and Luis looking at pictures of themselves from their childhood. They sing about how much they remember about being children ("When I Was Little"), and explain to Big Bird that everyone starts out as a child and grows into an adult over many years.

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon and Miles find Telly trying to read two books at once, claiming he doesn't want to hurt the feelings of the other if he reads them separately. Gordon points out the books aren't alive and won't feel hurt, relieving Telly, who asks if Gordon can read to them.

episodes.summaryEn: Maria is wrapping a package to send to her mother when Sonny Friendly appears with another one of his traveling game shows - this time it's "The Rhyming Game." episodes.summaryEn: A weary Slimey returns to Oscar's trash can from the park. Oscar tells Gordon and Telly that it's a six-hour round trip, leaving him no time to play with his mudball team (the Brown Sox) before he has to return for lunch.

The piano underscore used at Miss Matty's was also played by Buster the Horse in another saloon scene, when Forgetful Jones tries to figure out the name of a song.

episodes.summaryEn: Elmo is going mountain climbing and needs Oscar’s help in making sure he has brought everything he will need. On the condition that Elmo will begin his climb as soon as they're finished, Oscar helps him check that he has the appropriate clothes, food, and supplies.

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: This episode marks the debut of Telly's obsession with triangles, a trait that would stay with the character to this day. Scene 5 was also used on Sesamstrasse. Muppet Wiki note: Prior to this episode, Luis discussed the story of Telly and the triangles in scene 5 of Episode 2747, as both episodes were taped the same day. Muppet Wiki note: Telly's build-it-yourself triangle would later be seen hanging on the wall in the Monster Day Care in Episode 3890.

episodes.summaryEn: Holding a suitcase, Telly bangs on Oscar's trash can to let Oscar know that he will be away visiting his cousin for... one whole day! Telly fears that Oscar will miss him in his absence, so he has prepared all kinds of love messages to remind him - though Oscar is more disgusted than sad.

episodes.summaryEn: Telly hosts "The Wide World of Sesame Street," a program which shows a day in the life of someone on Sesame Street. Today's protagonist is Gordon, whom Telly locates by calling him from a phone booth that his crew has placed in the yard so he can talk to and watch Gordon at the same time.

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: The volcano film's leader comes from another Sesame Street film, and reads "CARPENTRY" when reversed.

Muppet Wiki note: This is one of the rare Sesame Street episodes that aired only once. In its place for the summer rerun, a different episode from season 20 was selected and edited with a different group of inserts, including previously unaired segments. For the summer airing, see Episode 2787/rerun.

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: One of the animals in the stampede is a bear puppet that would go on to become Baby Bear, who would make his debut later in season 22.

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: The Dawgs' family picture would later be used as decoration in Sing, Hoot & Howl with the Sesame Street Animals and the waiting room of Gina's veterinary office.

episodes.summaryEn: Mike looks after Hooper's Store while Gina runs some errands. Preston Rabbit appears and insists on giving Mike a present in honor of his generosity.

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: In addition to writing the episode's script, Jeff Moss wrote or co-wrote all of the songs used during Telly's search.

episodes.summaryEn: Uncle Wally comes across Telly in the yard, who's practicing standing still for all the situations that require it (taking photos, combing his fur, etc.). Telly demonstrates some of the poses he's worked on, and Wally claims he used to be a maverick at standing still in his youth.

Muppet Wiki note: Elmo's racing hat and goggles would be recycled whenever Elmo wore a superhero costume, such as Episode 3043.

She replies that everyone on Sesame Street is a variety of colors and sings about how they all make a "Fabulous Rainbow." The group becomes inspired and decides to draw a rainbow with all of their friends.

episodes.summaryEn: Elmo and Zelda have been given some empty oatmeal boxes to play with from Gina. Luis helps them use the boxes as a secret telephone device.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Susan finds Telly about to go on a morning run with Gordon, but he's gathered several items to take with him - an umbrella in case of rain, an extra pair of shoes in case he slips in a puddle and loses them in a tree, a stool to sit on when putting on the extra shoes, and a flashing light to warn others not to bump into the stool. She convinces Telly he won't be able to carry it all, setting off a chain reaction where he disposes of the extra items.

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: In addition to performing Telly, Martin P. Robinson voices the announcer for "Ask Oscar."

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Jim Martin performs Irvine in this episode.

episodes.summaryEn: Susan overhears a delivery person (Martin P. Robinson), carrying a large, heavy stack of packages, thanking Oscar for his help. He explains to Susan that the delivery person wanted directions to Big Bird's nest.

episodes.summaryEn: Gina, Uncle Wally, Snuffy, and the kids hang out in the yard when they're visited by Sonny Friendly with another one of his traveling game shows. Between scenes three and four, Telly visits the park to find Polly. He listens for her voice and hears it coming from Biff's radio (using a recording of "Counting One to Five"). He finally encounters Polly taking her dogs for a walk before she promises to reveal her favorite number after a commercial break.

episodes.summaryEn: Elmo welcomes the viewer, and Mike begins to read Elmo a copy of his favorite story - "Jack and the Beanstalk." Elmo loves it so much he tells more of the story than Mike does, barely giving Mike a word in. After Mike finishes "reading," Elmo runs off to find some magic beans so he can climb a beanstalk and get some "gooolllden eggs" (as Elmo puts it).

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: This episode was later repeated in Season 24 as Episode 3046. Muppet Wiki note: The original script contained an additional original song to be sung by the string beans.

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon meets Noel Cowherd, who is visiting an old friend on Sesame Street. He catches up with his old pal, Forgetful Jones (who doesn't remember who Noel is).

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: This episode was later repeated in Season 24 as Episode 3050. Muppet Wiki note: Additional performers include Martin P. Robinson (as Buster and a Pumpkin AM customer), Rick Lyon (as Fat Blue bartender), Pam Arciero (as Green cowgirl), and David Rudman (as a cow).

episodes.summaryEn: As the sun shines, Big Bird plays with his shadow along the construction door wall. He wants to introduce it to Gordon, but Gordon points out that because of a cloud covering the sun now, his shadow is gone.

episodes.summaryEn: Snuffy wants to recycle his soda can, but points out to Bob that Gordon and Susan's bin doesn't have enough room. Although the bin has plenty of room and there are already some cans inside it, it's too small to accommodate the Snuffleupagus-sized empty can of Snuffle Up.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: The Two-Headed Monster gives Luis his Learn Spanish book and wants to learn a few words. Luis doesn't have the time and picks out a quick, easy word for now - "hola." The monster has trouble saying it until Luis gets each head to say a syllable and blend them together.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Unlike most episodes, the theme song fades to black before the first scene rather than a cross dissolve. The first scene also doesn't have any opening theme music.

episodes.summaryEn: Telly excitedly rushes over to Oscar's trash can with a football helmet, tennis racket, beach ball, and butterfly net. He rushes out and back to get a tuba Oscar now says he'll need.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: At five o'clock in the morning, Oscar practices his yelling for an upcoming Grouch Yelling Contest, where he could win a free trip to Club Mud. Naturally, everyone on the block gets woken up and yells back at Oscar, who suggests they join the competition too.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: This episode was later repeated in Season 24 as Episode 3030. Muppet Wiki note: The "Map Song" sequence would be used as a stand-alone segment in later episodes, with a new introduction that doesn't reference Oscar's voice problem. Muppet Wiki note: The audience for the yelling contest is performed by Jim Martin, Camille Bonora, Carmen Osbahr, and Kathryn Mullen.

episodes.summaryEn: The Count asks Susan if he can accompany her on her errands today. She soon realizes he'll be counting every step she takes and tells him she'll be driven crazy.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Elmo greets the viewer as he waits for Savion's dance class to begin. He's fully prepared, already wearing his tap shoes, when Savion and Jelani happen by.

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: This episode was later re-broadcast in Season 24 as Episode 3028. Muppet Wiki note: In addition to performing Snuffy, Martin P. Robinson voices the announcer who introduces Elmo's imaginary tap dance number.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird wishes Luis, Mr. Handford, Mike, the kids, a couple of Honkers, Gordon, Lillian, and Barkley a good morning. He sings "Good Morning, Mr. Sun" afterward.

Before Birdland opens, Hoots the Owl explains that tonight is "Open Stage Night," where anyone can get their chance to perform on the Birdland stage. A man named Forest Wimbeldon (Branford Marsalis) enters looking for Hoots, wishing to play jazz tonight.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.titleEn: Big Bird's Birthday or Let Me Eat Cake
episodes.summaryEn: Snuffy wanders into Big Bird's nest area in the morning to make sure he's the first to wish Big Bird "Happy Birthday." The two head out down the street (as the opening credits roll), where all of Big Bird's friends wish him a "Happy Birthday" as well.

sources.label: Muppet Wiki, Big Bird's Birthday or Let Me Eat Cake

episodes.noteEn: Episode 2835 redirects to this published special. The source explicitly says its March 15, 1991 regular-slot version was numbered 2835 and ran 60 minutes with opening theme and added inserts. The pledge-drive edition has different content. Sponsors are not explicitly enumerated on this page; empty arrays mean unknown. Muppet Wiki note: Bert's sole line of dialogue in the special, exclaiming, "Ernie!" during the skating montage at the beginning of the third scene, is lifted from a 1970 sketch. Muppet Wiki note: The special was taped on September 11-12 (on-location at Central Park), September 21 (scenes 1-2), and December 10, 1990 (remaining scenes).

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon plays some football with Oscar, Bruno, and the Grouchketeers. Oscar naturally throws the ball too far and too deep when it lands into a nearby, vacant lot filled with trash and litter.

altLabels.labelEn: Cleaning the lot, part 1 – Gordon wants city hall to clean a littered lot
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Rick Lyon performs the three clerks at city hall, who happen to all look and sound identical.

episodes.summaryEn: The gang makes it to the lot where they meet its residents, Audrey and Louise, the Pigeon Sisters; Oscar takes an instant liking to them. Louise has a big appetite and continues pecking at the sign, mistaking it for a cracker.

altLabels.labelEn: Cleaning the lot, part 2 – Gordon organizes everyone to clean up the lot
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: The Pigeon Sisters do some morning strutting and cooing, when Gordon shows off the trash bins the city has provided them. The Pigeon Sisters are disappointed he has bins and not buns.

altLabels.labelEn: Cleaning the lot, part 3 – Gordon's plan to turn the lot into a garden
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon confirms with everyone on the plans for a garden in the cleaned up vacant lot. Snuffy, Elmo, and Prairie Dawn volunteer to help plant the vegetable area, marked with a "V" sign.

altLabels.labelEn: Cleaning the lot, part 4 – Planting a garden in the lot
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: In the vacant lot-turned-garden, everyone is gathered as Oscar and Bruno approach. Susan explains that Mayor David Dinkins will be presenting Gordon with a citizen's award for the work he's done turning the lot into a garden.

altLabels.labelEn: Cleaning the lot — NYC Mayor David Dinkins honors Gordon with a good citizens' award
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Elmo is curious about a large "mountain" of newspapers outside Hooper's Store and why people are adding to it. Gordon points out the sign reading, "Today is Newspaper Recycling Day," and explains why paper needs to be recycled.

altLabels.labelEn: Elmo looks for newspapers to recycle
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Monster on the Spot reporter Telly interviews twins Shawnee and Chai about how they are the same and different. He finds that they look the same and both wear their hair in pigtails, but the girls rattle off a seemingly endless list of the ways they're different.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gina gushes to the viewer about the tape of the opera La Bohème she watched late last night. She then attends to Wolfgang the Seal's fish needs in the yard and finds herself falling asleep.

altLabels.labelEn: Elmo wants to go miniature golfing
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird reads a large sign posted in the yard for Elmo and the Birdketeers, advertising a "Peck" (a special get-together for birds to dance) this afternoon at Birdland. He demonstrates to Elmo how birds peck, and Susan can even do it too and plans to go.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Two additional scenes were originally scripted, but later cut. In one scene, Savion gives Big Bird a quick tap lesson to prepare for the Peck. In the other scene, Gordon sings "Old MacDonald Had an Arm" to Big Bird and the Birdketeers. The latter scene, with some character changes, would later be repurposed for Episode 2929.

episodes.summaryEn: Luis greets the viewer when Telly runs past, clad in a red cape and exclaiming "Whoosh!" Today, he's imagining he's "Super Telly," the monster who never worries. He doesn't even worry when Luis questions the fanfare that's following him, but briefly breaks character to question the color of his cape.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria introduces the word "WET." She tries to describe it, but is interrupted by others (Alex, Lisa, Snuffy, and Kaitlyn) who remark how hot the weather is today. Maria writes the word "HOT" on the other side of her card, noting that when it's hot out it feels nice to get "WET." She's then doused with water from above.
Prairie Dawn plays the opening theme on her piano while Savion tap-dances in the yard. He has her play it slow, then fast, then in a fast jazzy style.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird and Jelani welcome the viewer when Elmo comes rushing in. He tells them and the kids about what just happened to him involving some blue monsters and a Wubbaball.

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Additional performers include David Rudman (shaggy blue monster) and Jim Martin (fat blue monster). Muppet Wiki note: The park scene would later be used as a stand-alone Muppet segment on several international co-productions, including Sesamstrasse.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird looks in his mailbox, and to his surprise he finds a square. He goes outside to find out who it belongs to, and finds that Mike and Maria also have squares of their own which they got in the mail.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: A blooper from scene 1 with Big Bird and his mailbox appears in the documentary Street Gang: How We Got to Sesame Street.

episodes.summaryEn: Savion is collecting old shoes for his school, which will be refurbished and donated to those in need. He picks out a small pair of tap shoes, which were his very first pair.

episodes.summaryEn: Natasha's father, Humphrey, has to go to the store and leaves Natasha in Maria’s care at the Fix-It Shop. He warns her that Natasha has just learned to crawl, and will do so all over the place if not in someone’s watchful eye.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: This episode was later repeated in Season 24 as Episode 3049. Muppet Wiki note: In a scene cut from later script drafts, Natasha makes her way to Big Bird's nest, where Big Bird and Alex are watching over the former's three baby cousins (Curly, Moe, and Harpo). Natasha joins the other baby birds, which prompts a round of "One of These Things." Though not present onscreen, Alex is one of the people heard calling for Natasha during the final scene.

episodes.summaryEn: Elmo tells Maria that today, he wants to learn how to be a Grouch for a day. Oscar refuses to help, constantly replying "NO" and waving a sign with the word.

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar is weary of hearing the "Sesame Street Theme" every day and wishes they'd come up with something better. Telly happens to have a composition ready and sings a song all about saying "Hi." He sings it again, only replacing "Hi" with "Hola," and Oscar considers it worse than the English version.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Elmo excitedly shows Oscar the globe he was just given by his daddy. He wants to travel the world and has Oscar spin the globe and point to a location he can go.

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: While playing football, Elmo wears the space helmet he'd previously worn in Episode 2689.

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: This episode was later repeated in Season 24 as Episode 3025.

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Among the topics written on Big Bird and Snuffy's puppet show list are "racial relations," "division of labor," and "human diversity."

episodes.summaryEn: Bob watches over Barkley while Linda paints her kitchen. Barkley is feeling very sad, though.
Gina welcomes the viewer when Grundgetta passes by with a wrapped gift, intended as a surprise for Telly. Since it's something he isn't expecting, he wonders what it could be and makes wild guesses.

episodes.summaryEn: Savion plays a rhyming game with the viewer while tap-dancing.

episodes.summaryEn: Elmo claims that he can imagine anything when he wears his hat. While Elmo is thinking of what to imagine next, Mike stops by to pick him up for their bike ride in the park today.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: This episode was later re-aired in Season 24 as Episode 3035.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird interrupts Jelani and Gordon's lesson to explain why he's saying "TOOTHPASTE!" Today's letter is F, and kids use toothpaste to brush their teeth; when their baby teeth fall out (using Gregory and Michael as an example), the tooth fairy collects them - and fairy starts with the letter F!

episodes.summaryEn: Savion gives a lesson to Mike and Alex, who want to know how they can be just as good. Savion begins rapping about the importance of practice.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: This episode was later repeated in Season 24 as Episode 3048.

episodes.summaryEn: As the meeting begins, Telly starts to weep at just the title of the storybook: The Grouches Who Lost All Their Pickles. He knows how much Grouches love to eat pickles, and the thought of them running out makes him and the Grouchketeers sad.

altLabels.labelEn: The story of "The Grouches Who Lost All Their Pickles"
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gina discovers Oscar's discarded "NO" sign left in Hooper's Store from this morning and asks Elmo to bring it to his trash can. Elmo is eager to take on the task.
Maria finds Elmo yelling "Stop!" over and over again. Elmo claims to be practicing his stopping ability and shows Maria what he can do.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Telly shows Uncle Wally his clown costume and claims he'll be a clown one day, only he can't do anything funny. Uncle Wally recalls his time as a young adult working at the circus (feeding the seals) and teaches Telly what he learned from watching the clowns.

altLabels.labelEn: Telly the clown / Baby Bear's broken chair
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Elmo observes Mike talking with rock stars Big Jeffie and Little Chrissy, who will be performing at Mike's high school dance tonight. However, lead singer Little Jerry has caught the chicken pox and can't perform, meaning they'll have to cancel.

altLabels.labelEn: Elmo fills in for Little Jerry
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: David Rudman puppeteers Little Chrissy, and Jim Martin puppeteers Big Jeffie.

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar is disgusted by the bouquet of flowers Mike has gotten for Gina. He claims if he ever gave those to Grundgetta, she'd never speak to him again.

altLabels.labelEn: Grundgetta refuses to talk to Oscar
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon encounters Slimey and the Worm Scouts in the midst of a hike. The worms have a problem when they are unable to get from one crate to another, and Gordon thinks of some possible ways they can do it.

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: This episode was later repeated in Season 24 as Episode 3024.

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon, Telly, Big Bird, and Mr. Handford see the latest newspaper headline in Hooper's Store - "WATER SHORTAGE IN CITY." Mr. Handford turns on the TV to see if there's anything in the news about it. A special weather report plays on television: "Weatherfront: City Dries Up, Day 30." Weatherman Caspar Pfluegy (Kevin Clash in an onscreen cameo) explains and demonstrates how rain and reservoirs work, and what happens when there's not enough rain.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: This episode's plot line is adapted from an earlier episode, Episode 1740. Muppet Wiki note: The weatherman role was originally intended for Willard Scott. Muppet Wiki note: Scene 2 would later be used as a stand-alone Muppet segment on several international co-productions, including Sesamstrasse. Muppet Wiki note: Martin P. Robinson voices the news announcer during scene 1.

episodes.summaryEn: Uncle Wally welcomes the viewer when Telly rushes in to inform him that the Grand High Triangle Lover - president of the Triangle Lovers Club - is coming to Sesame Street today! Telly doesn't know the reason for the visit, but a royal fanfare plays as the GHTL arrives with his assistant Norman, loudly playing his musical triangle.

altLabels.labelEn: The Grand High Triangle Lover visits Telly
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: This episode was later repeated in Season 24 as Episode 3022. Muppet Wiki note: During his acceptance speech, Telly comments that the first triangle he loved was in a mobile hanging above his crib. Years later, in Episode 4009, it's revealed that this was also the first time Telly had seen a triangle.

episodes.summaryEn: Telly, Rameek, and Katie welcome the viewer and demonstrate things one can do with their fingers. They show how they can wiggle, point, and tickle, ending the lecture by using their fingers to tickle Telly.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Bob and Linda watch as Barkley plays with his favorite ball, which is all chewed up given how much Barkley loves it. Bob accidentally tosses it over the doors to Big Bird's nest, where another dog (David Rudman) grabs it and leaves before Barkley gets there.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: "Can you tell me how to get, how to get to..." Telly interrupts the opening sequence: "Birdland! Can you tell me how to get to Birdland?!" Susan, Gordon, Miles, and some kids happen to be going there, and they say he can come with them.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: As they warm up their voices, Placido Flamingo presents the two candidates for the lead role in his new opera, "La Grouchiata" - Grundgetta and world-famous opera singer Wilhelmenia Fernandez. The two must audition first before he can decide who the role should go to.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Additional performers include Carmen Osbahr and Jim Martin (as AM chorus members in the opera).

episodes.summaryEn: The bird, a purple-tufted Fluter-tooter named Floyd, introduces himself to the group. He explains that Fluter-tooters are known for their graceful flying (yet lousy landing) and their happy song, which at the moment he doesn't feel like singing because he's sad.

altLabels.labelEn: Floyd the Fluter-tooter needs a new home
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: This episode was later re-aired in Season 25 as Episode 3175. Muppet Wiki note: David Rudman performs Flo, Flip, and Felix Fluter-tooter. Muppet Wiki note: During scene 2, Gina says that her friend helps endangered species. Big Bird isn't familiar with the term, but had previously been considered one ten years earlier. Muppet Wiki note: Beginning with this episode, certain season premieres would air with a full credit sequence originally shown for Friday episodes only.

episodes.summaryEn: Mr. Handford welcomes the viewer and points out that Grundgetta and her Grouch friends (Jim Martin and David Rudman) are waiting for a Grouch milkshake. All they say he needs is a piece of cardboard and a pen, which he uses to write the word "milk" on the card.

altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird teaches Barkley some tricks
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Maria reads the kids Hickory Dickory Dock: the Continuing Story. After the well-known verse the story goes on, where the mouse (David Rudman) complains that the clock's hands keep poking him in the rear every time it strikes one.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Oscar seeks shelter in the Fix-It Shop from whom he claims are "the happiest people in the world." Herb and Glo, the people Oscar is referring to, introduce themselves; they love to travel the globe and find joy in everything, and Maria and Luis are surprised to see that this includes someone as cantankerous as Oscar. Herb suddenly gets an urge, and Glo explains he likes to sing about the things that make him happy.

altLabels.labelEn: The Happiest People in the World
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird greets the viewer as he prepares to visit his friend Francis' house, which he's never been to before. He has a wagon full of all his toys, not sure of what Francis will have to play with.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Snuffy arrives at Big Bird's nest and offers to help him pack for the trip. Big Bird has made an illustrated list of all the things he thinks he'll need - clean underwear, some film, a toothbrush, and Radar.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: As Maria, Luis, Gabi, Big Bird, and the Count ride via pick-up truck to the Crow ranch with their friends, they sing a new version of the "Sesame Street Theme": "We're a long, long, long, long, long, long way from Sesame Street!" This theme sequence is used for every show for the rest of the week.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird stands in the middle of all the commotion as everyone gets ready for Francis' upcoming ceremony. He notices how much food has been prepared, but mostly gets in the way as the grown-ups carry the food, chairs, and other necessities for outside.

episodes.summaryEn: Gina notices Maria and Luis chatting with Gordon about their trip, and they show off the gifts they received during Francis' ceremony. They hear some loud crashing and a donkey braying.

episodes.summaryEn: To help with today's letter (the letter D), Telly has planned ahead so things wouldn't get too chaotic and asked everyone to bring a D word item. However, everyone has brought a dog instead of different things, and soon the pups gang up and start licking Telly all over.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: Additional performers include Kathryn Mullen (spotted puppy and eggplant), Joey Mazzarino (Anatole), David Rudman (Preposterous and eggplant), and Jim Martin. Muppet Wiki note: This episode marks the first appearance of Rosita and Roxie Marie, who both appear during the "Conga" segment. altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.noteEn: Muppet Wiki note: The original mural on Hooper's was noticeably fading as the series went on. Thus, during season 20, the mural would be painted over brick by brick following each show taping until it became a blank wall. The producers wished to add a new mural and Nancy Sans volunteered to write an episode around it. Muppet Wiki note: In addition to using fast-motion for Speedy's painting process, chroma key is utilized by having a solid color Townsend uses to paint with replaced by whatever finished artwork is needed. The end result makes it appear that a simple brush stroke produces a wide variety of details and color.

episodes.summaryEn: The games begin with the first event - cross-country skiing. Since the worms are so small, they will ski across a map of France, rather than the whole country.

Muppet Wiki note: When the episode was uploaded to the Sesame Street YouTube Channel in 2018, a full credit sequence was added to the end, despite the episode having aired on a Monday.

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird remembers how his dream went and begins to describe it. His dream took place in the Old West, where Mr. Handford runs the local general store, Gina is "Miss Gina" (owner of the Sesame Street Ranch), and Savion is Tapalong Savion, the fastest feet in the West (with Big Bird as "Bird," his sidekick).

Muppet Wiki note: In the last scene, Snuffy says "Say goodbye, Gracie," a reference to George Burns' signature signoff on his radio and television series with Gracie Allen. Muppet Wiki note: The original script differs in several ways compared to the final episode: Muppet Wiki note: Telly Monster was originally intended to be the "Duck for a Day" participant rather than Snuffy. Muppet Wiki note: During the first scene, two penguins chastise the faux-duck for their inability to properly portray the fowl. Muppet Wiki note: The adult duck was named Freddy instead of Duffy. Gracie was also originally named Celia. Muppet Wiki note: Freddy's lesson in walking like a duck is presented as a "duckrobics" class, with aerobic disco music playing throughout the session. Muppet Wiki note: After the voice lesson, Telly excitedly demonstrates to Gina how he's mastered the art of being a duck. Muppet Wiki note: While being followed by Gracie, Telly takes shelter in Hooper's Store. Although Gracie follows him in, she doesn't get the hint yet. Muppet Wiki note: A cut scene involved the language-translation song, "Hello-Quack-Quack." Muppet Wiki note: In the final scene, the secret word is "home," which is uttered by Telly as he (and the others) get impatient waiting for Sonny to return. When he wins, Telly is initially offered the chance to be "Moose for a Month," as some Anything Muppet stagehands bring out a moose head.

episodes.summaryEn: Maria and Luis witness Oscar and Grundgetta about to head off in the Sloppy Jalopy to the Nasty Car Races, the biggest Grouch car race in the world. episodes.summaryEn: Following his song, Elmo greets the viewer and says he plans to ride his tricycle all day. Big Bird encounters him and expresses interest in riding Elmo's tricycle and Elmo agrees to let Big Bird do so, despite the difference in their size.

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon and Maria are laughing at a joke when Oscar and Grundgetta tell them to keep it down. They're reading Grundgetta's favorite Grouch fairy tale, The Tale of Sleeping Grouchy; Grundgetta calls it, "the grouchiest tale ever told."

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Telly stares in awe at the Triangle Triple Crown, which will be worn for three weeks by the "Triangle Lover of the Day" at today's Triangle Lovers Club meeting. episodes.summaryEn: Prairie Dawn hosts a Fairy Tale News special report: Fairy Tale Emergencies - Are You Prepared? She explains that an emergency is something that you have to prepare for because you don't know when it will happen - and fairy tales are full of them.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Telly, Zoe and Rosita are all excited because today they're playing "house" and can't wait to pretend to be one big happy family - or as Rosita puts it in Spanish, a familia feliz. Rosita will be the mommy, Zoe will be the baby, and Telly will be the dog and the daddy (even though he'd rather be the dog).

episodes.summaryEn: At the Fix-It Shop, Abby Cadabby and Elmo watch Maria fix a toaster. ("I love having an audience," Maria says.) An excited Rosita rushes over to show them the letter she received from her abuelita and asks Maria to read it.

episodes.summaryEn: While pretending to be leaping elephants, Zoe and Rosita encounter a mysterious object lying on a crate in the yard. Rosita thinks it looks like a popsicle stick, but Zoe remembers where she's seen it: it's Abby Cadabby's magic wand!

The objective of the game is to find all the letters of the alphabet in the right order and to "beat the cluck" - that is, to do so before Cluck the chicken (Leslie Carrara-Rudolph) tap dances her way to hit a gong.

episodes.summaryEn: Rosita and Zoe are both excited about their play date together. As they start to play hide-and-seek, Abby Cadabby poofs in out of nowhere and interrupts the game.

episodes.summaryEn: Chris welcomes the viewer as he serves Telly his lunch: a grilled-cheese sandwich cut into triangles, Telly's favorite shape. Suddenly, heroic music plays as a swashbuckling hero makes a swinging entrance on a vine.

episodes.summaryEn: While a hungry customer outside Hooper's Store wonders whether to have the soup or the salad, Chris is creating a salad of his own when Abby poofs into view, causing the salad to fly out of his hands and land on the customer's head. "Guess I'm havin' the salad." decides the customer.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Chris welcomes the viewer as he finishes doing his laundry at the Sesame Street laundromat. He says he loves the noises the washing and drying machines make, which turns into a variation of "The Wheels on the Bus" with the other patrons.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Leela welcomes the viewer and shows off the video camera she's using to make a video of her new home, which she wants to show to her parents in India. She aims the camera at the laundromat where she works and has everyone inside wave to her parents (including a Honker and Carmen Osbahr in an onscreen cameo).

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: At dusk, Chris closes Hooper's Store and listens to all the nighttime sounds on Sesame Street. Telly and Baby Bear pass by him with a net and a jar, and tell him that they're trying to catch fireflies.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Chris serves some snacks to Big Bird, Elmo and Rosita in the yard outside Hooper's Store. When Elmo asks for a banana, Chris replies, "You just said the magic word!"

episodes.summaryEn: Telly excitedly tells Baby Bear that today is the Triangle Lovers Club's annual Triangle Toss, a game played with triangles. He displays his lucky triangle vest, which is what he claims helps him win every year.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Today is Baby Bear's birthday, and he's celebrating it with a party in the yard! Telly arrives with his present and Baby Bear goes over the plan: first they'll play some party games, then treat themselves to his Mama Bear's chocolate-porridge cake (with a dollop of meringue on the top).

altLabels.labelEn: Curly Bear chases Baby Bear's cake
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird and Snuffy, dressed in bow ties, welcome the viewer to the "Big Bird and Snuffy Talent Show!"... only to realize that they don't know what a talent show is. altLabels.labelEn: Big Bird and Snuffy Talent Show
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Chris finishes reading The Frog Prince to Abby, who really adores the ending where the princess kisses the frog and turns him back into a prince.

altLabels.labelEn: Abby thinks Oscar is a prince

episodes.summaryEn: Big Bird hangs up a sign for his "Nest Sale" as he welcomes the viewer. He’s selling toys that he doesn’t play with anymore, and says that all the toys in his nest are for sale, while everything out of the nest isn’t - and that especially means his favorite toy Radar, who is sitting on the edge of the nest.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gina meets up with Oscar, who’s trying to start up the Sloppy Jalopy, and Slimey, who eagerly bounces up and down in his booster seat. She learns that Oscar is taking Slimey to get his own pet bug, which Gina finds funny.

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

altLabels.labelEn: Elmo steps in for Super Grover
altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: It's nighttime on Sesame Street, and as Hoots sits on the roof and plays the theme song on his sax, Chris closes up Hooper's Store and welcomes the viewer. altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

episodes.summaryEn: Gordon steps out of Hooper's Store and says hello to everyone as he walks down the street (including Murray in a rare appearance on the street set). Elmo says hi to Gordon too, and comments how much he likes him.

episodes.summaryEn: Chris welcomes the viewer as Telly sits inside Hooper's Store, glued to the TV screen. He's watching his favorite game show, Hurry Up!

altLabels.sourceLabel: Muppet Wiki, descriptive label (not a published title)

Chris serves him a bowl of cream of birdseed soup when Freddy Flapman (Lin-Manuel Miranda), a bird real estate agent, pops up when he hears Big Bird comment on feeling cold and offers his services.
